# SE Dev MES & RivalAI Modding Guide

**Applies to Space Engineers version 1 with Modular Encounters Systems (MES) and RivalAI.**

**Claim classification**:
- **[HARD]** = verified in the local MES C# source or enforced by the SE engine. Violations fail deterministically (crash, silent no-op, profile load failure).
- **[SOFT]** = field-tested on a live server, not pinned to a code path. Re-check after an MES or SE update.

---

## 1. Source of Truth & Reference Library

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **The MES C# source is the sole source of truth.** Online wikis are often outdated. This skill (1,868 tags across 41 profile types, checked against that source) overrides generic MES overviews: never use Godimas101's `se-frameworks/references/mes.md`.

C# ModAPI, decompiled engine code, Torch and PB scripts: [CometWorks skills](https://github.com/CometWorks/skills) (`se-dev-game-code`, `se-dev-server-code`, `se-dev-mod`, `se-dev-torch`); `.mwm` models and TextSurfaceScripts: [Godimas101's se-claude-skill](https://github.com/Godimas101/se-claude-skill) (`se-assets`, `se-tss`; not its `mes.md`).

---

## 2. MES Architecture & Core Mental Models

- **Events vs. Triggers**: MES Events run globally (`EventManager`, no grid needed); RivalAI Triggers run per grid on its Remote Control. **They use different tag names** (`[Spawner:]` vs `[SpawnData:]`, singular vs plural zone lists): Tag-Name Matrix in [`events_and_zones.md`](references/events_and_zones.md) §1.A.
- **ContainerTypes & Loot**: paired list counts **must match 1:1** or MES drops every assignment. → [`manipulation_and_dereliction.md`](references/manipulation_and_dereliction.md) §6

---

## 3. SBC XML Deserialization Quirks

> [!CAUTION]
> **Hard Rules (`audit_sbc.ps1` enforces them)**:
> 1. **One `<SubtypeId>` per `<Id>`**: extras are discarded and the profile fails to load.
> 2. **One `<Id>` per `<Prefab>`**: duplicates register the prefab under the wrong Subtype.
> 3. **`[//Comment]` inside `<Description>`, never `<!-- -->`**: an XML comment there aborts loading the whole mod.
> 4. **UTF-8 only**: UTF-16 or legacy-codepage files fail the deserializer.
> 5. **No empty `.sbc` files**: `Root element is missing` stops the whole world loading.
>
> **[HARD]** XML (SBC, store items) silently keeps the FIRST copy of a repeated value and the LAST of a repeated block (two `<EntityComponents>`: only the last loads); one bad value drops the file. Description tags keep the LAST copy.

Formatting rules and snippet tooling: [`sbc_xml_editing_guide.md`](references/sbc_xml_editing_guide.md).

---

## 4. Boolean Master Gates (Events and RivalAI Actions)

> [!CAUTION]
> **[HARD]** A child tag runs only when its gate is `true`, in `[MES Event Action]` and `[RivalAI Action]` alike: `[ChangeCounters:true]` + `[SetCounters:]`, `[SpawnEncounter:true]` + `[SpawnData:]`/`[Spawner:]`, `[UseChatBroadcast:true]` + `[ChatData:]`, `[ChangeAutopilotProfile:true]` + `[AutopilotProfile:]`. Triggers, chats and spawns need `[UseTrigger:true]`/`[UseChat:true]`/`[UseSpawn:true]` (conditions default to on).

Gate tables: [`events_and_zones.md`](references/events_and_zones.md) §2; RivalAI action tags: [`profiles_and_tags.md`](references/profiles_and_tags.md) §2C.

---

## 5. The Zero-Stripping Bug (`TagParse.cs`)

**[HARD]** Integer-list parsers strip `0` values: `[CustomCountersTargets:0]` becomes an empty list (`Counter Names and Targets List Counts Don't Match`). Use `-1` with `[CounterCompareTypes:LessOrEqual]` / `[Greater]`. Affected tags: [`events_and_zones.md`](references/events_and_zones.md) §3.

---

## 6. Token Matrix & Scope (`IdsReplacer.cs`)

**[HARD]** `{Faction}`, `{SpawnGroupName}`, `{Position}` and custom tokens resolve **only in RivalAI Triggers**; Event chat replaces only `{PlayerName}`/`{GPS}` (exception: an Event `[SpawnEncounter:true]` replaces `{Faction}` in the `[SpawnData:]` spawner's `[SpawnGroups:]`, from `[SpawnFactionTags:]`). Tokens in profile names (`[Actions:]`, `[Triggers:]`) **never resolve**. The separate string-**Tag** broadcast (`[Tags:]` + `[EnableTriggerTags:]`, `[ToggleEventTags:]`, ...) reaches every Trigger or Event with that tag; Trigger and Event tags are separate pools. → [`profiles_and_tags.md`](references/profiles_and_tags.md) §5-6

---

## 7. Verified Engine Pitfalls & Workarounds

Each is **[HARD]** unless marked; detail behind the arrow.

- **Weapons**: turret ranges clamp to 800 m on spawn (`[SetWeaponsToMaxRange:true]`, which can set WeaponCore weapons to 0 m and skips subgrid vanilla turrets, MES #332); WeaponCore fixed guns on "Auto (AI Controlled)" ignore MES, so save them on **Mouse Control** (`wc_shootmode.py`); `[UseAntiSmartWeapons]` sees only WC1 `AntiSmart` flares. → [`third_party_integrations.md`](references/third_party_integrations.md) §1
- **Relations**: after 2.75.02 (`49b3380`, PR #463) MES rates NPC-vs-NPC, fixed-gun line of fire and `IsAttacker*` from the faction-to-faction relation like turrets (unset = Enemies, 500 = Friends); up to 2.75.02 it used the target owner's own reputation (500 = Neutral). Forced targets use `[OverrideTargetData:]` (default Enemy-only). → [`behaviors_and_autopilot.md`](references/behaviors_and_autopilot.md) target profiles, [`third_party_integrations.md`](references/third_party_integrations.md) §1H
- **Stores** sell prefabs from the MES store-items file (quantity 1); `GridsForSale` is only for Keen stations. → [`economy_and_stores.md`](references/economy_and_stores.md)
- **`[Type:WaypointNear]`/`WaypointFar` off a CargoShip stalls every NPC's AI**; use `BehaviorTriggerA` or `Position`. → [`diagnostics_and_troubleshooting.md`](references/diagnostics_and_troubleshooting.md) §4.4
- **Zones** match `[PublicName:]`, never `[Name:]`; use `InsideActiveZone` (`InsideZone` is true for inactive zones). → [`events_and_zones.md`](references/events_and_zones.md) §4
- **Manipulation**: dereliction needs `[UseGridDereliction:true]` + a `[Blocks:]` list, and its percentages `[UseSeparatePercentages:true]`; the weapon randomizer skips definitions without `<Public>true</Public>`. → [`manipulation_and_dereliction.md`](references/manipulation_and_dereliction.md) §2-3
- **A misspelled faction tag** drops the spawn group to 0% (`Could Not Get Valid NPC Faction`). → [`spawning_and_conditions.md`](references/spawning_and_conditions.md) §6
- **Waypoints, commands, timers**: `RelativeRandom` follows the grid (use `EntityRandom`); random waypoints ignore water; replies beat `EnableTriggers`; `CommandFromParent` matches only the real parent from 2.75.00; cooldowns re-roll and persist. → [`behaviors_and_autopilot.md`](references/behaviors_and_autopilot.md) §5, §7, §8
- **Weak gyro turning (rovers included)**: Keen's gyro ramp cuts the push to ~1/8 for a request far from the current rate and MES rewrites it every 0.25 s, so more gyros or multipliers barely help. Put `[UseAircraftFlightModel:true]` + `[MaxRotationStep:0.5]` + `[LimitRotationSpeed:false]` on any gyro-steered NPC and set `MaxRotationMagnitude` to a rate it can stop from. → [`behaviors_and_autopilot.md`](references/behaviors_and_autopilot.md) §3G
- **`MaxVelocityAngleForSpeedControl`**: the default 5 overshoots moving waypoints. **180** on MES 2.75.00+ (field-tested); 90 at most before. → [`aircraft_behaviors_and_tuning.md`](references/aircraft_behaviors_and_tuning.md) §1
- **Target triggers** (2.75.02+): `TargetFar` + `[AllowTargetFarWithoutTarget:true]` fires once the target is gone, and every `LostTarget` trigger sees the edge; on older builds use a `NoTarget` timer. → [`aircraft_behaviors_and_tuning.md`](references/aircraft_behaviors_and_tuning.md) §2
- **Escorts**: up to 2.75.01 a slot is never freed while the escort lives (2.75.02+: dead escorts are cleaned up, `[LeaveEscortSlot:true]` frees one); a refused request gets no reply; Escort Retreat is one-way. → [`behaviors_and_autopilot.md`](references/behaviors_and_autopilot.md) §3D
- **Dialogue banks**: a bank's chat profile is ONE object shared by every grid on it (grids set up at the same moment can get their own copy), chosen per behavior, never per `{Faction}`. → [`dialogue_and_chat.md`](references/dialogue_and_chat.md)
- **Despawn**: `[Type:DespawnMES]` needs `[DespawnTypeFromSpawner:Any]`; up to 2.75.02 ships of 12+ grids only partly despawn (MES #412). → [`behaviors_and_autopilot.md`](references/behaviors_and_autopilot.md) §9, [`diagnostics_and_troubleshooting.md`](references/diagnostics_and_troubleshooting.md) §4.17
- **Bots** (MES `master` after 2.75.03): Keen's 120 s sweep deletes every bot more than 400 m from a player, MES crews included; `[SpawnBlocks:]` needs `MyObjectBuilder_` IDs; `[CheckBotsRemaining:]` counts 0 without `[CheckBotTags:]`; `[UseAiEnabled:]` now defaults to `false`. → [`bots_and_crews.md`](references/bots_and_crews.md) §2-§5
- **Contracts**: `[ContractBlocks:]`/`[ContractBlockProfiles:]` pair by index; template event instances are never removed automatically. → [`events_and_zones.md`](references/events_and_zones.md) §5D-F
- **Silently ignored**: a spawn group without the `[Modular Encounters SpawnGroup]` header; `[RivalAI Target]` without `[UseCustomTargeting:true]`; inline spawn conditions next to `[SpawnConditionsProfiles:]` (and the reverse for statics: a Description with `[StaticEncounter:true]` hides the referenced profile); `[Type:Damage]` without `[DamageTypes:Any]`; `[Triggers:A,B]` (one name per tag); all but one copy of a repeated single-value tag. `[Type:HealthPercentage]` fires at or *above* the threshold. → [`spawning_and_conditions.md`](references/spawning_and_conditions.md) §2, [`behaviors_and_autopilot.md`](references/behaviors_and_autopilot.md) §4
- **[SOFT]** Force-despawn disabled aircraft to avoid falling-airframe Havok loops. → [`diagnostics_and_troubleshooting.md`](references/diagnostics_and_troubleshooting.md) §5

---

## 8. Tooling & Diagnostics

### A. Skill Scripts
The scripts live in the skill, never in the mod: run them from the skill root as `uv run scripts/<name>.py` or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/<name>.ps1` (audits take `-Path <mod Data dir>`); a mod project may have a `run-mes-audit.ps1 -Audit sbc|tags|refs|prefabs|unknown|wc` shim.

**Before MES work, run `check_mes_sync.py`**: it compares the tag cache with the installed MES source (`%AppData%\SpaceEngineers\Mods\Modular-Encounters-Systems`) and lists newer MES commits. On drift, `Update-MesSkill.ps1` rebuilds the cache and re-runs the audits.

| Tool | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- |
| `query_mes_tags.py` | Tag, data type and master-gate lookup (`--tag Zone`) |
| `audit_unknown_tags.py` | Tags, headers and trigger types MES does not parse; single-value tags written twice |
| `audit_sbc.ps1` | Deserializer hazards (§3), MES store-items XML |
| `audit_mes_tags.ps1` | Master gates, zero-stripping, factions, dead triggers |
| `audit_mes_references.ps1` | Cross-file profile references, RivalAI remote setup (WARN only; vanilla remotes stay legal) (`-WarnOrphans -SkipPrefabs`) |
| `audit_prefabs.ps1` | Prefab SubtypeId vs file name, stale `.sbcB5` (`-CleanStaleB5`) |
| `audit_prefab_thrust.py` | Thruster directions per NPC prefab vs its behavior (`--path <Data>/Prefabs`) |
| `test_tag_recipes.py` | Builds every recipe and runs the audits on it; run after editing `tag_recipes.md` |
| `wc_shootmode.py` | WeaponCore shoot mode (`list`/`classify`/`audit`, set Mouse Control); `neutrals` override |
| `save_relations.py` | Faction and identity reputations in a save's `Sandbox.sbc` (turret vs MES relations) |
| `Format-MesSbc.ps1`, `Add-MesProfileSnippet.ps1` | Formatting and `EntityComponent` injection that protect `<Description>` |
| `New-MesProfile.ps1` | Scaffolds (`-Pattern -ModPrefix -Name -Faction`): `DefendedWreck`, `ConvoyLeaderEscort`, `DynamicZoneLadder`, `StoreGrid`, `DynamicStateNpc`, `PlanetaryInstallation`, `CombatDrone`, `ReinforcementNetwork`, `BossEncounter` |

### B. In-Game Testing & Troubleshooting
**Write every test procedure per [`testing_and_debugging.md`](references/testing_and_debugging.md)**: spawn the NPC with `/MES.Spawn.<Type>.<SpawnGroup>` (its conditions need that spawn type; never paste a blueprint), check visually first (`/MES.IGGB`, `/MES.Debug.DrawPaths`, `/MES.Debug.ShowAllZones`), then `[DebugMessage:]`, then logs (`/MES.BehaviorDebug.Trigger.true`, copied with `/MES.IGLBD.Trigger`; the type is required), and only last debug lines in the local MES copy. Every step and check must be something a player can do and see. `[DebugMessage:]` and the event debug tags are development-only. Commands and log signatures: [`diagnostics_and_troubleshooting.md`](references/diagnostics_and_troubleshooting.md) §2, §4.

# se-dev-mes: Space Engineers MES & RivalAI Developer Skill & Tooling Suite [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT) [![Space Engineers](https://img.shields.io/badge/Space%20Engineers-v1-blue.svg)](https://www.spaceengineersgame.com/) [![Modular Encounters Systems](https://img.shields.io/badge/MES-v2.x-orange.svg)](https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1521905890) A comprehensive, production-grade developer skill, reference library, and automated diagnostics suite for modding **Modular Encounters Systems (MES)** and **RivalAI** in Space Engineers. Equips AI coding assistants (Antigravity, Claude Code, Cursor, Cline) and encounter modders with source-verified engine constraints, syntax rules, pitfall detection, safe XML tooling, and automated scaffolding. [![se-dev-mes Architecture & Toolkit](docs/se-dev-mes-diagram-only.png)](docs/se-dev-mes-diagram-only.png) --- ## Background & Development This skill was created by **Mike Dude**, born out of years of real-world server operation, encounter design, and combat balancing on the **GV: Deserts of Kharak (GVK)** rover-PvPvE server. To eliminate the guesswork and silent failures that plague Space Engineers modding, it was developed in close pair-programming collaboration with **Google DeepMind's Gemini (Antigravity)**. Every tag, master gate, parsing behavior, and execution pathway was systematically audited and cross-referenced directly against the local **Modular Encounters Systems (MES)** and **RivalAI** C# source code. --- ## What `se-dev-mes` Gives You 1. **1,868 C# Verified Tags (Not Guesswork)**: - Full tag database across all 41 MES & RivalAI profile schemas, parsed line-by-line from source code. - Every rule is classified as **`[HARD]`** (code-verified against Keen/MES binaries) or **`[SOFT]`** (field-tested operational heuristic) so you know exactly how much to trust it. 2. **Safe XML Tooling (Eliminating `MOD_CRITICAL_ERROR`)**: - Standard XML comments (``) inside `` blocks crash Keen's deserializer (`ReadElementString()`), causing the game to silently drop the entire mod. - `Format-MesSbc.ps1` protects descriptions and converts comments to RivalAI `[//]` syntax automatically. 3. **Automated Auditing for Silent Engine Traps**: - `run-mes-audit.ps1` catches bugs MES never logs: missing boolean master gates (`[SpawnEncounter:true]`), zero-stripping bugs (`[CustomCountersTargets:0]`), and unchecked `WaypointNear` crashes that freeze the AI loop of **every NPC on the server**. 4. **9 Production Scaffolding Archetypes**: - `New-MesProfile.ps1` instantly scaffolds ready-to-run boilerplate: defended wrecks, convoys with escorts, boss encounters, combat drones, store grids, and dynamic zone ladders. 5. **Automated Staleness & Version Drift Detection**: - `check_mes_sync.py` compares the skill's offline tag cache against your local MES install, alerting you immediately if upstream updates add or modify tags. 6. **Empirical Reliability (+60.0% Net Advantage)**: - # Versioning & Release Policy for se-dev-mes

This project follows **Semantic Versioning 2.0.0** (`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`). 

To ensure consistency across human developers and AI coding agents, all future releases and tag updates must adhere to the rules outlined in this document.

---

## 1. Version Number Criteria

### A. PATCH (`1.0.0` ➔ `1.0.1`) — Bug Fixes & Documentation Polish
Bump the **Patch** number for backward-compatible bug fixes, linter corrections, and documentation polish.

**Qualifying changes:**
- Bug fixes or false-positive corrections in PowerShell scripts (`scripts/audit_sbc.ps1`, `scripts/audit_mes_tags.ps1`, `scripts/New-MesProfile.ps1`).
- Adding newly discovered error signatures or engine bugs to `references/diagnostics_and_troubleshooting.md`.
- Correcting typos, broken markdown links, or formatting glitches across `references/` and `README.md`.
- Minor clarifications or updates to existing reference guides without adding new tools or profiles.

---

### B. MINOR (`1.0.0` ➔ `1.1.0`) — New Features & Expanded Coverage (Backward-Compatible)
Bump the **Minor** number when adding new capabilities, expanding the MES tag database, or introducing new reference guides without breaking existing workflows or CLI interfaces.

**Qualifying changes:**
- **MES Upstream Updates**: Rebuilding the offline tag database (`scripts/mes_tag_cache.json`) to track newly released MES tags or profiles from upstream MES updates.
- **New Scaffolding Archetypes**: Adding new archetype templates to `scripts/New-MesProfile.ps1` (e.g., `-Archetype CarrierFleet`).
- **New Linter Checks**: Introducing new audit checks to `scripts/audit_mes_tags.ps1` or `scripts/audit_sbc.ps1`.
- **New Reference Guides**: Adding comprehensive guides for additional third-party mods (e.g., `references/water_mod_integration.md`).
- **New Diagnostic Commands or Tools**: Adding new helper utilities or CLI options to the `scripts/` suite.

---

### C. MAJOR (`1.0.0` ➔ `2.0.0`) — Breaking Changes
Bump the **Major** number when changes break existing workflows, CLI command signatures, or repository structure.

**Qualifying changes:**
- **Breaking Script CLI Changes**: Renaming or removing command-line parameters in `New-MesProfile.ps1`, `audit_sbc.ps1`, or `audit_mes_tags.ps1` that break existing automated scripts or user workflows.
- **Repository Restructuring**: Moving or renaming core reference files in `references/` or `scripts/` that external AI agents or git submodules rely upon at fixed paths.
- **Major MES Schema Overhaul**: If Keen Software House or Modular Encounters Systems introduces an incompatible, non-backward-compatible profile format or XML structure requiring complete rewrites of user profiles.

---

## 2. Release & Tagging Checklist

Whenever a release is cut, follow these steps sequentially:

1. **Pre-Flight Validation**:
   Run the 1-step updater to verify that all XML definitions pass deserialization and semantic checks:
   ```powershell
   powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/Update-MesSkill.ps1
   ```
   *Do not proceed if any errors or warnings are flagged.*

2. **Commit Changes**:
   Stage and commit modified files using conventional commit messages:
   ```bash
   git add -A
   git commit -m "fix: resolve sbcB5 cache invalidation in troubleshooting guide"
   # or
   git commit -m "feat: add water mod integration reference guide"
   ```

3. **Tag the Release**:
   Create an annotated Git tag matching the new version:
   ```bash
   git tag -a v1.0.1 -m "v1.0.1 - Bug fixes and troubleshooting guide expansion"
   ```

4. **Push Commit and Tag**:
   ```bash
   git push origin main --tags
   ```

5. **Publish GitHub Release**:
   Use the GitHub CLI (`gh`) to publish the release with structured release notes:
   ```powershell
   & "C:\Program Files\GitHub CLI\gh.exe" release create v1.0.1 `
     --title "v1.0.1 — Troubleshooting Expansion & Diagnostics Fixes" `
     --notes-file "path/to/release_notes.md"
   ```

---

## 3. Golden Rule on Published Tags
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Never force-push or overwrite a published tag** once public users or automated agents have cloned or downloaded it. Doing so desynchronizes local git clones and breaks package references.
> 
> If a bug or omission is discovered immediately after release, publish a **Patch bump (`v1.0.1`)** rather than moving the existing tag.

# Aircraft Attack Runs, Triggers, Weapons & Tuning

Companion to `behaviors_and_autopilot.md` for anything that flies (propeller aircraft and hover fighters). That file already covers the subclass list, the
`FighterPlane` breakaway (section 6B), the thruster-direction requirements (6A) and the `LevelWithGravity` pitch lockout (section 3A and 6D). This file adds what
is not there yet: how the attack-run cycle is tuned, which triggers swap profiles, the gates and ammo rules for fixed guns, **why WeaponCore fixed guns never fire from MES**, and a tuning method.

**Verified against**: MES 2.74.00 and CoreSystems (WeaponCore) 3.0 source, plus in-game testing of forward-thrust propeller aircraft. Hover/omni-thrust statements are read from source and
were **not** flight-tested unless stated. **[HARD]** = read in source (file:line given) or seen in a real log/prefab. **[SOFT]** = inferred or measured in play.

---

## 1. The attack-run cycle (`Strike` / `FighterPlane`) **[HARD]**

States: `WaitingForTarget` -> `ApproachTarget` -> `EngageTarget` -> back to `ApproachTarget` after the breakaway. `FighterPlane` is `Strike` line for line except the breakaway offset keeps the
plane's velocity direction (`FighterPlane.cs:256`); both read their distances from the **autopilot profile** whenever one is attached (`Strike.cs:22-25`), so the behavior-level
`[StrikeBegin...]` / `[FighterPlaneBegin...]` tags do nothing in practice. `Fighter` is the reverse: `[FighterEngageDistancePlanet:]` wins when set above 0 (`Fighter.cs:20`).

1. **Approach.** The autopilot flies to an **offset waypoint** around the target: `OffsetPlanetMinDistFromTarget` / `OffsetPlanetMaxDistFromTarget` away and
   `OffsetPlanetMinTargetAltitude` / `MaxTargetAltitude` above **the target's own position**, not the terrain (`OffsetSpace*` in space). Recalculated every `OffsetRecalculationTime` s (default 30).
   Which side of the target the offset lands on is random unless `OffsetMaxAngleFromTarget` limits it; that tag has caveats (`behaviors_and_autopilot.md` section 3E).
   Terrain floor: if that point would sit less than `MinimumPlanetAltitude` above the surface, MES moves it to `max(offset altitude, the midpoint of MinimumPlanetAltitude and IdealPlanetAltitude)` above the surface (`MathTools.ValueBetween` returns the midpoint, not a random value)
   (`AutoPilotSystem.cs:1597-1617`, MES 5fd61d1; the offset matrix is the target entity's world matrix, `:1531`). So against ground targets the line-up height is set by those two altitudes, and against air targets by the offset.
   The point follows the target: every update re-reads the target's world position (`OffsetWaypointGenerator`, only its translation is used), while the direction stays fixed until the next pick (MES `49b3380`). A point on the far side of a fleeing target moves away at the target's speed, so the plane may never get within `AttackRunDistancePlanet` of it; only `AttackRunOverrideWithDistanceAndTimer` and `OffsetRecalculationTime` end that chase.
2. **Run start.** The run begins when the plane is within `AttackRunDistancePlanet` of the **offset waypoint** (not of the target) **and** the target is farther than
   `AttackRunBreakawayDistance`. With `AttackRunOverrideWithDistanceAndTimer:true` it is also forced when the plane stays within `AttackRunOverrideDistance` of the offset waypoint for
   `AttackRunOverrideTimerTrigger` s (stops a plane circling the offset forever). `AttackRunDistancePlanet` should exceed the turn radius (`speed / rotation rate`) or the plane can orbit the offset without
   getting inside. **[SOFT]**
3. **Run.** The waypoint becomes the target. `AttackRunUseSafePlanetPathing` keeps the terrain climb active; `AttackRunUseCollisionEvasionPlanet` (default false) leaves collision evasion off because the target itself would count as the obstacle.
4. **Run end.** The run ends when the distance to the target is `<= AttackRunBreakawayDistance` (default 450) or on `BehaviorActionA` (table below). Then the next offset is picked. `Strike` raises `BehaviorTriggerB` when a run starts (`Strike.cs:194`) and `BehaviorTriggerA` when it ends (`:257`).
   **`[AttackRunMaxTimeTrigger:]` does nothing.** The engage code checks `Data.AttackRunMaxTimeTrigger > 0` (`Strike.cs:239`, `FighterPlane.cs:239`) but `AutoPilotProfile.cs` has no parser for the tag, so it is always -1 (off).
   **[SOFT] Against an aircraft a run can last forever.** Two planes on runs at each other at the same speed never get inside the breakaway distance, so neither run ends; with `[LimitPitchTurning:true]` they circled and climbed past 7 km (MES d500922).
   **Run time limit from triggers** (**[HARD]** code; **[SOFT]** flown, field result below):
   - A `[Type:BehaviorTriggerB]` trigger sets a boolean and restarts a Timer trigger with `[ResetCooldownTimeOfTriggers:true]` + `[ResetTriggerCooldownNames:]`.
   - The Timer trigger has `[StartsReady:false]` and the limit as its cooldown. Its conditions need the boolean and `[BehaviorModeCheck:true]` + `[CurrentBehaviorMode:EngageTarget]`. Its action sets `[BehaviorSpecificEventA:true]` and clears the boolean.
   - A `[Type:BehaviorTriggerA]` trigger clears the boolean too, as does any action that changes the subclass (a restart abandons the run without `BehaviorTriggerA`).
   - Why the boolean: MES checks every trigger (`ProcessTriggerWatchers`) before it runs any trigger's actions (`ProcessActivatedTriggers`), so without it the Timer can fire in the tick the run starts, before the reset lands. Why `StartsReady:false`: a trigger with `StartsReady:true` skips its cooldown until it first fires (`TriggerProfile.cs:397`), and the reset only moves `LastTriggerTime`.
   **Swapping a profile by altitude** (**[HARD]** code; **[SOFT]** flown, field result below):
   - `[OverwriteAutopilotProfile:true]` only replaces the slot's profile object (`AutoPilotSystem.AssignAutoPilotDataMode`), so a swap in the middle of a run keeps the run going with the new values.
   - To change one setting with height (for example `[LimitPitchTurning:false]` up high), load a copy of the profile from two Timer triggers with `[AltitudeCheck:true]`, a gap between their two heights, and a boolean for which copy is loaded. `MinAltitude`/`MaxAltitude` are above the surface, compared with a strict `>`/`<`, and the check fails off-planet (`ConditionProfile.cs:1204`).
   - MES runs the actions of every fired trigger in the order the triggers were added (`ProcessActivatedTriggers`, trigger-group list order), so when two triggers write one slot in the same tick the later one wins. List the altitude swaps before the triggers that load profiles for other reasons, and have those clear the boolean.
   **[SOFT] Field result, NPC against NPC** (MES d500922; suggested values, tune per server): three changes together kept the dogfight under about 1 km, with varied dives and climbs. They were a 10 s run limit, line-up points 50-200 m below the target, and `LimitPitchTurning` off above 1000 m (back on under 900 m). Short of all three, the fight still climbed:
   - With only the run limit, the endless spiral was gone but the pair slowly drifted up.
   - Line-up points 150-300 m below the target slowed the drift but didn't stop it, and they sometimes flew planes into the ground.
   - A `[MaxAltitude:]` gate on the trigger that starts a break turn did nothing for the climb (see the LimitPitchTurning entry in `behaviors_and_autopilot.md`).
5. **Distances that must agree.**
   - Offset distance = turn-around space. A longer offset gives a longer straight approach to line up, and a shallower dive (`atan(offset altitude / offset distance)`), which matters for targets on the ground.
   - The plane has to stay inside the target's acquisition range: compare the offset distance (plus turn-around overshoot) with the targeting profile's `MaxDistance` / `NonBroadcastVisualRange` and any `TargetFar` trigger distance (section 2).
   - The breakaway distance must leave room to pull out. Pull-out radius is about `speed / rotation rate`; a dive at angle `a` loses about `R * (1 - cos a)` plus gyro spin-up. **[SOFT]**
   - The gun firing window is roughly `MaxStaticWeaponRange - AttackRunBreakawayDistance` (section 3).
   - **Line up before the guns reach.** **[SOFT]** (GVK playtest) Put the offset distance at least 800 m beyond the fixed guns' max target distance, so the plane is lined up and on a straight approach before the target is in range, and widen the target profile's `MaxDistance` / `MaxExistingTargetDistance` and any `TargetNear`/`TargetFar` distances to cover the offset plus the turn-around (about 1 km), or the target is dropped between passes.
   - **Air-to-air: keep line-ups level or slightly low, and the floor low.** **[HARD]** mechanism (`AutoPilotSystem.cs:1610-1628`, MES `49b3380`); **[SOFT]** values (GVK playtest).
     Two NPC aircraft that target each other line up relative to each other's height, so any upward lean compounds: the plane that lines up above pulls its target up after it, and the target's next line-ups start from there. The terrain floor only ever raises a point: against a target flying under `MinimumPlanetAltitude`, every line-up goes to the Minimum/Ideal midpoint, and nothing moves one down. An upward offset (a run lined up hundreds of metres above the target) or a high floor sends a dogfight upward until it ends in space.
     - Keep the target-relative offset altitude small on every aircraft profile. On a profile that fights aircraft, lean it slightly low, for example -100 to +50, so line-ups average a little below the target and cancel the floor's push.
     - Give that profile a low floor and ideal (for example 75-150 m and 200-300 m): their midpoint is where every line-up against a low aircraft goes. Leave room to dive.
     - To fly higher over ground targets, raise the floor only on the attack-run profile, and swap a low, level dogfight profile in against aircraft (section 2).
     - An aircraft with an even offset (-100 to +100) and its own altitude band seldom climbs: the floor lifts its line-ups only into that band. **[SOFT]** (inferred, not seen) Two of them fighting well above their floors can still drift up slowly, since nothing pulls them back down.
   - The offset has to be reachable before it expires: `OffsetRecalculationTime` must exceed the flight time to the offset (`offset distance / speed`, plus the turn after a breakaway), or the plane chases a new offset every cycle and never starts a run. **[SOFT]**

**Speed during a run ([HARD] change in MES 2.75.00).** This only matters with `[SlowDownOnWaypointApproach:true]`; the default is `false`, and then `CalculateStoppingDistance` returns `-1` and nothing below applies. With it on, `CalculateDirectForwardThrust` (the straight forward-thrust path a `FighterPlane` uses; a grid in gravity with a level-with-gravity profile uses the separate hover path instead) cuts forward thrust once `CalculateStoppingDistance(...)` reaches the waypoint distance (`ThrustSystem.cs:210`).
- **Up to MES 2.74.05** it passed `Direction.Forward`, so the estimate summed the **forward** thrusters (`ThrusterProfile.GetEffectiveThrust`), the same ones driven for forward thrust. On an aircraft with only forward propellers that gave a non-zero estimate, thrust was cut inside it and the plane **coasted** (it never braked down to `IdealMinSpeed`, and in a dive gravity added speed). Flight tests on forward-propeller aircraft matched this.
- **From commit `941e8c2` (2.75.00, jayph)** it passes `Direction.Backward`: braking is measured with the reverse thrusters, as `behaviors_and_autopilot.md` section 6A item 2 always described. With no reverse thrusters `accel <= 0` and the estimate is `0`, so thrust is no longer cut by the slow-down; the plane keeps its throttle through a run. Reverse thrusters present: no change.

A forward-only plane in a dive therefore gets a non-zero estimate and can still lose thrust inside it once its speed is at or above `IdealMinSpeed`. In level flight the term is `0`, and in a climb the acceleration is negative, so the estimate is `0` and thrust is held. Expect the largest difference from 2.74.05 in level and climbing approaches, and the smallest in steep gun dives.
- Over-speed braking (`Brake To Desired Speed`) already used the reverse thrusters, so a forward-only plane still cannot brake in either build.

### Autopilot tags that do little or nothing for aircraft **[HARD]**
Checked against MES `bc71965` (upstream master).

| Tag | What the code does |
| :--- | :--- |
| `UseRotationBoostUp`, `RotationBoostUpAmount` | Parsed (`AutoPilotProfile.cs:690-699`) but never read. No effect. |
| `DesiredAngleToTarget` | No parser; always 0. |
| `MinAngleForLeveledDescent`, `MaxAngleForLeveledAscent` | Only in `CalculateHoverThrust` (`ThrustSystem.cs:355-372`); planes on direct forward thrust never use them. |
| `TryToLevelWithTarget` | Only for a static target below ground within 1200 m (`AutoPilotSystem.cs:1115`). |
| `BehaviorActionA` / `B` | `[BehaviorSpecificEventA:true]` sets A; `FighterPlane` and `Strike` end the run on it, and `Hunter` and `Nautical` read it too. `Strike` reads it only during a run (`Strike.cs:252`): set while the plane lines up, it stays set and ends the next run one behavior tick after it starts, so gate the action on `[CurrentBehaviorMode:EngageTarget]`. `BehaviorSpecificEventB` to `H` have no parser (only A is in `ActionReferenceProfile.cs:1211`), so the forced run start (B, `Strike.cs`/`FighterPlane.cs:181`) can't be set from SBC. To give a `Strike` plane a new line-up point, switch the subclass away and back in one trigger (two `[Actions:]`, each `[ChangeBehaviorSubclass:true]`, run in order): a changed subclass restarts in Init, which picks a new offset. **[HARD]** code, not yet flown. |
| `UseCollisionLeadPrediction` | Aims at a collision course (no projectile travel time) and is checked before `UseProjectileLeadPrediction`, so it replaces gun leading (`AutoPilotSystem.cs:1277`). For rams, not guns. |
| `ReverseOffsetDistAltAboveHeight` + `ReverseOffsetHeight` | When the target is more than `ReverseOffsetHeight` above the surface, the offset distance and altitude ranges swap (`AutoPilotSystem.cs:1495-1511`): the line-up point goes offset-distance **above** the target. That is the upward cascade in item 5 above; avoid it for air-to-air. |

Tags that do work and are easy to miss:
- **`[UseAircraftFlightModel:true]` (MES 2.75.00 / PR #390)**: Native atmospheric flight physics rules for gyro-steered aircraft. Enables `MaxAngleFromVelocity` (stops flat sideways sliding/drifting, e.g. `25`), `RollIntoTurnsMultiplier` (banks naturally into turns in gravity, e.g. `0.8`), `MaxBankAngle` (caps bank degrees, e.g. `45`), `ReturnToLevelMultiplier` (auto-levels wings when idle above `ReturnToLevelSpeedCutOff`), and `MaxRotationStep` (suggested `0.5`; lets the gyros push at full strength through Keen's override ramp, and builds turn and bank rate fastest: `behaviors_and_autopilot.md` §3G). See `behaviors_and_autopilot.md` §3F.
- **`[Unused:]` (default true) breaks off an attack run** when a velocity collision is predicted within `CollisionTimeTrigger` (5 s, set in `SetDefaultTags`) (`FighterPlane.cs:252, 329`; `Strike.cs` the same). At 130 m/s that is about 650 m, so a run near terrain or close to the target can end before `AttackRunBreakawayDistance`. The ray stops at any grid except the NPC's own construct, the target included (`CollisionResult.TargetIntersectionCheck`, MES `49b3380`), so a run flown straight at the target ends about 5 s of flight out, and a shorter `AttackRunBreakawayDistance` only applies to passes that aren't on a collision course (most noticeable air-to-air). `[Unused:false]` on the autopilot profile removes the check, at the risk of ramming.
- **`UseForcedRotationDampening` + `ForcedRotationDampeningAmount` (default off, 0.15):** after each gyro update MES cuts the grid's existing spin by the amount, directly through `Physics.SetSpeeds` (`RotationSystem.cs:47-80`). Less overshoot and wobble, slower turns. **[SOFT]** not flight-tested.
- **`RotationSlowdownAngle` (default 70):** above this error the gyro runs at full rate; below it the rate is the error in radians (`RotationSystem.cs:118`). It changes big turns only; small-angle wobble is already in the proportional range.
- **`MaxPlanetPathCheckDistance` (default 1000 m):** how far ahead planetary pathing scans terrain (`AutoPilotSystem.cs:2068`). At 130 m/s that is under 8 s of warning. The approach always uses planetary pathing; the run only with `AttackRunUseSafePlanetPathing:true`.
- **In gravity, a predicted terrain hit does not trigger collision evasion.** Voxel evasion runs only out of gravity; in gravity the only voxel case is the "fall" evade while moving within 15° of straight up (despite its name, it fires on climbs, not falls) (`AutoPilotSystem.cs:1037-1058`). Planetary pathing is what keeps planes off the ground.

### B. WeaponCore fixed guns must not be in "Auto (AI Controlled)" **[HARD]**
The usual reason "MES aims at the target but the WeaponCore guns never fire".

- MES fires a WC fixed gun with `ToggleWeaponFire(block, true, false, id)` (`CoreWeapon.cs:443`), which becomes `RequestShootSync(0, On, Signals.On)` (CoreSystems `ApiBackend.cs:1151`).
- WeaponCore only honors an "On" trigger when the weapon's shoot mode is **not** `AiShoot` (or the signal is `Manual`): `onConfirmed = Trigger == On && (ShootMode != AiShoot || Signal == Manual)` (`SessionUpdate.cs:576`).
- `AiShoot` is the default (`ProtoWeapon.cs:616`), shown as "Auto (AI Controlled)". A fixed gun (`TrackTargets:false`, `TurretAttached:false`) cannot fire itself in that mode, so MES's command is dropped.
- Setting the block to **Mouse Control** fixes it (confirmed in game). `KeyToggle` / `KeyFire` also pass the code check but were not tested. **[SOFT]**
- MES has no code to set the mode and the WC API has no setter, so it has to be **saved in the prefab/blueprint**. WeaponCore stores it as protobuf in the block's `ModStorageComponent` (key `75bbb4f5-4fb9-4230-beef-bb79c9811501`).
  `scripts/wc_shootmode.py` lists and sets it in `.sbc` prefabs, and its `classify` command tells fixed guns from turrets (turrets track and fire themselves; leave them on Auto).
- MES ignores WeaponCore's `AimLeadingPrediction`; it leads targets itself with the autopilot tags `UseProjectileLeadPrediction` (default true) / `UseCollisionLeadPrediction` (`AutoPilotSystem.cs:1275-1290`).

## 4. Hover / omni-thrust fighters **[SOFT]** (source-read, not flight-tested)

- `Fighter` approaches with `RotateToWaypoint | ThrustForward | PlanetaryPathing | WaypointFromTarget`, then **engages with `RotateToWaypoint | Strafe | WaypointFromTarget` and no `ThrustForward`**: it strafes with lateral/up/down thrusters and needs `[AllowStrafing:true]` (`Fighter.cs`). Strafing needs thrusters on every side it strafes toward (`behaviors_and_autopilot.md` §6A).
- For hover craft, `LevelWithGravity` is the intended mode rather than a bug: in gravity with `ThrustForward` it swaps `CalculateDirectForwardThrust` for `CalculateHoverThrust` (`ThrustSystem.cs:70`), which holds altitude against the waypoint
  (`AltitudeTolerance`, `MaxVerticalSpeed`, `HoverUpAngle`). The price is the pitch lockout: the nose stays level, so a leveled hover craft will not nose-dive at targets. `UseSurfaceHoverThrustMode` is a separate pathing switch, not this routine (`behaviors_and_autopilot.md` §3A).
- If a hover fighter must aim its nose up or down at targets, run it without `LevelWithGravity` and give it enough vertical thrust to hold altitude on its own.

## 5. Tuning method (what worked)

1. **Change one thing at a time and test it.** A rewrite that changed six numbers at once made every plane crash and identified nothing. Keep numbered copies of the behavior files and install one at a time.
2. **Watch the flight path, not just the nose.** Fly the NPC variant in steady flight and see how far its path actually follows a turn, and how much speed and height it loses.
   Typical findings: wings add little yaw authority, high nose rates bleed speed, path radius grows with speed squared. **[SOFT]**
3. **Read what MES actually loaded**: `/MES.Info.GetGridBehavior` (`/MES.IGGB`) prints the live autopilot flags, including `LevelWithGravity`.
4. **Find silent no-ops**: run `scripts/audit_unknown_tags.py` over your behavior folder; MES never reads a tag its parser does not know (a typo, or a tag from another profile type).
5. **Judge thrust after manipulation.** The prefab's thruster blocks are not its real thrust when its spawn group's manipulation profile sets `[ConfigureSpecialNpcThrusters:true]` with `[NpcHydroThrustForceMultiply:]` (or the Ion and Atmo versions): that multiplies every thruster of the type on the grid, lift and brakes included. MES also drives forward thrust only at a full override, never a partial one (`ThrustSystem.cs`, `SetZ` with strength 1), so a ship whose forward thrust far outweighs its brakes jumps its speed on every correction. No autopilot tag softens that: use fewer or smaller forward thrusters in the prefab, or the multiplier if lift and brakes can lose the same share. **[HARD]**

## 6. Debugging aircraft (commands are in `diagnostics_and_troubleshooting.md`, section B)

- **Guns silent while the plane lines up**: `/MES.BehaviorDebug.Weapon.true`. Each gun logs `NoAmmo`, `StaticWeaponNotAligned` (the flying is the problem, see 3A) or `ReadyToFire` + "Start Fire" (MES is firing; if nothing comes out, check 3B).
- **Yaws at the target but never pitches**: `/MES.IGGB` and look for `LevelWithGravity`; see section 2 above and 6D.
- **Speed is wrong**: `/MES.IGGB` (AutoPilot section, `Forward Thrust Mode`) shows the thrust branch ("Brake To Desired Speed", "Drifting At Desired Speed", "Thrust Angle Not Matched").
- **A spawn never produces the aircraft**: `/MES.SpawnDebug.SpawnGroup.true` prints why each group was rejected (for example "Could Not Get Valid NPC Faction" when the group's `FactionOverride` does not exist in the world). Without it the log only says "Eligible SpawnGroup Count 0".

## 7. Escort wingmen that hold their slot

Applies to aircraft (and fast hover craft) flying MES's `Escort` behavior on a leader's `[EscortOffsets:]`.

- **Overshoot and turnaround [mechanism HARD, SOFT seen].** An escort flies at its slot, a waypoint fixed to the leader. Once the slot is more than 90° off its nose it gets no forward thrust and turns back toward it (`ThrustSystem.cs`, forward axis). An aircraft that passes its slot by a few metres therefore swings around, falls behind and repeats, and soon loses the formation. Aircraft brake weakly (few reverse thrusters; without `[SlowDownOnWaypointApproach:true]` only over-speed braking applies), which makes the overshoot likely.
- **Speed matching is the fix** (`Escort.cs:107-128`). Within `[EscortSpeedMatchMaxDistance:]` the speed cap scales from the leader's speed, at `[EscortSpeedMatchMinDistance:]`, up to the escort's `IdealMaxSpeed` at the max distance.
  - With a small minimum (10 m) the escort reached the slot faster than the leader and overshot it. Shortening the max distance made it worse.
  - **Field-tested (suggestion):** escort `IdealMaxSpeed` 150 behind a leader at 40-120 m/s, max distance 300 m, `MaxSpeedTolerance` 5, minimum raised in steps to 170 m: the escort reaches the leader's speed long before the slot and holds it.
  - The cost: the escort settles behind its slot, roughly at the minimum distance, so put the slot ahead of where the wing should fly (negative Z, about half the minimum distance).
  - Ground and hover escorts at 35-110 m/s did well with much smaller values: minimum 20 m, max 200 m, `MaxSpeedTolerance` 2.
- **Slot geometry.** `EscortOffsets` are in the leader's frame (+X right, +Y up, +Z behind its Remote Control). A slot swings sideways at the leader's turn rate times its distance from the leader, so closer slots move less in turns. A slot far ahead flips behind the wing when the leader reverses and forces a turnaround.
- **Turn rate and speed.** Give the escort at least the leader's yaw multiplier, or it falls behind in every turn. A leader slower than the escort's `IdealMaxSpeed` (30 m/s of headroom worked) leaves it room to catch up.
- **Disrupting manoeuvres.** A barrel roll or random strafe on the leader throws the escort off its slot. If your triggers start them, block them while the grid has escorts.

# NPC Bots & Crews Reference

Bots on MES encounters: Keen's combat bots (the Warfare 3 bots, SE 1.211) spawned through MES `[MES Bot Spawn]` profiles, Keen's own prefab crews, AiEnabled bots, and the despawn rules that apply to all of them.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Version.** MES support for Keen's bots is on upstream `master` after 2.75.03 (commits from 2026-11-13 on). The Workshop still runs 2.75.03 as of 2026-11-21. On 2.75.03 and older, `[MES Bot Spawn]` spawns AiEnabled bots only (§8) and `[UseAiEnabled:]` defaults to `true`. The tag cache follows the installed MES, so `query_mes_tags.py` and `audit_unknown_tags.py` know the tags in §3-§5 only once the installed MES has the bot code (then run `Update-MesSkill.ps1` and remove the `unreleased` fence markers, which make the audit list those tags as notes). MES line numbers are for `master` at `88ebcf0`; game references are SE 1.211.018 (the 2026-11-20 patch; the bot code is the same as in 1.211.017).

---

## 1. Keen's Bots (Game Side)

**[HARD]** From `IMyNPCSpawnerSessionComponent` and `MyBotAnchorComponent.cs`:

- **Squads**: a bot spawned with a grid joins that grid's squad. Squad members share alerts from damage to the grid, hits on any member and gunshots near the grid, and stay leashed to the grid. A bot spawned without a grid reacts only to hits on itself. One squad per grid; all its bots share the first bot's faction.
- **Behavior** is the bot definition's behavior tree. No ModAPI call (so no MES tag) can send a bot somewhere, pick its target or change its behavior. MES can only spawn bots, seat or unseat them, and delete them.
- **Setup** per bot: a weapons container (a `ContainerTypeDefinition` such as `NPCWeaponsContainerType`), a chat message set (`NpcChatMessageSetDefinition`) and loot (the faction's `BotLootContainerType` unless overridden).
- **Keen's own prefab crews**: the prefab or spawn-group prefab fields `MinNPCCount`/`MaxNPCCount`, `NPCBotSubtypes`, `NPCWeaponsContainerType`, `NPCChatMessageSet`, `NPCSpawnBlocksOverride`, `NPCSpawnPointsOverride` and `NPCHealth` create an "encounter crew" when the spawn group spawns. MES raises the same spawn event for its own spawns (`PrefabSpawner.cs:367`, already in 2.75.03), so these fields crew MES encounters too. MES does not link those bots to the grid: `[RemoveBotsFromGrid:]`, `[EjectBotsFromSeats:]` and `[CheckBotsRemaining:]` never see them, and Keen refuses `[AddBotsToGrid:]` on a grid that already has an encounter crew.

---

## 2. What Removes a Bot

| Cause | When | Source |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Keen's distance sweep | Every 120 s: every bot more than 400 m from a human player who controls a character or a ship. Both values are hard-coded, and there is no exception for ModAPI or MES bots. A bot in a cockpit or seat is deleted with the others; one in a cryo chamber keeps its body but loses its player and AI. | `MyEnvironmentBotSpawningSystem.cs:20,26,112`, `MyPlayerCollection.cs:1756` **[HARD]** |
| Keen's encounter crew (§1) | No player within the encounter despawn distance (600 m default): the crew is despawned. | `MyGridBotPopulator.TickAnchor` **[HARD]** |
| MES grid cleanup | MES despawns the grid: its MES bots are deleted first. | `GridCleanup.cs:128` **[HARD]** |
| `[RemoveBotsFromGrid:true]` | The action runs (§5). | `ActionSystem.cs:2137` **[HARD]** |

> [!CAUTION]
> **[HARD] MES crews despawn by distance.** Keen's `SpawnBot` comment ("never despawns by distance") and the MES bot primer say these bots persist away from players. That holds for the squad, which never despawns anything, but the separate wildlife sweep above still deletes them. Modders have seen it in game with bots spawned through the ModAPI; an MES crew has not been tested in game yet. Keen had told the MES maintainer that these bots do not despawn by distance, and as of 2026-11-21 the maintainer is asking Keen whether a game patch will change it.
> - A crew on an encounter with no player within 400 m can be gone within 2 minutes of spawning.
> - MES then drops the deleted bots from the grid, so `[CheckBotsRemaining:]` counts 0 and a "crew wiped out" trigger fires without a fight. Suggestion: pair that trigger with `[Type:PlayerNear]` or a damage trigger, or add the crew from a `PlayerNear` trigger instead of at spawn.

## 3. Bot Spawn Profile (`[MES Bot Spawn]`)

```xml unreleased
<EntityComponent xsi:type="MyObjectBuilder_InventoryComponentDefinition">
  <Id>
    <TypeId>Inventory</TypeId>
    <SubtypeId>ModPrefix-BotSpawn-Guard</SubtypeId>
  </Id>
  <Description>
    [MES Bot Spawn]
    [BotType:HumanoidBot/CombatAstronaut]
    [BotFactionTag:{Faction}]
    [SpawnBlocks:MyObjectBuilder_CryoChamber/LargeBlockCryoChamber]
    [SpawnSeated:true]
    [Tags:Guards]
  </Description>
</EntityComponent>
```

| Tag | Default | Notes **[HARD]** (`BotSpawnProfile.cs`, `BotSpawner.cs`) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `[UseAiEnabled:]` | `false` (was `true` up to 2.75.03) | `true` takes the AiEnabled path (§8). AiEnabled profiles that relied on the old default need `[UseAiEnabled:true]`. |
| `[BotType:]` | none | Bot definition ID, `HumanoidBot/CombatAstronaut` or with the `MyObjectBuilder_` prefix (both parse). |
| `[BotFactionTag:]` | none | Required: a faction tag that exists in the world, or the action logs `Could not find faction with tag` and spawns nothing. `{Faction}` resolves. Every bot on one grid must share a faction (Keen's squad rule). |
| `[BotDisplayName:]` | random `CharacterName` | |
| `[WeaponsContainerId:]` | the definition's `StartingItem` | `ContainerTypeDefinition` subtype. |
| `[LootContainerId:]` | the faction's loot | `ContainerTypeDefinition` subtype. |
| `[ChatMessageSetId:]` | the definition's set | `NpcChatMessageSetDefinition` subtype. |
| `[SpawnBlocks:]` | none | Block IDs **with the `MyObjectBuilder_` prefix**, e.g. `MyObjectBuilder_Cockpit/LargeBlockCockpitSeat`. MES compares the text with the block's full ID string (`ActionSystem.cs:2074`), so `Cockpit/LargeBlockCockpitSeat` never matches. |
| `[SpawnSeated:]` | `true` | See §4. |
| `[Color:]` | unset | Suit RGB, 0-255: `[Color:{X:200 Y:30 Z:30}]`. |
| `[AssetOverrideSets:]` | faction skin | Skin set names from `SkinSetEnum` (`Soldier`, `Hazmat`, `Scavenger`, ...). One name per tag line; repeat the tag for more, and MES picks one at random. A comma list in one tag parses as a combined enum value and gives the wrong skin or none. `FactionDefault` adds nothing. |
| `[Tags:]` | none | Labels for the §5 filters, merged with the action's `[BotTags:]`. |

## 4. Spawning a Crew (`[AddBotsToGrid:true]`)

A RivalAI Action only. Event Actions cannot spawn bots (there is no grid to tie the squad to), and spawn-group bots are broken on `master` (§7).

```
[AddBotsToGrid:true]
[BotSpawnProfileNames:ModPrefix-BotSpawn-Guard]
[BotCount:3]
[BotTags:Guards]
```

**[HARD]** (`ActionSystem.cs:2047`, `BotSpawner.cs:210-340`):
- **One profile per run**: MES picks one name from `[BotSpawnProfileNames:]` and spawns all `[BotCount:]` bots from it.
- **Placement**: blocks on the grid matching the profile's `[SpawnBlocks:]`, or the action's `[BotSpawnBlockOverrides:]` in their place (`[SpawnBlockOverrides:]`, as the MES bot primer writes it, is not parsed). With no matching block, `[BotSpawnPointOverrides:{X:0 Y:1 Z:-2}]` gives positions relative to the Remote Control (comma list or repeated tags). With neither, nothing spawns.
- **`[SpawnSeated:true]` (default)**: only working, unoccupied seats count (cockpits, seats, cryo chambers). Other spawn blocks are skipped, so once the seats are full the remaining bots do not spawn (`No valid SpawnBlocks on grid` in the spawn log). Match `[BotCount:]` to the seats. Bots are seated one tick after they spawn. There is no standing fallback by design: a seat fills its block's space, so it has no safe spot for a standing bot (MES maintainer, 2026-11-21).
- **`[SpawnSeated:false]`**: seats are skipped; each bot appears at the center of a non-seat spawn block, facing the Remote Control's backward direction, with no gravity correction.
- **Keen's refusals** go to the game log as `SpawnBot: '<type>' not spawned; ...`: the grid already has an encounter crew, the squad has living bots of another faction, the bot limit is reached, or the bot type or faction is unknown.
- `[OnlySpawnBotsInPressurizedRooms:]` applies to AiEnabled bots only.

---

## 5. Managing Crews

**[HARD]** (`ActionSystem.cs`, `ConditionProfile.cs`, `NpcData.cs:1209`):
- `[RemoveBotsFromGrid:true]` deletes the grid's MES bots; `[EjectBotsFromSeats:true]` makes the seated ones stand up. With `[BotTags:]`, only bots carrying one of those tags. The same `[BotTags:]` also labels bots that `[AddBotsToGrid:]` spawns, and in one action the add runs first, so keep adding and removing in separate actions.
- `[CheckBotsRemaining:true]` with `[MaxRemainingBots:]` and/or `[MinRemainingBots:]` (either one satisfied passes) counts the grid's MES bots that still exist. **Always set `[CheckBotTags:]`**: the count includes only bots with one of those tags, so without it the count is always 0. `[MaxRemainingBots:0]` is then true at once, and `[MinRemainingBots:1]` is never true. On master from `2b1e88b` (2026-11-21, not in a Workshop release yet) an empty `[CheckBotTags:]` counts every MES bot on the grid; set the tags anyway until that release.
- `[IsTargetBot:true]` is true when the current target is a bot. On `master`, `[IsTargetGrid:true]` matches only grids and blocks; it used to match anything that was not a player.
- `[Target:]` in `[RivalAI Target]` gains `Bot`, `PlayerAndBot`, `PlayerAndBotAndGrid` and `PlayerAndBotAndBlock`. A bot target candidate is any bot MES tracks within `[MaxDistance:]`, Keen crews and other mods' bots included (`TargetingSystem.cs:525`).
- WeaponCore homing weapons whose threats include Characters accept a bot target (`CoreWeapon.cs`).
- MES bots are saved with the grid's NPC data (`NpcData.cs:447`) and relinked on load.

---

## 6. Debugging

- `/MES.Info.GetActiveBots` copies every bot MES tracks to the clipboard, grouped by grid: name, faction, profile, tags, alive. Bots MES did not spawn (Keen crews, other mods) are listed under "Tracked Non-MES Bots".
- `/MES.Info.GetGridBehavior` and `/MES.Info.GetGridData` list the grid's MES bots under `Bots:`.
- Spawn errors go to the spawn log (`/MES.SpawnDebug.Spawning.true`, copied with `/MES.IGLSD.Spawning`). Action errors (unknown profile, missing faction, no spawn blocks) go to `/MES.BehaviorDebug.Action.true` (`/MES.IGLBD.Action`). Keen's refusals are only in the game log.
- To test the distance sweep, spawn the crew, check `/MES.Info.GetActiveBots`, move more than 400 m away for over 2 minutes, come back and check again. The sweep measures from the character or ship you control, so moving only the spectator camera does not count.

## 7. Known Issues (`master` at `88ebcf0`, re-checked at `6d12572`)

- **Spawn-group bots never spawn.** `[CreatureSpawn:true]` + `[BotProfiles:]` calls `SpawnBotRequest` without `useBuiltIn` (`BotSpawner.cs:92`), so it takes the built-in path whatever `[UseAiEnabled:]` says; only the RivalAI action reads that tag. With no spawn blocks or points it logs `No SpawnBlocks nor SpawnPoints defined` and spawns nothing, AiEnabled profiles included (they worked on 2.75.03). Spawn groups using `[CreatureIds:]` are unaffected.
- **The distance sweep** (§2) deletes MES crews away from players. This is game code, not MES; the MES maintainer is waiting on Keen (2026-11-21).

---

## 8. AiEnabled Bots

With the **AiEnabled** mod loaded, `[UseAiEnabled:true]` profiles spawn AiEnabled bots:

```xml
<Description>
  [MES Bot Spawn]
  [UseAiEnabled:true]
  [BotType:<AiEnabled bot subtype>]
  [BotBehavior:Soldier]
  [BotDisplayName:Security]
  [CanUseSeats:true]
  [CanDamageGrids:false]
</Description>
```

1. **Crew inside a live grid (RivalAI Action)**: `[AddBotsToGrid:true]` + `[BotSpawnProfileNames:]` + `[BotCount:]`, optionally `[OnlySpawnBotsInPressurizedRooms:true]`. AiEnabled picks free spots on the grid itself; `[SpawnBlocks:]` and `[SpawnSeated:]` do not apply.
2. **Standalone ground spawns (Spawn Conditions)**: `[CreatureSpawn:true]` + `[BotProfiles:]` + `[MinCreatureCount:]`/`[MaxCreatureCount:]` + `[MinCreatureDistance:]`/`[MaxCreatureDistance:]`. On 2.75.03 MES picks one listed profile at random per bot (`BotSpawner.cs:65`); broken on `master` (§7).

- AiEnabled bots need navigable corridors or walkable surfaces on the grid.
- Up to 2.75.03 `[UseAiEnabled:]` defaults to `true`; without the AiEnabled mod loaded, only vanilla creature types spawn.
- `[BotBehavior:]` is the AiEnabled role and must be set: the default `Default` is not a role, and AiEnabled refuses the bot. Roles: [`third_party_integrations.md`](third_party_integrations.md) §3.

# In-Game Diagnostics, Logging & Troubleshooting Reference

Diagnostic reference covering in-game admin chat commands, log file auditing, sim-speed optimization, anti-clang physics mitigations, and common error signatures.

---

## 1. Action & Trigger Debugging: [DebugMessage] vs. Chat Profiles

When testing whether triggers fire and actions execute, **never create throwaway `[RivalAI Chat]` profiles**. Doing so introduces redundant `<EntityComponent>` blocks, bloats XML, and clutters cross-referencing. Instead, use native MES debug tags:

### A. RivalAI Action Debugging
- **Tag**: `[DebugMessage:<Your Debug Message Here>]`
- **Location**: Inside `[RivalAI Action]` or `[MES AI Action]`.
- **Mechanism** (`ActionSystem.cs:3047`):
  - Sends a chat message to all players attributed to the grid name.
  - Automatically evaluates dynamic replacement tokens: `{Faction}`, `{Position}`, `{PlayerName}`, etc.
  - Automatically evaluates grid custom counter variables: `{<CounterName>}`.
  - Example:
    ```xml
    <Description>
      [RivalAI Action]
      [DebugMessage:TRIGGER FIRED: Health < 50% | Faction: {Faction}]
      [ChangeBehaviorSubclass:true]
      [NewBehaviorSubclass:Fighter]
    </Description>
    ```

### B. MES Event Action Debugging
- **Tags**: `[DebugChatMessage:<Text>]` and `[DebugHudMessage:<Text>]`
- **Location**: Inside `[MES Event Action]`.
- **Mechanism** (`EventActionExecution.cs:701-716`):
  - `[DebugChatMessage:<Text>]`: Sends an in-game chat message attributed to the Event Action's SubtypeId with token evaluation.
  - `[DebugHudMessage:<Text>]`: Sends an on-screen HUD notification (3000ms duration) and a chat line to all players.
  - Example:
    ```xml
    <Description>
      [MES Event Action]
      [DebugHudMessage:EVENT EXECUTED: Territory Ladder Up triggered!]
      [ChangeCounters:true]
      [IncreaseCounters:TerritoryPoints]
      [IncreaseCountersAmount:10]
    </Description>
    ```

### C. Strict Production Rule
> [!WARNING]
> **Remove Debug Tags Before Production Release**:
> - `[DebugMessage]` is strictly a development diagnostic. It sends raw chat messages to all players without checking player distances, faction relations, broadcast radius, or radio antennas.
> - **Never** use `[DebugMessage]` as a substitute for real NPC chat messages.
> - For in-game player-facing dialogue, always use dedicated `[RivalAI Chat]` profiles configured with proper broadcast range (antenna range, or `[IgnoreAntennaRequirement:true]` + `[IgnoredAntennaRangeOverride:<m>]`), `[BroadcastChatType:]`, colors, and audio.

---

## 2. In-Game Admin Diagnostics & Logging Commands

MES and RivalAI include deep runtime logging and telemetry systems that can be toggled on-the-fly via in-game admin chat.

### A. Spawner Logging (`/MES.SpawnDebug.<Type>.<true/false>`)
Controls verbose diagnostic logging for the encounter spawner. Set `<Type>` to any of the following:

| Spawner Debug Type | Diagnostic Information Logged |
| :--- | :--- |
| `Spawning` | Spawner candidate evaluation, spawn distance checks, and final spawn execution. |
| `SpawnGroup` | Detailed eligibility breakdown (why each spawn group passed or failed its conditions). |
| `Zone` | Zone boundary detection, zone condition filters, and restricted spawn group checks. |
| `Pathing` | Spawner trajectory, altitude checks, and waypoint pathing generation. |
| `Manipulation` | Block replacement, weapon randomization, dereliction damage, and loot injection. |
| `CleanUp` | Grid despawn distance scans, player proximity checks, and cleanup timer evaluations. |
| `PostSpawn` | Post-spawn physics stabilization, ownership assignment, and AI attachment. |
| `GameLog` | Routes all spawner debug messages directly to `SpaceEngineers.log`. |

Also valid (`SpawnerDebugEnum`): `API`, `BlockLogic`, `Entity`, `Error`, `Settings`, `Startup`, `SpawnRecord`, `Dev`.

**[HARD] `All`** (MES `master` after 2.75.03, `9c8e211`, not released): `/MES.SpawnDebug.All.true` turns on every spawner debug type at once, `GameLog` included, so everything also goes to the game log; `.false` turns them all off. Behavior debug has no `All`. Up to 2.75.03 turn types on one at a time.

- **Example**: Enable detailed spawn group condition logging and send output to `SpaceEngineers.log`:
  ```
  /MES.SpawnDebug.SpawnGroup.true
  /MES.SpawnDebug.GameLog.true
  ```

### B. Behavior & AI Logging (`/MES.BehaviorDebug.<Type>.<true/false>`)
Controls verbose diagnostic logging for RivalAI grid behaviors. Set `<Type>` to any of the following:

| Behavior Debug Type | Diagnostic Information Logged |
| :--- | :--- |
| `Trigger` | Condition evaluation results, execution cooldowns, and trigger firing events. |
| `Action` | Action execution steps, variable mutations, and unhandled action failures. |
| `Condition` | Granular condition checks (custom counters, sandbox booleans, distance, speed). |
| `AutoPilot` | Waypoint navigation, collision evasion vectors, and flight mode calculations. |
| `TargetAcquisition`| Target scan passes, relation filtering, and potential target candidate lists. |
| `TargetEvaluation` | Target priority scoring, distance weighting, and subsystem target locking. |
| `Weapon` | WeaponCore/vanilla turret range clamping, firing sequences, and ammo checks. Per-gun status such as `NoAmmo`, `StaticWeaponNotAligned`, `ReadyToFire` (see `aircraft_behaviors_and_tuning.md` section 6). |
| `Command` | Squad radio command transmissions, frequency matches, and recipient processing. |
| `Chat` | Chat broadcast range checks, relation filtering, and broadcast transmission. |
| `Collision` | Raycasting results, asteroid/terrain obstacle avoidance, and evasion maneuvers. |
| `Despawn` | Timeout timers, player distance retreat checks, and force-despawn execution. |
| `BehaviorMode` | Subclass switching (`ChangeBehaviorSubclass`) and state transitions. |
| `BehaviorSetup` | Remote Control registration and behavior attachment at spawn (first stop when a grid has no AI at all). |
| `Owner` | Remote Control and grid ownership handling. |
| `General` | Behavior-manager messages, including `Exception in Parallel Calculations`. |
| `Error` | Caught exceptions. |
| `GameLog` | Routes all behavior debug messages directly to `SpaceEngineers.log`. |

Also valid (`BehaviorDebugEnum`): `BehaviorSpecific`, `Settings`, `Spawn`, `Startup`, `Target`, `Thrust` (logs thruster removal only), `Dev`, `BehaviorLog`.

- **Example**: Track why a combat trigger isn't firing:
  ```
  /MES.BehaviorDebug.Trigger.true
  /MES.BehaviorDebug.Condition.true
  /MES.BehaviorDebug.Action.true
  /MES.BehaviorDebug.GameLog.true
  ```

### C. Clipboard Export Commands (`/MES.Info.*`)
MES can dump internal diagnostic logs directly to your Windows clipboard for fast analysis without digging through log files:

| Chat Command | Shortcut | Data Copied to Windows Clipboard |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `/MES.Info.GetLogging.SpawnDebug.<Type>` | `/MES.IGLSD.<Type>` | Copies one spawner log buffer, e.g. `/MES.IGLSD.SpawnGroup`. |
| `/MES.Info.GetLogging.BehaviorDebug.<Type>` | `/MES.IGLBD.<Type>` | Copies one behavior log buffer, e.g. `/MES.IGLBD.Trigger`. |
| `/MES.Info.GetGridBehavior` | `/MES.IGGB` | Dumps targeted grid's active behavior, autopilot, and trigger states. |
| `/MES.Info.GetGridData` | `/MES.IGGD` | Dumps targeted grid's core MES entity parameters. |
| `/MES.Info.GetEligibleSpawnsAtPosition` | `/MES.GESAP` | Lists all spawn groups eligible to spawn at the player's current location. On MES `master` after 2.75.03 (`b728e8d` to `88ebcf0`, not released) it adds a `Spawner Status` section: for each spawner, whether the area is eligible, the active NPCs in its area, `Area Current / Max`, the area radius and `Time To Next Spawn Check`. |
| `/MES.Info.GetActiveNpcs` | | Every NPC grid MES tracks, by ownership class. On `master` after 2.75.03 (`7f05d02`) each grid also lists its `LinkedGrids`. |
| `/MES.Info.GetThreatScore` | `/MES.GTS` | Calculates and displays player combat threat score at current position. |
| `/MES.Info.GetDiagnostics` | `/MES.IGD` | General diagnostic telemetry dump. |

**[HARD] The `<Type>` is required** on `GetLogging` (`LoggerTools.GetLogging` needs 5 parts): a bare `/MES.IGLBD` or `/MES.IGLSD` only returns `Command Missing Parameters.` Each debug type has its own buffer, so copy each type you enabled (`.Trigger`, `.Condition`, `.Action`, …).

### D. Spawning & Encounter Force-Spawn Commands
- `/MES.Spawn.<Type>.<SpawnGroupName>` (`ChatMessage.ProcessSpawn`): runs a spawn of that type at your position; with the optional `.<SpawnGroupName>` it tries only that group (still subject to its conditions). Parts are split on `.`, so a SpawnGroup name containing a dot cannot be named here. Types and shortcuts: `SpaceCargoShip` (`/MES.SSCS`), `RandomEncounter` (`/MES.SRE`), `PlanetaryCargoShip` (`/MES.SPCS`), `PlanetaryInstallation` (`/MES.SPI`), `BossEncounter` (`/MES.SBE`), `Creature` (`/MES.SC`), `DroneEncounter` (`/MES.SDE`), `Prefab` (`/MES.SP`), `PrefabStation` (`/MES.SSP`). **[HARD]** `/MES.SSE` is rewritten to `/MES.Spawn.StaticEncounter`. From master after 2.75.02 (`a1895d9`, PR #447) that spawns a pending static encounter by name at its own coordinates (details in `testing_and_debugging.md` §2); up to 2.75.02 `ProcessSpawn` did not handle it (reply: `No Spawning Type From Chat`) and statics spawned only when a player came near. Statics reset with the commands below. It is an admin spawn: spawn timeouts and the global NPC cap are skipped, every other condition still applies, and the group needs a conditions profile with the matching spawn type (table in `testing_and_debugging.md` §2). Also `/MES.Spawn.WaveSpawner.<Space|Planet|Creature>` and `/MES.Spawn.ForceSpawnTimer`.
- There is no chat command to toggle all MES spawning, reset all counters or GPS-mark encounters; use `/MES.Debug.ChangeCounter` / `ChangeBool` below for single values and `/MES.Info.GetActiveNpcs` to list live NPCs.
- `/MES.Debug.ShowZone.<PublicName|ZoneSubtypeId>`, `/MES.Debug.HideZone.<...>`, `/MES.Debug.ShowAllZones`, `/MES.Debug.HideAllZones` *(2.74.04)*: Draw zone spheres (including multi-sphere zones) in-world, with temporary GPS markers.
- `/MES.Debug.CreateKPL.<Faction>.<Radius>.<Minutes>.<MaxEncounters>.<MinThreat>`: Creates a Known Player Location at your position. Minutes defaults to `30`; since 2.74.04 a value of `0` or less creates nothing (HUD: `KPL Not Created: Duration Must Be Greater Than 0`).
  - `ShowAllZones` draws KPLs too (they are active zones), but the visualizer keys zones by `PublicName`, then `Name`, and KPLs have neither, so only **one** KPL is drawn at a time and `ShowZone` cannot target a KPL (`ZoneDebugVisualizer.GetZoneKey`). Still the quickest way to see whether a KPL exists and how far it reaches.
- `/MES.Debug.DrawPaths`: toggles in-world lines from every AI-ready NPC to its waypoints (`AutoPilotSystem.DebugDrawingToWaypoints`): **green** current waypoint, **cyan** offset waypoint (attack-run line-up, escort slot), **magenta** planet-pathing waypoint, **red/orange** collision evasion. Drawn from the behavior loop, so it shows in singleplayer or on the hosting machine **[SOFT]: not expected to show for a client of a dedicated server**.
- `/MES.Debug.ChangeBool.<Name>.<true|false>`: sets a sandbox boolean. `/MES.Debug.ChangeCounter.<Name>.<Amount>`: **adds** `<Amount>` to a sandbox counter (use a negative amount to subtract; it is not a set).
- `/MES.Debug.ClearUniqueEncounters`: forgets which `UniqueEncounter` spawn groups have spawned. `/MES.Debug.ClearStaticEncounters`: invalidates every saved static-encounter record, so statics respawn.
- `/MES.Debug.ResetStaticEncounters` *(MES 2.75.00 / PR #389)*: replaces every spawned static encounter in the world with a fresh copy from current definitions (useful after a mod update changed prefabs, behaviors, or coordinates). Grids are closed directly (bypassing Despawn handling and Compromised/Despawn triggers) and re-spawned immediately. Skips any encounter whose grids have player-owned blocks (`FactionHelper.IsIdentityPlayer`), players seated, foreign attached grids, or other entities within 250m.
- `/MES.Debug.ResetStaticEncounters.Info`: dry-run report for `ResetStaticEncounters`; evaluates every spawned static encounter, reports which would reset or be skipped (with reasons), copies output to the clipboard, and writes to `SpawnRecord.log`.
- `/MES.Debug.ResetThisStaticEncounters.<SpawnGroupName>`: resets a single named static encounter so it respawns when players next approach. Fixed in commit `af492a5` to scan for the first `[StaticEncounter:true]` condition profile rather than aborting if non-static condition profiles are listed first.

### E. No `/RivalAI.*` Commands
RivalAI is merged into MES; current MES has no `/RivalAI.*` chat commands (none are parsed in `Sync/ChatMessage.cs`). For a grid's live AI state use `/MES.IGGB` (§C), and `/MES.Debug.DrawPaths` (§D) for waypoints.

## 3. The Agent Troubleshooting Protocol (When Something Fails)

### 6. Prefab SubtypeId vs. File Name Mismatch (Silent Spawn Failure / `Prefab Not Found`)
- **Cause**: The `SpawnGroup` references a prefab by its SubtypeId (e.g. `<Prefabs><Prefab SubtypeId="MyPatrolDrone">`), but the prefab file on disk has a different internal SubtypeId.
- **The Critical Rule**: **Space Engineers and MES completely ignore the prefab's file name on disk** (`MyPatrolDrone.sbc`). Spawning resolves *strictly and exclusively* against the `<Id><SubtypeId>` element declared inside the prefab XML:
  ```xml
  <Prefabs>
    <Prefab>
      <Id>
        <TypeId>MyObjectBuilder_PrefabDefinition</TypeId>
        <SubtypeId>MyPatrolDrone</SubtypeId> <!-- MUST MATCH THE SPAWNGROUP -->
      </Id>
    ...
  ```
- **Symptom**: Spawning silently fails, or `SpaceEngineers.log` reports `Prefab [MyPatrolDrone] was not found in PrefabManager` or `NullReferenceException` in `SpawnProcess`.
- **Fix**: Verify that the `<SubtypeId>` inside `Data/Prefabs/<FileName>.sbc` matches the `SubtypeId` in your `SpawnGroupDefinition` verbatim.

### 7. The `.sbcB5` Stale Binary Cache Trap
- **Cause**: When Space Engineers or the Dedicated Server loads a prefab `.sbc` for the first time, it compiles and caches it into a binary `.sbcB5` file in the same `Data/Prefabs/` folder. When a modder subsequently modifies the prefab `.sbc` (updating blocks, changing names, re-exporting, or tweaking weapon mounts), the game frequently **ignores the updated `.sbc` text file and loads the stale `.sbcB5` binary file instead**.
- **Symptom**:
  - In-game spawned grids do not reflect recent block changes or terminal renames.
  - Spawning fails or throws deserialization errors due to outdated grid offsets.
  - WeaponCore or RivalAI behaviors fail because newly added blocks are missing from the loaded binary cache.
- **Fix**: **Always delete the `.sbcB5` binary file whenever modifying a prefab.**
  ```powershell
  # Remove all stale sbcB5 cache files across prefabs
  Get-ChildItem -Path "Data/Prefabs" -Filter "*.sbcB5" -Recurse | Remove-Item -Force
  ```
  Keen will recompile fresh binary caches from the updated XML on the next world load.

### 8. Spawning As "Nobody" / Inactive AI (Missing or Dead Remote Control)
- **Cause**: The spawned prefab does not contain an undamaged, operational `MyObjectBuilder_RemoteControl` block, or the Remote Control block is not owned by the spawning NPC faction.
- **Result**: The grid spawns as unowned ("Nobody") or drifts inertly without executing its RivalAI behavior profile.
- **Fix**:
  1. Ensure the prefab contains at least one intact Remote Control block.
  2. If the prefab has multiple Remote Controls, MES attaches the behavior to the one flagged **Main Remote Control** in the prefab, otherwise the first one it finds (`BehaviorBuilder.cs`). To pick one by name, set `[ApplyBehaviorToNamedBlock:<CustomName>]` in the `[MES Manipulation]` profile.
  3. Ensure ownership is properly assigned via `[FactionOwner:<FactionTag>]` (Spawn Conditions, or inline in the `[Modular Encounters SpawnGroup]` Description).

### 9. Grid Sets Waypoints Properly But Refuses to Tilt Up or Down (Pitch Lock)
- **Cause**:
  1. `[LevelWithGravityWhenIdle:true]` state bleed: In `FighterPlane`, `Strike`, `Sniper`, and `HorseFighter`, entering idle sets `State.UseFlyLevelWithGravityIdle = true`. Because `EngageTarget` omits the idle parameter when calling `ActivateAutoPilot()`, the flag never resets, permanently latching `NewAutoPilotMode.LevelWithGravity` onto combat runs.
  2. `[FlyLevelWithGravity:true]`: Actively forces `LevelWithGravity` across all flight modes in all subclasses.
- **Result**: In `RotationSystem.cs:187`, `LevelWithGravity` forces gyro pitch to align solely with the planetary horizon, completely bypassing `directionToTarget`. The craft yaws toward waypoints but cannot dive to fire fixed guns or pitch up to climb toward breakaway waypoints.
- **Fix**: In the `[RivalAI Autopilot]` profile, explicitly disable both tags:
  ```xml
  [FlyLevelWithGravity:false]
  [LevelWithGravityWhenIdle:false]
  ```

### 10. NPC Reverses Into Space at Max Thrust / Overshoots Waypoints and Swings Back
- **Before MES 2.75.00 (runaway into space)**: `CalculateDirectForwardThrust` compared the unsigned `velocity.Length()` with `MaxSpeed`. A grid moving backwards faster than `MaxSpeed` (a rover rolling back downhill, or an aircraft facing its waypoint while drifting away with `MaxVelocityAngleForSpeedControl` above 90) showed `Brake To Desired Speed` in `/MES.IGGB`, fired reverse thrust and accelerated away indefinitely. Fixed in 2.75.00 (MES PR #402): it now uses the forward component of velocity, so a grid moving backwards gets forward thrust. Grids missing thruster directions no longer run away (field-observed).
- **2.75.00+ (overshoot and swing back, bounded)**: no reverse thrusters means `CalculateStoppingDistance()` is `0`, so the grid keeps full thrust until `WaypointTolerance`, coasts through the waypoint, turns around and comes back.
- **Fix**:
  1. `MaxVelocityAngleForSpeedControl:180` on 2.75.00+ (at most 90 on older builds); see [aircraft_behaviors_and_tuning.md](aircraft_behaviors_and_tuning.md) section 1.
  2. Add reverse thrusters so it can brake; see [behaviors_and_autopilot.md](behaviors_and_autopilot.md) §6A for what each direction does. On builds before 2.75.00, give it all six directions.
  3. For atmospheric aircraft with forward-only thrust, switch behavior subclass to `FighterPlane` (which uses velocity-aligned climbing breakaway without braking).
  3. For thrust-driven rovers, see [behaviors_and_autopilot.md §6.C](file:///c:/Users/blayl/source/repos/se-dev-mes/references/behaviors_and_autopilot.md#c-thrust-driven-rovers--ground-vehicles-best-practices--pitfalls-hard--soft) for the complete rover setup (`[UseSurfaceHoverThrustMode:true]`, `[FlyLevelWithGravity:false]`, and matching `[IdealPlanetAltitude]` to Remote Control height).

### 20. Jetpack inhibitor does nothing to players on a dedicated server
**[HARD]** code (MES `49b3380` `BlockLogic/JetpackInhibitor.cs`; game `MyCharacter.SetNetState`); **[SOFT]** seen on a live dedicated server.
- `[UseJetpackInhibitorEffect:true]` (RivalAI action) and MES's jetpack suppressor blocks both use `JetpackInhibitor`, which runs on the server only (`:34-39`). Without an antenna the ranges are fixed: dampeners off within 800 m, jetpack off within about 267 m (`:53-55`); no tag changes them.
