### 21. Workshop update refused: "Could not update because you are not the owner of this mod"
Applies to any mod (an encounter pack, a prefab mod) whose Workshop item another Steam account created, with you added as a contributor. **[HARD]** code (SE `MyGuiScreenMods.OnPublishModQuestionAnswer`, `MyModsLoadListResult`); **[SOFT]** the fix worked in game.
- Steam accepts a contributor's update; the refusal is the game's own check. Before publishing, the Mods screen looks the item up among your subscriptions and in the mod list of the world the screen was opened from, and stops if that copy's owner isn't you. If neither list holds the item, it publishes straight to the ID in the local mod's `modinfo.sbmi`.
- **Fix**: unsubscribe from the item and restart the game. Open the Mods screen from a world that doesn't load the item (a new game's settings will do), select the local mod, click Publish and answer Yes to "update". Unsubscribing alone still fails while the screen is opened from a test world that loads the Workshop copy.
- Keep the `modinfo.sbmi` that names the item: without it the game creates a new item with a new ID. Its `SteamIDOwner` line plays no part in the check.
- The game's publish adds no change note; write it on the item's Change Notes page afterwards.
- SEWorkshopTool (SEWT, the command-line uploader) runs its own owner check with no option to skip it ("Owner mismatch", 0.7.20 `Uploader.cs`), so a contributor item can only be updated from the game.

### 22. Ships with wheels, rotors or pistons count as several NPCs in area spawn limits (MES 2.71.41 and later)
- **Symptom**: a spawn type stops spawning with `Max SpawnType NPCs Reached/Exceeded for: <type>` (`/MES.SpawnDebug.Spawning.true`) while fewer encounters than its `MaxShipsPerArea` are nearby. `/MES.Info.GetActiveNpcs` lists each wheel and rotor top as an NPC of its own (on `master` after 2.75.03, `/MES.GESAP`'s Spawner Status shows them as extra `Small Grid` entries); the Entity List shows only the root grid.
- **[HARD] Cause** (`Spawning/PrefabSpawner.cs` `GridsSpawned`, since `9ea651c`, first released in 2.71.41): MES gives the spawn's NpcData to each grid of the prefab before suspensions, rotors and pistons attach their top parts, so every wheel, rotor head, hinge top and piston top is tracked as an NPC of that spawn type, and the area count (`NpcManager.GetAreaNpcCount`) counts each one: a rover with four wheels counts as five. The NpcData is saved with each top part, so the count survives a reload.
- **Applies to** the spawn types with an area limit (`AreaSize` and `MaxShipsPerArea` in each type's config): space and planetary cargo ships, random encounters, planetary installations and boss encounters. Drones and creatures have no area radius.
- **Fix pending**: MeridiusIX/Modular-Encounters-Systems#468 (open as of 2026-11-21) skips top-part grids and counts each spawn once. Until it ships, raise `MaxShipsPerArea` for the affected type to allow for the extra grids.

### 23. Other mods' storage on a prefab grid or block is lost when MES spawns it
- **Symptom**: a prefab grid or block carries another mod's storage (a script's settings, a mod's saved state), and the spawned copy has lost it. Only grids and blocks where MES adds its own storage are affected: every grid (NpcData), NPC thrusters and gyros, and blocks given container types.
- **[HARD] Cause** (`Spawning/Manipulation/StorageTools.cs` `ApplyCustomBlockStorage` and `ApplyCustomEntityStorage`, unchanged since 2021): MES looks for an existing storage component with TypeId `MyModStorageComponentBase`. Storage that has been through a save and load is written as `MyModStorageComponent`, which is how it appears in a prefab made from a saved grid. MES misses it and adds a second component, and on spawn the second replaces the first.
- **Fix pending**: MeridiusIX/Modular-Encounters-Systems#469 (open as of 2026-11-21) makes MES add its keys to the existing component. No workaround in the prefab is known.

## 5. Sim-Speed Health & Anti-Clang Physics Mitigations

### A. Voxel Phasing & Solver Saturation
- **The Problem**: High-speed aircraft or rovers crashing into terrain meshes can tunnel past the surface voxel boundary, trapping rigid bodies in continuous Havok collision solver loops and dropping server sim-speed from 1.0 to 0.2.
- **The Solution**:
  1. Disabled aircraft grids should be force-despawned immediately on compromise (`[Type:Compromised]` -> `[ForceDespawn:true]`).
  2. Rovers operating near voxels must maintain `[MinimumPlanetAltitude:15]` or higher to prevent chassis collision clipping.

### B. Raycasting & Trigger Throttling
- Non-urgent distance or condition checks should never run on every frame. Use stepped cooldown intervals (`[MinCooldownMs:5000]`, `[MaxCooldownMs:5001]`) rather than 100ms loops.
- Use `[MatchSenderReceiverOwners:true]` in command profiles to prevent grid-to-grid broadcasts from flooding all network entities.

# Dialogue Banks, Chat Profiles & Chatter Triggers Reference

How NPC chat actually runs: dialogue banks, the shared chat profile behind them, chance rolls, tokens, broadcast range, the trigger patterns that drive "radio chatter", and chat sounds (section 7). Everything here is generic: any number marked **[SOFT]** is an illustrative starting point to tune per server, not a rule.

**Classification**: **[HARD]** = read in the MES source (paths under `Data/Scripts/ModularEncountersSystems/`, MES `b8f86a2` / 2.74.06 dev, rechecked for the target-edge and recipient-filter items against `bc71965` (2.75.02); line numbers drift between builds, so search by function name if a line is off). **[SOFT]** = inferred, a design recommendation, or not yet measured in play. Each item says what it "Fails as" so it can be used as a pitfall line.

---

## 1. The Dialogue Pipeline

```text
Behavior : [DialogueBanks:MyBank]                      (one tag line per bank)
Action   : [PlayDialogueCue:true] [DialogueCueId:Attacked]
Bank file: <mod>/Data/DialogueBanks/MyBank             (XML, not an .sbc profile)
```

```xml
<DialogueBank>
  <ChatProfileId>ModPrefix-Chat-Radio</ChatProfileId>      <!-- a registered [RivalAI Chat] profile -->
  <DialogueCue>
    <DialogueCueId>Attacked</DialogueCueId>
    <Entries>                                               <!-- first matching <Entries> block wins -->
      <EventConditionId>ModPrefix-EventCondition-SomeState</EventConditionId>
      <Entry><Message>Taking fire!</Message><AudioId></AudioId><Weights>1</Weights></Entry>
    </Entries>
    <Entries>                                               <!-- no EventConditionId = fallback; list it last -->
      <Entry><Message>Contact.</Message><AudioId></AudioId><Weights>1</Weights></Entry>
    </Entries>
  </DialogueCue>
</DialogueBank>
```

- **[HARD] Loading**: `ProfileManager.GetDialogueBank` reads `Data\DialogueBanks\{name}` from the first loaded mod that has the file (the tag value is the literal file name, extension included) and caches the bank by name.
- **[HARD] One bank per grid**: `CoreBehavior.cs` (`Beginning DialogueBank setup`) picks one of the behavior's listed banks at random and keeps it for the grid's life.
- **[HARD] Entry choice**: `DialogueBank.GetChatProfile` walks the cue's `<Entries>` blocks in order and uses the first whose `<EventConditionId>` is empty or a currently-true `[MES Event Condition]`; then picks one `<Entry>` by `<Weights>`.
- **[HARD] Everything fails silent in play.** The only trace is one game-log line at load:
  - Missing bank file: `Could Not Add DialogueBank To Behavior: [name]` (`TriggerSystem.cs`, `[DialogueBanks:` parse). The behavior keeps an empty bank, so every cue does nothing.
  - Unknown `<ChatProfileId>`: `Chat Profile Not Registered in Profile Manager: [id]` (`DialogueBank.init`). `GetChatProfile` then returns false for every cue.
  - Unknown cue id, no `<Entries>` block that passes, or an `<EventConditionId>` that isn't registered (that block is skipped): no broadcast, no log.
  - Audit: `audit_mes_references.ps1` checks the bank file and chat profile; `audit_mes_tags.ps1` checks the chat profile settings (section 2).

---

## 2. Dialogue Banks Share One Chat Profile

- **[HARD] A bank's chat profile is one shared object.** `ProfileManager.GetDialogueBank` caches each bank by name, `DialogueBank.init()` builds one `_chatProfile` per bank, and `GetChatProfile` hands that same object to `ActionSystem.cs` (`PlayDialogueCue` → `_broadcast.BroadcastRequest`). State on the profile is shared by every grid using that bank file, server-wide.
- **[HARD code; SOFT seen once] Except grids set up at the same moment.** Each new NPC registers on its own background task (`Tasks/BehaviorRegister.cs:30`). When two grids miss the `GetDialogueBank` cache together (`Helpers/ProfileManager.cs:889-949`, MES `49b3380`), each loads and keeps its own copy, with its own chat profile and throttle; the lock only stops a second `Add`. A wing spawned together, or every NPC after a world load, can talk over each other. Line picks also create `new Random()` per call (`Files/DialogueBank.cs:176-202`), seeded from the clock, so two picks in the same moment roll the same line. Seen in game: two wingmen sent the same line in the same second. Nothing in SBC works around it.
- **[HARD] `[MaxChats:]` becomes a server-wide lifetime cap.** `ChatProfile.ProcessChat`: `ChatSentCount >= MaxChats` sets `UseChat = false` on the shared copy. **Fails as**: the first grids to speak use up the voice for everyone until restart. Never set it on a bank's chat profile (default `-1` is fine).
- **[HARD] `[MinTime:]`/`[MaxTime:]` is a shared timer.** `ProcessChat` drops a line while `SecondsUntilChat` hasn't elapsed (`Chat Timer Not Ready`, not queued) and rerolls the window after each send. **Fails as**: a long window silences the whole voice. The defaults (`MinTime 0`, `MaxTime 1`) mean no wait. Also: `ChatProfile.InitTags` lowers `MinTime` to `MaxTime` when it is larger, and the default `MaxTime` is `1`, so `[MinTime:30]` alone gives a 1 s window with no error; set both (`audit_mes_tags.ps1` check 18). The window is `Rnd.Next(MinTime, MaxTime)`, which excludes `MaxTime`: `[MinTime:30]` + `[MaxTime:60]` waits 30-59 s.
- **[SOFT] A short shared timer works as a squad throttle.** A window of a few seconds allows one line per bank however many grids react to the same event (for example a squad acquiring one target). Tune to squad size, grids per bank and desired chattiness. Trade-off: a rare, important line is dropped if another grid on the bank spoke just before.
- **[HARD] The first grid's custom author name sticks.** `BroadcastSystem.BroadcastRequest` sets `chat.CheckForCustomNames = true` once and copies `Npc.ChatAuthorName` (from a manipulation's `[CustomChatAuthorName:]`) into the shared `chat.Author`. **Fails as**: every later grid on that bank uses the first grid's name. Leave `[CustomChatAuthorName:]` off grids whose behavior has a bank.
- **[HARD] The bank is per behavior and cannot use `{Faction}`.** `[DialogueBanks:]` is read as a literal file name. **Fails as**: a behavior shared by several factions' spawn groups speaks one voice for all of them. Make one behavior copy per faction.
- **[HARD] Chance and range live on the chat profile**, and a bank names exactly one `<ChatProfileId>`, so chance and range are per bank file. **[SOFT]** Generate tiered bank files (for example one per chat range) from one source draft instead of duplicating lines by hand.
- **[HARD] Same-line suppression is per grid.** `LastChatMessageSent` lives on each grid's `BroadcastSystem`; one grid never repeats its previous line unless `[AllowDuplicatedMessages:true]`.

## 3. Chance Rolls

- **[HARD] Two independent rolls multiply.** `ActionSystem.cs` rolls the action's `[Chance:]` (skipped at 100); `BroadcastSystem.BroadcastRequest` rolls the chat profile's `[Chance:]` per broadcast (skipped at 100). **Technique**: for per-cue chance, set the chat profile to `100` and put a chance on each cue's action.
- **[HARD] A failed action roll skips the whole action** (`ActionSystem.cs` returns before any tag runs). **Fails as**: a chance on an action that also does essential work (points, despawn, spawns) randomly skips that work. **[SOFT]** Put chat in its own action and list both actions with `[ActionExecution:All]`.
- **[HARD] A failed roll still uses the trigger's cooldown.** The trigger is already `Triggered` before the action rolls. **Fails as**: a lower chance gives a longer average interval (cooldown ÷ chance), not a retry.
- **[HARD] Order inside one action**: `PlayDialogueCue` runs before `ManuallyActivateTrigger` and the `[ChatData:]` broadcast. A last-words cue in an action that also triggers a despawn goes out first.

## 4. Tokens in Chat Messages

- **[HARD] Available** (`BroadcastSystem.cs`): `{GridName}`, `{AntennaName}`, `{Faction}` (the speaking NPC); `{GPS}` (a GPS point at the NPC); then `IdsReplacer` tokens (custom strings, counters, sandbox variables, `{SpawnGroupName}`).
- **[HARD] `{PlayerName}` and `{PlayerFactionName}` are filled in per recipient**, inside the per-player send loop. Every reader sees their own name, so the NPC appears to address each reader personally.
- **[HARD] There is no token for the target's or attacker's name.** No such replacement exists in `BroadcastSystem.cs` or `IdsReplacer.ReplaceId`.

---

## 5. Broadcast Range

- **[HARD] A chat from a `[Type:PlayerFar]` trigger can reach nobody.** The trigger fires only with no player inside its `[TargetDistance:]`, so a chat with `[IgnoredAntennaRangeOverride:]` at or below that distance (and without `[SendToAllOnlinePlayers:true]`) has no one in range. Give it a radius well beyond `TargetDistance`.
- **[HARD] With `[IgnoreAntennaRequirement:true]`, `[IgnoredAntennaRangeOverride:]` is the broadcast radius** (`BroadcastSystem.cs` sets `HighestRadius` from it, then skips players beyond it). **Fails as**: `9999999` sends the line to every player on the server. **[SOFT]** That value is a common copy-paste default in chat profiles.
- **[HARD, 2.75.00 and master `bc71965`] `[SendToAllOnlinePlayers:true]` now skips players with no character.** The NPC-check migration turned `!SendToAll && (IsBot || Character == null)` into `!SendToAll && IsIdentityNPC(...) || Character == null`, so a dead or respawning player no longer receives it (`BroadcastSystem.cs`, recipient filter; reported as MeridiusIX/Modular-Encounters-Systems#414).

---

## 6. Triggers & Targeting for Chatter

- **[HARD] `[ElseActions:]` also runs when the trigger's own type check fails**, not only when its conditions fail (`TriggerProfile.ActivateTrigger`: any `!Triggered` with `UseElseActions`, gated only by cooldown; `TriggerSystem.cs` then runs `ElseActions`). **Fails as**: on a Timer, AcquiredTarget or Damage trigger the else actions fire on every check with no event. **[SOFT]** Only use ElseActions on Manual triggers.
- **If/else chains with Manual triggers.**
  - **[HARD] mechanism**: `ManuallyActivatedTriggerNames` only searches the behavior's own `Triggers` list, so Manual triggers must be attached to the behavior. TriggerGroups don't nest (`TriggerGroupProfile.cs` only reads `[Triggers:]`).
  - **[SOFT] pattern** (not yet play-tested): event trigger → action activates Manual trigger A (a condition), whose `ElseActions` activate Manual trigger B, and so on, ending in a fallback action. Example: target-type callouts checking static > aircraft > on foot > fast > far > generic.
- **[HARD] Target conditions** (`ConditionProfile.cs`): `IsTargetStatic`, `IsTargetPlayer` (a player character, i.e. on foot), `IsTargetGrid`, `TargetAltitudeCheck` (height above terrain per `PlanetEntity.cs`; not yet play-tested, and the cutoff for "is an aircraft" is a per-server choice), `CheckTargetSpeed`, `CheckTargetDistance`. There is no condition for the target's grid size, name or block types. **Fails as**: `CheckGridSize` tests the NPC's **own** grid, not the target.
- **[HARD] `AcquiredTarget` fires once per new lock** (`TriggerChecks.CheckAcquiredTarget` returns and clears `TargetAcquired`). **Fails as**: with `[MaxActions:1]` a grid only ever reacts to its first target. For repeat callouts use `[MaxActions:-1]` with a cooldown.

### Target-state edges and debouncing

- **[HARD] `NoTarget` fires whenever the grid has no target, including before its first lock** (`CheckNoTarget` is `!HasTarget()`). Edge flags come from `TargetingSystem.cs`: `TargetAcquired` (none → some), `TargetLost` (some → none), `TargetSwitched` (A → B). **Fails as**: a "lost contact" line on `NoTarget` plays shortly after spawn. Use `LostTarget` for "had one, lost it".
- **[HARD] Edge flags last one trigger pass; an edge during a cooldown is dropped, not delayed.** `TriggerSystem.cs` clears `TargetAcquired`, `TargetLost`, `TargetSwitched`, `TargetChanged` and `BehaviorTriggerA`-`G` at the end of every pass, and `ValidateTrigger` skips the type check while on cooldown. **Fails as**: a `LostTarget`, `AcquiredTarget` or `BehaviorTrigger*` trigger with a cooldown misses any edge that happens during it. Keep such triggers cooldown-free and rate-limit in what they arm instead.
- **[HARD] Before MES 2.75.02 (`d6e5e43`, PR #405), the first `AcquiredTarget`, `LostTarget`, `SwitchedTarget` or `ChangedTarget` trigger to check its flag also cleared it**, so in one pass only the first such trigger in the behavior's list order saw the edge. **Fails as** (older builds): a chatter trigger listed before a behavior-switching trigger of the same type silently steals the edge from it. From `d6e5e43` every trigger of that type sees the edge in the same pass. On older builds give each grid one trigger per edge type, or make the other consumers state-based (`aircraft_behaviors_and_tuning.md` §2).
- **[HARD] `[ConditionCheckResetsTimer:true]` resets the cooldown only when the trigger's conditions fail, not when its type check fails** (`TriggerProfile.ValidateTrigger`). **Technique**: to require a state to hold for N seconds in a row, use `[Type:Timer]` with a condition for the state, for example `[NoTarget:true]`, plus `[ConditionCheckResetsTimer:true]`.
- **[SOFT] Pattern: "lost contact" only after a real loss** (not yet confirmed in play). A `LostTarget` trigger arms a disabled `Timer` trigger with `[EnableTriggers:]` and `[ResetCooldownTimeOfTriggers:]`; the Timer trigger uses the debounce above, plays the chatter and disables itself. Put the disable in its own action (section 3) so a failed chance roll can't leave the trigger armed. A cooldown on the `LostTarget` trigger is a per-server choice; it caps how often one grid can say the line. Before `d6e5e43` this `LostTarget` trigger takes the edge from any later `LostTarget` trigger on the grid (above), so switch the grid back to patrol with a `NoTarget` timer, not `LostTarget`.

---

## 7. Chat Sounds

Rechecked against MES master `5899d09`.

```text
[ChatMessages:Contact. Moving to intercept.]
[ChatAudio:ArcHudGPSNotification1]
[BroadcastChatType:Chat]
[ChatMessages:Taking fire!]
[ChatAudio:ArcHudGPSNotification2]
[BroadcastChatType:Chat]
```

- **[HARD] One `[BroadcastChatType:]` per message, or nothing is sent.** With fewer type lines than messages the type stays `None` and `ChatProfile.ProcessChat` drops the line (`Broadcast None` in the chat debug log), text and sound both. A bank's chat profile needs at least one. `audit_mes_tags.ps1` check 19 flags short lists.
- **[HARD] One `[ChatAudio:]` line per `[ChatMessages:]` line, matched by position.** `ChatProfile.GetChatAndSoundFromLists` uses the sound only when there are at least as many `[ChatAudio:]` entries as messages. **Fails as**: one `[ChatAudio:]` for three messages plays no sound on any of them. `[BroadcastChatType:]`, `[ChatAvatar:]` and `[ChatVolumeMultiplier:]` pair the same way. Each line is one entry: `[ChatAudio:A,B]` is a single sound named `A,B`.
- **[HARD] In a dialogue bank each `<Entry>` has its own `<AudioId>`** (`DialogueBank.cs` builds a one-message chat from the chosen entry). Empty or `None` means no sound.
- **[HARD] The sound plays in 2D on each recipient's client**, so it is heard in vacuum and with realistic sound on (`EffectManager.ProcessPlayerSoundEffect`, `PlaySound(..., force2D: true, alwaysHearOnRealistic: true)`). Volume is the sound definition's `<Volume>` times `[ChatVolumeMultiplier:]`.
- **[HARD] Chat sounds queue per player:** the next one waits until the current one stops. **Fails as**: a looping sound (`<Loopable>true</Loopable>`, such as `ArcSoundBlockAlert1`) never stops, so that player hears no other NPC chat sound until they change what they control or respawn. Use short one-shot sounds.
- **[HARD] Name lookup** (`MySoundPair.Init`): the exact sound SubtypeId first, then `Arc` + name and `Real` + name. A name that matches nothing plays nothing and only writes `Could not find any sound for '<name>'` to the **client** log.

### Common NPC chat sounds

From the `[ChatAudio:]` values in 642 locally installed workshop mods (6 of them use chat audio):

| SubtypeId | Source | Use |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ArcHudGPSNotification1` | Vanilla (GPS ping) | Most used; a short ping before any line |
| `ArcHudGPSNotification2` | Vanilla (GPS ping) | Second most used; gives a second voice or faction a different ping |
| `ArcHudGPSNotification3` | Vanilla (GPS ping) | Third variant |
| `MES-HostileJumpIn` | Ships with MES | Hostile arrival sting, no extra mod needed |

- A voiced line needs its own sound: an `.xwm` file plus a `MyObjectBuilder_AudioDefinition` with `<Category>HUD</Category>` in the mod's `Data/Audio*.sbc`.
- **Pitfalls seen in workshop mods**: `GreetingSoundId-A`/`-B` is a placeholder from the MES wiki, not a real sound (silent in three mods). `ArcHudSensors` is not vanilla; it comes from another workshop mod, so it is silent without that mod.

Each refresh re-lists it. - **[HARD] Price**: `CustomPrice` if set (> -1), otherwise MES's minimum-value table or `EconomyHelper.CalculatePrefabCost`, then the price multipliers. Set `CustomPrice` for a fixed price. - `` on the item is what the game checks against the buyer's PCU limit (`MyStoreBlock.BuyPrefabInternal`); the world block limits are checked against the real prefab as well. #### Store-items file traps (`audit_sbc.ps1` check 7) MES reads the file with `MyAPIGateway.Utilities.SerializeFromXML`, a plain `XmlSerializer` (`ProfileManager.GetStoreItemContainer`). It searches the loaded mods in load order for `Data\StoreItems\` (exact file name) and uses the first copy that parses. Tested on .NET Framework 4.8, the game's runtime. - **[HARD] A repeated single-value element keeps its FIRST copy.** In `1000...15` only 1000 is read; the second copy is skipped unread, with no error or log. Edit the first copy, or the change does nothing. Description tags are the opposite: a repeated single-value tag keeps the LAST copy that parses (see [`profiles_and_tags.md`](profiles_and_tags.md) §3). - **[HARD] A repeated list wrapper keeps its LAST copy.** Two `` blocks (or two ``, two ``): every copy is read, then the last replaces the others, so the items in the earlier blocks vanish. Put all items in one block. Inside a block, ``, `` and `` repeat normally; `` entries are added to the store too. A second bare `` directly under `` is a single value, so it is ignored. - **[HARD] One bad value drops the whole file**, and MES logs `Could Not Serialize From XML` only when the Error debug flag is on, so every `[MES Store]` profile using the file just stocks nothing. `XmlSerializer` throws on: - a non-number or a number out of range (`MinPriceMultiplier`/`MaxPriceMultiplier` are `short`, max 32767; `5.0` and an empty value fail too); - a sign on `RequiredMod` (`+5`, `-1`); - a wrong-case or padded `ItemType` (`hydrogen`, ` Hydrogen `); - `True` for `IsCustomItem` (only `true`/`false`/`1`/`0`); - a `` or child element inside a value, a ``, or an `xmlns` on the root. - **[HARD] Unknown element names are ignored silently**, and names are case-sensitive (`` for ``, `` for ``). - **[HARD] `ItemType` `Gas` breaks the stocking action**: `StoreProfile.CreateStoreItem` returns null for it and `AddItemToStore` throws, so the `ApplyStoreProfiles` action stops part-way (the rest of that store and the rest of the action are skipped; log `Error while executing action: 'ApplyStoreProfiles'`). Use `Hydrogen` or `Oxygen`. An item with no `ItemType` (`None`) is skipped. - **[HARD] A missing `` list** (or `xsi:nil="true"`) makes `StoreProfile.Setup` throw on `StoreItems.Length` for every profile using the file (read in code, not tested in game: it may stop the world loading). - **[HARD] Store limits are shared.** `StoreProfile._storeLimits` is `static`: every `[MES Store]` profile uses the `` of the last-loaded profile whose file has them, whichever file it reads itself. Only the first `` entry is used. - A `StoreItemId` used twice (including the `/` ids MES makes for `` entries) is stocked from every match: its draw chance multiplies, items merge into one listing with the amounts added, and a prefab is listed twice. ### Part 2: MES Store Profile (`[MES Store]`) ```xml Inventory ModPrefix-StoreProfile-HeavyCruiser [MES Store] [FileSource:ModPrefix-StoreItems.xml] [MinOfferItems:1] [MaxOfferItems:1] [RequiredOffers:HeavyCruiser] ``` - `[FileSource:]`: File name under `Data\StoreItems\` (Part 1). - `[Offers:]` / `[Orders:]`: StoreItemIds eligible for random selection; `[RequiredOffers:]` / `[RequiredOrders:]`: always listed. - `[Min/MaxOfferItems:]`, `[Min/MaxOrderItems:]`: How many items the refresh rolls. - `[AddedItemsCombineQuantity:]`, `[AddedItemsAveragePrice:]`, `[EqualizeOffersAndOrders:]`. - There is no `[StoreItems:]` or `[ItemsRequireInventory:]` tag; MES ignores both. ### Part 3: `GridsForSale` Is Not Needed for MES Stores [HARD] - `` in `FactionTypes_Economy.sbc` is read only by Keen's own station store generator (`MyGenericFactionTypeStrategy.GenerateGridOffers`). MES never reads it, and the purchase path (`MyStoreBlock.BuyPrefabInternal`) never checks it. An MES store sells any prefab in its store-items file. - Add a prefab there only if you want **Keen-generated** economy stations of that faction type to roll it too, at Keen's calculated price. Automated Store Refreshing (Mike Dude's GVK Pattern) In long-running multiplayer worlds, economy station store inventories become depleted or cluttered. RivalAI actions can dynamically refresh store inventories on a timer: ```xml Inventory GVK-Store-Action-UpdateRoverSales [MES AI Action] [ApplyStoreProfiles:true] [ClearStoreContentsFirst:true] [StoreBlocks:Store-Rovers] [StoreProfiles:GVK-Store-StoreProfile-BasicVehicles] ``` - `[ApplyStoreProfiles:true]`: Pushes fresh store profiles to matching blocks. - `[ClearStoreContentsFirst:true]`: Flushes old or empty listings. - `[StoreBlocks:]`: Targets specific store terminal blocks on the station grid. --- ## 3. Physical Clearance & Icon Requirements ### A. Where a Bought Grid Spawns [HARD] `MyStoreBlock.BuyPrefabInternal` searches for free space near the store block, sized to the prefab's bounding sphere: - **In natural gravity** (a store not on a Keen station counts as an Outpost there): `MyRespawnComponentBase.FindPositionAbovePlanet` with an optimal distance of 60 m from the store and up to 30 tries, deploying at 1.05 × the prefab's radius above the ground. - **In space**: `MyEntities.FindFreePlace` around the store, up to 20 tries. - No free spot: the purchase fails with `FreePositionNotFound`. Before that, it fails on PCU (`NotEnoughPCU`) or world block limits. - **[SOFT]** Leave open, flat ground around a planetary store, larger than the biggest grid it sells; a store boxed in by station structure or steep terrain fails intermittently. ### B. Icons & Tooltip Images - **[SOFT] PNG vs DDS**: DDS textures for prefab store previews frequently fail to load or become corrupted in the client cache. Always use **256x256 PNG** files for `` and ``. - **[HARD] Keen Store Icon Bug (Topic 49223)**: Mod-added ships in economy stores have an engine bug where preview icons occasionally fail to render until the client `.sbcB5` cache is regenerated. ### C. Store Icons & Preview Thumbnails Getting prefab thumbnails to render correctly in economy store blocks requires navigating three specific engine requirements: ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph Store_List ["Store Catalog Listing"] SI["StoreItems.sbc
<StoreItem>
<Icon>Textures\GUI\Icons\Store\Ship.png</Icon>"] SI -->|"Renders in"| UI_List["Catalog List Row"] end subgraph Preview_Pane ["Detail Preview Pane"] PF["Prefabs.sbc
<Prefab>
<Icon>Textures\GUI\Icons\Store\Ship.png</Icon>
<TooltipImage>Textures\GUI\Icons\Store\Ship.png</TooltipImage>"] PF -->|"Renders in"| UI_Preview["Ship Detail Preview Window"] end ``` 1. **The Dual Declaration Requirement (Catalog List vs. Preview Pane)**: - **`` Definition (`StoreItems.sbc`)**: Must include `` when the store uses vanilla `StoreItemDefinition`s. MES store-item XML (§1 Part 1) has no icon field, so for MES-stocked grids the prefab's own icons below are what render. - **`` Definition (`Prefabs.sbc`)**: Must include **both** `` and ``. - **[HARD] The Missing Preview Bug**: Keen's store block UI queries `` when a player clicks a ship to view its stats. If `` is omitted from the prefab definition, the preview pane renders completely blank/transparent. 2. **Image Format & Resolution (DDS vs. PNG)**: - **Modern Standard (BC7 DDS)**: In modern Space Engineers (DX11), **BC7** is the gold standard for GUI icons and store thumbnails. It provides superior compression quality without the blocky color artifacts of older formats: ```bash texconv.exe -f BC7_UNORM_SRGB -m 1 -y InputIcon.png -o OutputFolder/ ``` - **Legacy Fallback (BC3 / DXT5 DDS)**: ```bash texconv.exe -f BC3_UNORM -m 1 -srgb -y InputIcon.png -o OutputFolder/ ``` - **The #1 DDS Trap: Mipmaps (`-m 1`)**: - When saving DDS icons, **never generate a mipmap chain (hard cap to 1 mip level)**. - If mipmaps are included, Keen's texture streaming system treats the icon like a 3D model texture. On clients with Texture Quality set to Medium or Low, the game displays a low-resolution mip (e.g. 16x16 or 32x32), turning the store icon into blurry mud. - **Dimensions**: Must be **Power of Two (POT)** (256x256 or 512x512) with a 1:1 square aspect ratio. Non-square textures stretch and distort. - **Color Space & Alpha**: Always use **sRGB** (prevents washed-out colors) and **straight alpha** (prevents dark fringe halos around edges). - **PNG Fallback**: Standard 256x256 32-bit RGBA PNG files work cleanly if you do not want to run a DDS conversion pipeline. 3. **Pathing Syntax**: - Must be mod-root relative: e.g. `Textures\GUI\Icons\Store\ModPrefix_HeavyCruiser.png`. - **Always use Windows backslashes (`\`)**: Forward slashes (`/`) cause Keen's content loader on Windows dedicated servers to fail file resolution. 4. **The Client `.sbcB5` Binary Cache Trap (Keen Bug Topic 49223)**: - Keen precompiles SBC files into binary `.sbcB5` cache files in `%AppData%\SpaceEngineers\Cache\`. - When a mod updates an icon path or adds a new store prefab, clients frequently retain stale null references from their cached `.sbcB5` file. - **Resolution**: Clients must clear their `.sbcB5` cache, or the mod author must update the mod version/timestamp to force cache regeneration. --- ## 4. A player who picks it up gets a delivery contract to a station. From 2.74.03, MES raises Keen's `MySpawnGroupDefinition.OnSpawnGroupGridsCreated` for its own spawns, so this (and Keen's grid-triggered contracts, if the vanilla `` defines a contract trigger) works on MES encounters. - **Opt-in per spawn**: `[EnableItemTriggeredContracts:true]` in `[MES Spawn Conditions]` (default `false`). MES forces it `true` for vanilla SpawnGroups it converts (`SpawnGroupManager.cs`, `Context.IsBaseGame`). - **[HARD] Requirements** (`MySessionComponentItemTriggeredContracts.OnEncounterSpawned`): server side, world setting **Economy enabled**, and at least one `MyCargoContainer` with an inventory on the spawned grids. The item goes into one random cargo container. Grids without cargo containers never get one. - **[HARD] MES overrides the contract definition**: at load, MES re-initializes **every** `SessionComponentItemTriggeredContractsDefinition` (vanilla and other mods') with its own hardcoded values: `SpawnChance 0.35`, `AllowEnemyFactions true`, the five `Deliver_*` entries above at weight 1. Custom tuning of that definition in another mod has no effect while MES is loaded. - **Whitelist by SpawnGroup name, per session**: a spawn with the flag adds its SpawnGroup name to the whitelist before the grids are created. The list is not saved, and once a group is on it, any later spawn of that group in the same session qualifies, even through a conditions profile without the flag. - **2.74.03 bug, fixed in 2.74.04**: the whitelist started empty, which Keen treats as "all SpawnGroups", so every MES spawn could roll a contract item until the first opted-in group spawned (patch note: "the first encounter type that spawned after a load would always contain an item contract"). 2.74.04 seeds it with a dummy entry.

# MES Events, Zones & Sandbox Persistence Reference

Architectural reference covering global MES Events, dynamic spherical/box zones, boolean master gates, and session sandbox variable persistence.

---

## 1. MES Event System Architecture

Unlike RivalAI Triggers which run locally on in-world grids via Remote Control blocks, **MES Events** run globally at the session level via `EventManager`:
- **Server-Authoritative**: Runs exclusively on dedicated servers and host machines (`IsServer`).
- **No Grid Required**: Executes even when no NPC grids exist in the world.
- **Global Coordination**: Manages server-wide progression, zone radius expansions, territory ladders, weekly schedules, and scripted campaign encounters.

### A. Tag-Name Matrix: RivalAI Grid Triggers vs. MES Event Actions
MES Events and RivalAI Grid Triggers use **different tag names** for sub-profiles and lists. Using the wrong variant silently fails:

| Feature | RivalAI Grid Action Tag | MES Event Action Tag | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Encounter Spawner** | `[Spawner:ProfileId]` | `[SpawnData:ProfileId]` | Using `[Spawner:]` in an Event Action causes silent failure (`Spawner.Count == 0`). |
| **Chat Message** | `[UseChatBroadcast:true]` + `[ChatData:ProfileId]` | `[UseChatBroadcast:true]` + `[ChatData:ProfileId]` | Same tag on both sides (`ActionProfile.cs:73`, `EventActionProfile.cs:73`). There is no `[Chat:]` tag anywhere. |
| **Counter Changes** | `[IncreaseSandboxCounters:Name]` | `[ChangeCounters:true]` + `[IncreaseCounters:Name]` | MES Event Actions **require** `[ChangeCounters:true]` gating. |
| **Zone Resizing** | `[ChangeZoneAtPosition:true]` (grid inside the zone) or `[ChangeZoneOnlyByName:true]` (any distance, 2.74.00) + `[ZoneName:]` + `[ZoneRadiusChangeType:]` + `[ZoneRadiusChangeAmount:]` | `[ChangeZoneByName:true]` + `[ZoneNames:]` + `[ZoneRadiusChangeTypes:]` + `[ZoneRadiusChangeAmounts:]` (2.74.00) | RivalAI actions use **singular** tag names and have no `ChangeZoneByName`; MES Event Actions use **plural lists**. `ActionSystem.cs:1916` runs the RivalAI zone block only when one of the two RivalAI gates is true. |

---

## 2. Boolean Master-Gate Protocol (MES Events Only)

> [!CAUTION]
> **The Golden Rule**: Sub-configuration tags inside `[MES Event Action]` and `[MES Event Condition]` **do nothing on their own**. They are guarded by boolean master gates that default to `false`.
> Omitting the master gate causes **silent failure**: MES logs no errors, but skips the action entirely.

### A. MES Event Action Master Gates (`EventActionExecution.cs`)

| Master Gating Tag (Required) | Dependent Child Tags Enabled | Purpose / Effect |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `[ChangeCounters:true]` | `[SetCounters:]`, `[SetCountersAmount:]`, `[IncreaseCounters:]`, `[IncreaseCountersAmount:]`, `[DecreaseCounters:]`, `[DecreaseCountersAmount:]` | Mutating Sandbox integer counters. |
| `[ChangeBooleans:true]` | `[SetBooleansTrue:]`, `[SetBooleansFalse:]` | Setting Sandbox boolean variables. |
| `[SpawnEncounter:true]` | `[SpawnCoords:]`, `[SpawnFactionTags:]`, `[SpawnData:]`, `[SpawnReplaceKeys:]`, `[SpawnReplaceValues:]` | Spawning encounters via event actions. **[HARD]** `{Faction}` in the `[SpawnGroups:]` list of the spawner that `[SpawnData:]` names *does* resolve here (not in the `[SpawnData:]` value itself) — a bespoke, index-aligned `{Faction}` → `[SpawnFactionTags:]` replace, not `IdsReplacer`. See [`references/profiles_and_tags.md`](references/profiles_and_tags.md) §5 Rule 1. |
| `[ChangeZoneByName:true]` | `[ZoneNames:]`, `[ZoneRadiusChangeTypes:]`, `[ZoneRadiusChangeAmounts:]` | Dynamically modifying spherical zones by name (`PublicName`, §4 rule 2; `Persistent` zones only). **[HARD]** Change types are `ModifierEnum`: `Set`, `Add`, `Subtract`, `Multiply`, `Divide`. `Increase`/`Decrease` fail to parse, the entry is dropped, and the index-aligned change is silently skipped. Same values for the RivalAI `[ZoneRadiusChangeType:]`. |
| `[ChangeZoneAtPosition:true]` | `[ZoneCoords:]`, `[ZoneToggleActiveModes:]` | Activating/deactivating zones at coordinates. |
| `[ToggleEvents:true]` | `[ToggleEventIds:]`, `[ToggleEventIdModes:]`, `[ToggleEventTags:]`, `[ToggleEventTagModes:]` | Enabling or disabling other MES Events. **[HARD]** These same four tags also exist on `[RivalAI Action]`/`[MES AI Action]` (a different C# class, `ActionReferenceProfile.cs`). On that side they token-resolve via `IdsReplacer`; here, in `[MES Event Action]`, they don't — `EventActionExecution.cs` never wraps them. Full rundown: [`references/profiles_and_tags.md`](references/profiles_and_tags.md) §6C. |
| `[ResetCooldownTimeOfEvents:true]` | `[ResetEventCooldownIds:]`, `[ResetEventCooldownTags:]` | Forcing events back to 0 or full cooldown. Same RivalAI-vs-Event dual-declaration/token-asymmetry as `[ToggleEvents:]` above — see [`references/profiles_and_tags.md`](references/profiles_and_tags.md) §6C. |
| `[UseChatBroadcast:true]` | `[ChatData:]`, `[UseChatOverrideAuthor:true]`, `[ChatOverrideAuthor:]`, `[UseChatOverrideMessage:true]` | Transmitting HUD / chat notifications. |
| `[SetSandboxStrings:true]` *(2.74.00)* | `[SandboxStrings:name,value]` | Sets sandbox string variables (sandbox-var tokens resolve in name and value). **[HARD]** An entry with an empty name or value hits a `return` inside the loop (`EventActionExecution.cs:119`), which aborts **every later step of this action**, not just that entry. |
| `[SetSandboxVector3Ds:true]` *(2.74.00)* | `[SandboxVector3Ds:name,{X:0 Y:0 Z:0}]` | Sets sandbox Vector3D variables. |
| `[AddInstanceEventGroup:true]` | `[InstanceEventGroupId:]`, `[InstanceEventGroupReplaceKeys:]`, `[InstanceEventGroupReplaceValues:]` | Instantiates a `[MES Event TemplateGroup]` (§5). |
| `[RemoveThisInstanceGroup:true]` | *(none)* | Marks every event of this instance (same `InstanceId` tag) for removal; runs last in the action. See §5E. |
| `[TryContractSuccess:true]` / `[TryContractFail:true]` | *(none)* | Finish/fail the MES mission contract whose id seeded this event instance, then remove the instance's events like `[RemoveThisInstanceGroup:true]` (§5E-F). **[HARD]** A `[MES Mission]`'s `[EventConditionIds:]` (with `[UseAnyPassingEventCondition:]`) were never read before MES 2.74.04 (`Mission.cs` looped `PlayerConditionIds` instead), so only `[PersistantEventConditionIds:]` gated missions on older builds. |
| `[AddGPSToPlayers:true]` | `[GPSNames:]`, `[GPSDescriptions:]`, `[GPSCoords:]`, `[GPSColors:]`, `[GPSColorVariables:]`, `[UseGPSObjective:true]` | Creating HUD GPS waypoints for players. **[HARD]** `[GPSDescriptions:]` and `[GPSColors:]` were parsed but never applied before MES 2.75.00 (every GPS got the default description and orange); they now apply per index. `[GPSColors:]` (0-255 per channel) wins; if it is empty or zero for that index, `[GPSColorVariables:name]` reads a sandbox Vector3D of that name (the `{}` are optional). **[HARD] Channel order is `{X:Red Y:Blue Z:Green}`**: both code paths assign `color.B = Y` and `color.G = Z`, so `{X:255 Y:0 Z:128}` is orange (R 255, G 128, B 0), not an RGB-ordered vector (reported as MeridiusIX/Modular-Encounters-Systems#413). Descriptions resolve tokens (`IdsReplacer`; with no NpcData in an Event Action only sandbox variables work). The RivalAI Action version also falls back to the grid's custom Vector3D variables for the color. |
| `[RemoveGPSFromPlayers:true]` | `[RemoveGPSNames:]` | Deleting HUD GPS waypoints from players. |
| *None (Self-gated)* | `[DebugChatMessage:<Text>]`, `[DebugHudMessage:<Text>]` | Diagnostic test messages for event development (never use in production). |

| `[CheckPlayerNear:true]` | `[PlayerNearCoords:]`, `[PlayerNearDistanceFromCoords:]`, `[PlayerNearMinDistanceFromCoords:]` | Distance checks from specified coords. |

## 3. The Zero-Stripping Bug & Workarounds

In `TagParse.cs`, MES strips all `0` values from integer lists unless called with `preserveZero: true`:
```csharp
if (!preserveZero)
    result.RemoveAll(item => item == 0);
```

- **[HARD] Affected Tags**:
  - `CustomCountersTargets` in `EventConditions.cs`
  - `CustomSandboxCountersTargets` in `ConditionReferenceProfile.cs`
  - `CustomSandboxCountersTargets` in `SpawnConditionsProfile.cs`
  - `CustomZoneCounterValue` in `ZoneConditionsProfile.cs`
  - `IncreaseCountersAmount` / `DecreaseCountersAmount` in `EventActionReference.cs`
  - `MinPlayerReputation` / `MaxPlayerReputation` in `PlayerConditionProfile.cs` (`[MES Player Condition]`) and `ConditionReferenceProfile.cs` (`[RivalAI Condition]`). `[MaxPlayerReputation:0]` leaves the lists uneven, so the reputation check always fails (logged only as `do not match in count`); use `-1` as the cap. A `[RivalAI Trigger]` reads these tags as single integers, so `0` is safe there.
- **Symptom**: Using `[CustomCountersTargets:0]` strips the `0`, resulting in an empty list. Evaluation fails with `Counter Names and Targets List Counts Don't Match`.
- **Workaround**:
  - To test `< 0` (e.g. floor clamp): Use `[CustomCountersTargets:-1]` with `[CounterCompareTypes:LessOrEqual]`.
  - To test `>= 0` (e.g. positive gate): Use `[CustomCountersTargets:-1]` with `[CounterCompareTypes:Greater]`.

## 4. Dynamic Zones & Progression Ladders (`[MES Zone]`)

Zones define spatial volumes that enforce territory rules, modify spawn pools, and track localized counters:

```xml
<EntityComponent xsi:type="MyObjectBuilder_InventoryComponentDefinition">
  <Id>
    <TypeId>Inventory</TypeId>
    <SubtypeId>ModPrefix-Zone-TerritoryAlpha</SubtypeId>
  </Id>
  <Description>
    [MES Zone]
    [Name:ModPrefix_Zone_Alpha]
    [PublicName:Contested Territory Alpha]
    [Active:true]
    [Persistent:true]
    [Coordinates:{X:62495 Y:28019 Z:37195}]
    [Radius:25000]
  </Description>
</EntityComponent>
```

### Critical Zone Rules & Quirks:
1. **[HARD] `[Type:InsideZone]` vs `[Type:InsideActiveZone]`**:
   - `[Type:InsideZone]` calls `ZoneManager.InsideZoneWithName(..., onlyActive: false)`. It evaluates `true` even when the target zone is deactivated!
   - Always use `[Type:InsideActiveZone]` and `[Type:OutsideActiveZone]`.
2. **[HARD] Zones are looked up by `[PublicName:]`, not `[Name:]`**: every by-name zone lookup compares `zone.PublicName` (`ZoneManager.cs` `InsideZoneWithName`, `ToggleZones`, `ChangeZoneRadius/Counters/Bools`; `SpawnConditions.cs:1926` for Zone Conditions). `[ZoneName:]` (Triggers, RivalAI Actions, Zone Conditions, Player Conditions) and `[ZoneNames:]` (MES Event Actions) must therefore equal the zone's `[PublicName:]`. `[Name:]` is stored but no lookup reads it, and `[ZoneName:]` inside `[MES Zone]` is ignored. `scripts/audit_mes_references.ps1` errors on a reference that matches a zone's `[Name:]` but not its `[PublicName:]`.
3. **Spawn restrictions (overhauled in MES 2.74.00)** — `ZoneManager.GetAllowedSpawns()`, evaluated only for **Active** zones:

   | Restriction | Tags | Applies when | Precedence |
   | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
   | No spawns at all | `[NoSpawnZone:true]` | position inside zone (not gated by `Persistent`) | overrides everything |
   | SpawnGroup whitelist | `[UseAllowedSpawnGroups:true]` + `[AllowedSpawnGroups:]` | see note below | over mod ID and faction |
   | SpawnGroup blacklist | `[UseRestrictedSpawnGroups:true]` + `[RestrictedSpawnGroups:]` | inside zone **and** `[Persistent:true]` | over mod ID and faction |
   | Mod ID white/blacklist | `[UseAllowedModIDs:true]` + `[AllowedModIDs:]` / `[UseRestrictedModIDs:true]` + `[RestrictedModIDs:]` | inside zone **and** `[Persistent:true]` | over faction |
   | Faction white/blacklist | `[UseAllowedFactions:true]` + `[AllowedFactions:]` / `[UseRestrictedFactions:true]` + `[RestrictedFactions:]` | inside zone **and** (`[Persistent:true]` or `[PlayerKnownLocation:true]`) | lowest |

   - **[HARD] `Persistent` still gates most restrictions** (`ZoneManager.cs:287-344`), and `Persistent` defaults to `false`.
   - **[HARD] AllowedSpawnGroups is two rules in one**: with `[UseAllowedSpawnGroups:true]`, every listed SpawnGroup becomes *zone-only* world-wide — it can no longer spawn outside any zone that allows it (`OnlyAllowedZoneSpawns`, collected from every active zone regardless of position). Separately, inside a `Persistent` zone the list restricts spawns to only those groups (collected even without the `Use` gate).
   - The short-lived `[UseLimitedFactions:]` / `[LimitedFactions:]` zone tags from the first 2.74.00 build were renamed to `UseAllowedFactions` / `AllowedFactions` (MES commit e2d53a7) and are no longer parsed.
4. **Multiple spheres per zone** *(2.74.00)*: `[CoordinateRadiusPairs:{X:0 Y:0 Z:0},5000]` (repeatable, one pair per tag) adds extra coordinate/radius spheres to one zone.
5. **Placement & debug helpers**: `/MES.Info.GetLocationMatrix` *(2.74.03)* copies your position/orientation to the clipboard for zone setup; `/MES.Debug.ShowZone.<name>`, `/MES.Debug.HideZone.<name>`, `/MES.Debug.ShowAllZones`, `/MES.Debug.HideAllZones` *(2.74.04)* draw zone spheres in-world (`<name>` is the `PublicName` or zone profile SubtypeId).
6. **[HARD] Zone custom bools/counters (RivalAI Action only; broken before MES 2.74.04)**: gate `[ChangeZoneAtPosition:true]` (grid must be inside the zone) or `[ChangeZoneOnlyByName:true]` (any distance), then `[ZoneCustomBoolChange:true]` + `[ZoneCustomBoolChangeName:]` + `[ZoneCustomBoolChangeValue:]`, and/or `[ZoneCustomCounterChange:true]` + `[ZoneCustomCounterChangeName:]` + `[ZoneCustomCounterChangeAmount:]` + `[ZoneCustomCounterChangeType:Set|Add|Subtract|Multiply|Divide]`, with `[ZoneName:<PublicName>]`. Read back with `[MES Zone Conditions]` `[CheckCustomZoneBools:true]` / `[CheckCustomZoneCounters:true]`.
   - Up to 2.74.03 these actions **did nothing**: `MathTools.LowestCount` always returned `0`, so no value was ever written (also affected the KPL variants below); the `...UseKPL` routing was inverted, and the at-position check skipped zones the grid was *inside*. All fixed in 2.74.04 (MES PR #374).
   - Only `[Persistent:true]` zones are changed, matched by `PublicName` (rule 2).
   - Name/amount/type lists are index-aligned; MES uses the **shortest** list and silently drops extra entries. `ZoneCustomCounterChangeAmount` and `ZoneCustomCounterChangeType` take **one value per tag line** (no comma lists; `[ZoneCustomCounterChangeAmount:5,10]` fails to parse and adds nothing). Names and bool values accept comma lists.
   - `[CheckCustomZoneBools:true]` **fails when the bool was never set** on that zone, even when you check for `false`. Set it explicitly first.
7. **[HARD] Known Player Locations (KPLs)**: temporary zones created by `[CreateKnownPlayerArea:true]` (RivalAI Action, at the NPC's position, owned by the NPC's faction), the `/MES.Debug.CreateKPL.<Faction>.<Radius>.<Minutes>` admin command (duration defaults to 30), or the MES API. `[KnownPlayerAreaRadius:]`, `[KnownPlayerAreaTimer:]` (minutes, or `Day`), `[KnownPlayerAreaMaxSpawns:]`. Target KPL variables with `[ZoneCustomBoolChangeUseKPL:true]` / `[ZoneCustomCounterChangeUseKPL:true]` (matches KPLs of the NPC's own faction; `ZoneName` is not used).
   - **Timer must be > 0** *(2.74.04)*: `[KnownPlayerAreaTimer:]` defaults to `30`; a value of `0` or less now **creates no KPL** (logged under `/MES.SpawnDebug.Zone`: `KnownPlayerLocation Not Created At ...: Duration Must Be Greater Than 0`). Before 2.74.04, `-1` created a KPL with no timer. There is no longer a non-expiring KPL. Player presence inside the KPL resets its timer.
   - **KPLs now survive a server restart** *(2.74.04)*. Before, the startup zone validation deleted every KPL (they have no zone profile), so all KPLs vanished on each load.
   - Overlapping KPLs of the same faction merge into one. Since 2.74.04 the merged KPL keeps both zones' bools (OR) and counters (summed); before, the old values were lost.
   - **Faction lock**: while a player is inside a KPL, only spawn groups of the KPL's faction pass `SpawnConditions.ZoneValidation` there (logged as "not among Allowed Zone Factions"), RivalAI custom spawns (`[SpawnEncounter:true]` Defense waves, helper spawns) included. Overlapping KPLs of different factions allow all of their factions (`ZoneManager.GetAllowedSpawns`). A KPL is always owned by the creating grid's faction; no tag names another faction.
   - **See them**: `/MES.Debug.ShowAllZones` draws a KPL (only one at a time; `diagnostics_and_troubleshooting.md` §2.D).
8. **[HARD] Zones can only be required, never excluded.** `SpawnConditions.ZoneValidation` passes a spawn only when its position is inside an allowed zone; no spawn condition rejects a position for being inside a zone. A zone whitelist also checks where the **player** stands, while planetary installations and drones land kilometres away, so a spawn requested from outside can land inside the zone. To keep encounters out of an area, give their behaviors an `[Type:InsideActiveZone]` trigger for that zone that despawns them.

## 5. MES Event Templates & Instance Event Groups

Templates let one set of event profiles be **stamped out as independent live event instances at runtime**, each with its own replaced values (target coordinates, faction, names). This is how MES missions and multi-stage scripted encounters spawn per-instance event chains. It is **not** a random-selection pool.

### A. Profile Types (verified: `ProfileManager.cs`, `TemplateEventGroup.cs`, `Event.cs`)

| Header | Stored as | Role |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `[MES Event Template]` | raw Description text (`TemplateEventProfiles`) | A full `[MES Event]` profile (cooldowns, `[ConditionIds:]`, `[ActionIds:]`, ...) whose text is token-replaced per instance. |
| `[MES Event Condition Template]` | raw text (`TemplateEventConditions`) | An `[MES Event Condition]` resolved and token-replaced per instance. |
| `[MES Event Action Template]` | raw text (`TemplateEventActionProfiles`) | An `[MES Event Action]` resolved and token-replaced per instance. Same master gates as §2.A. |
| `[MES Event TemplateGroup]` | `TemplateEventGroup` | Lists event templates with `[TemplateEventIds:<SubtypeId>]`, **one per tag line** (parsed with `TagStringCheck`, so a comma list becomes one bad id). |

### B. Instantiation
- **Trigger it** with `[AddInstanceEventGroup:true]` + `[InstanceEventGroupId:<TemplateGroup SubtypeId>]` + `[InstanceEventGroupReplaceKeys:{Key1},{Key2}]` + `[InstanceEventGroupReplaceValues:v1,v2]` on a `[MES Event Action]` or a RivalAI Action (RivalAI resolves its own tokens in the values first), or through a `[MES Mission]`'s `[InstanceEventGroupId:]`.
- **[HARD] Every template in the group is instantiated**, not one at random (`AddEventsAsInsertible` loops all `EventIds`). Each becomes an `Event` with SubtypeId `<template>@<InstanceId>`; unknown template ids are skipped silently.
- **[HARD] Token replacement**: the template text, and every condition/action template it references by `[ConditionIds:]`/`[PersistantConditionIds:]`/`[ActionIds:]`, is run through `IdsReplacer.ReplaceText()` with the replace keys plus an automatic `{InstanceId}` (game-time ticks, or the mission's id). Referenced ids that are **not** templates fall back to the normal shared `[MES Event Condition]`/`[MES Event Action]` profiles, un-replaced.
- Lookup of the group happens when the action runs, so load order between these profiles does not matter.
- Instanced events are saved with the world (`Event.Insertable`, `ReplaceKeys`/`ReplaceValues` are ProtoMembers).

### C. Minimal Example

```xml
<!-- Instantiates the group (referenced from an [MES Event] via [ActionIds:]) -->
<EntityComponent xsi:type="MyObjectBuilder_InventoryComponentDefinition">
  <Id><TypeId>Inventory</TypeId><SubtypeId>GVK-EventAction-StartRaid</SubtypeId></Id>
  <Description>
    [MES Event Action]
    [AddInstanceEventGroup:true]
    [InstanceEventGroupId:GVK-TemplateGroup-Raid]
    [InstanceEventGroupReplaceKeys:{RaidSpawn}]
    [InstanceEventGroupReplaceValues:GVK-Spawn-ScoutRaid]
  </Description>
</EntityComponent>

<!-- The group: one [TemplateEventIds:] line per event template -->
<EntityComponent xsi:type="MyObjectBuilder_InventoryComponentDefinition">
  <Id><TypeId>Inventory</TypeId><SubtypeId>GVK-TemplateGroup-Raid</SubtypeId></Id>
  <Description>
    [MES Event TemplateGroup]
    [TemplateEventIds:GVK-EventTemplate-Raid]
  </Description>
</EntityComponent>

<!-- The event template: a normal [MES Event] body, token-replaced per instance -->
<EntityComponent xsi:type="MyObjectBuilder_InventoryComponentDefinition">
  <Id><TypeId>Inventory</TypeId><SubtypeId>GVK-EventTemplate-Raid</SubtypeId></Id>
  <Description>
    [MES Event Template]
    [UseEvent:true]
    [UniqueEvent:true]
    [MinCooldownMs:60000]
    [MaxCooldownMs:60000]
    [ActionIds:GVK-EventActionTemplate-Raid]
  </Description>
</EntityComponent>

<!-- The action template: {RaidSpawn} is replaced for this instance -->
<EntityComponent xsi:type="MyObjectBuilder_InventoryComponentDefinition">
  <Id><TypeId>Inventory</TypeId><SubtypeId>GVK-EventActionTemplate-Raid</SubtypeId></Id>
  <Description>
    [MES Event Action Template]
    [SpawnEncounter:true]
    [SpawnData:{RaidSpawn}]
    [SpawnCoords:{X:0 Y:0 Z:0}]
    [SpawnFactionTags:SPRT]
  </Description>
</EntityComponent>
```

### D. Contract Blocks (RivalAI Action)
- **[HARD]** `[ApplyContractProfiles:true]` + `[ContractBlocks:<block CustomName>]` + `[ContractBlockProfiles:<[MES Contract Block] SubtypeId>]` exist only on RivalAI Actions. `[ContractProfiles:]` is an alias of `[ContractBlockProfiles:]`.
- **[HARD] Pairing trap**: `[ContractBlocks:]` and `[ContractBlockProfiles:]` are two separate lists **paired by index**, and `ActionSystem.cs` loops only to the **shorter** list. Two `[ContractBlocks:]` lines with one `[ContractBlockProfiles:]` line fill only the first board and nothing is logged. To fill two boards, write two of each in the same order, even when both boards use the same profile:
  ```
  [ApplyContractProfiles:true]
  [ContractBlocks:Contracts North]
  [ContractBlocks:Contracts South]
  [ContractBlockProfiles:ModPrefix-ContractBoard-Escort]
  [ContractBlockProfiles:ModPrefix-ContractBoard-Escort]
  ```
  Both tags drop blank entries at parse time, so an empty slot shifts every later pair; a pair whose profile id isn't registered is skipped (only logged under `/MES.BehaviorDebug.Action.true`: `Couldn't find Mission Profile With Name`).
- **[HARD] Matching**: a name must equal the block's `CustomName` exactly (case-sensitive), and only blocks on the grid that runs the behavior count (`CurrentGrid.Contracts`; not linked subgrids). Each name matches every contract block with that name.
- **[HARD] `[ClearContractContentsFirst:true]` runs per pair** (`ContractBlockProfile.ApplyProfileToBlock` → `InGameContractManager.ClearBlockContracts`) and removes the block's generated, not-yet-accepted contracts. Two pairs that target the same block name therefore clear each other's missions: the second pair wipes what the first just added. Put every mission for one board in one `[MES Contract Block]` profile's `[MissionIds:]` instead.

### E. Relationship Model, Lifecycle & Limits [HARD]
Verified: `Event.cs`, `TemplateEventGroup.cs`, `EventManager.cs`, `EventActionExecution.cs`, `Mission/*.cs`, `IdsReplacer.cs`.

```text
[MES Event]               static: ONE shared Event per profile, created at world load, id = its SubtypeId
[MES Event Template]      stamped: ONE Event per instantiation, id = <template>@<InstanceId>
[MES Event TemplateGroup] bundle: instantiates EVERY listed template in one call, all sharing one InstanceId
   condition/action ids on a stamped event:
     id is a [... Condition Template]/[... Action Template]  -> stamped per instance (<id>@<InstanceId>), text token-replaced
     id is a plain [MES Event Condition]/[MES Event Action]  -> the shared profile, NOT replaced (no tokens resolve)
```

- **Same tags everywhere.** A template is parsed by the same `InitTags` as its non-template twin (`EventProfile`, `EventCondition`, `EventActionReferenceProfile`/`EventActionProfile`), after `string.Replace`. Event-only, template-only and shared tag sets are therefore identical; the only template-specific thing is that `{Key}` text is replaced first. `{Key}` stays literal in non-template profiles. `[MES Event TemplateGroup]` reads only `[TemplateEventIds:]`.
- **Each instance joins the event-tag pool** with its `[Tags:]` plus its `InstanceId` as an extra tag (`Event.Profile`), which is how `RemoveThisInstanceGroup` finds its siblings.
- **Who can start a group**: `[AddInstanceEventGroup:true]` on an `[MES Event Action]`; the same tag on a `[RivalAI Action]` (the values pass through `IdsReplacer` with the Remote Control position, the keys do not); a `[MES Mission]` when its contract is **accepted** (`Contract.TryToActivateCustomContract` → `Mission.Start`, not when the contract is generated); and the `InsertInstanceEventGroup` mod API. An unknown group id silently does nothing.
- **Ids**: `AddEventsAsInsertible` uses `GameDateTime.Ticks` as `{InstanceId}` when no id is passed (event action, RivalAI action, API), one id per call. Two instantiations in the same game tick therefore get the same id: duplicate `<template>@<id>` events that share a tag and are removed together. A `[MES Mission]` passes the Keen contract id instead.
- **Persistence**: instances live in the same `EventsList` and save as `MES-EventsList`, with `Insertable`, `ReplaceKeys`, `ReplaceValues`, `InstanceId`, `TemplateProfileSubtype` and `MarkedforRemoval` stored.
  - On load `Event.Init()` rebuilds each instance from the **current** template text plus the saved keys/values: editing a template changes live instances at the next load (run count and cooldown are kept).
  - Deleting a template leaves its instances in the save, invalid (`ErrorOnSetup`) and silently skipped every pass. The load-time cleanup ("Delete Old Events") skips every `Insertable` event, so nothing ever removes them.
- **Nothing ends an instance by itself.** `[UniqueEvent:true]` only stops further runs; the event stays in the list and the save. Remove one with `[RemoveThisInstanceGroup:true]` or `[TryContractSuccess:true]`/`[TryContractFail:true]` on an `[MES Event Action]` (they run last in the action and mark every event tagged with this `InstanceId` as `MarkedforRemoval`; `EventManager.ProcessEvents` drops them on its next 30-tick pass).
  - **Hazard**: those removal loops read `Event.Profile.Tags` with no null check, and `Profile` is `null` for an orphaned instance, so after a template is deleted they throw on reaching it and the action stops partway. Remove instances before deleting the template. *(Read from source, not reproduced in play; reported as MeridiusIX/Modular-Encounters-Systems#415.)*
- **No instance cap.** Nothing limits how many exist. Every live instance is evaluated on each 30-tick `ProcessEvents` pass, and each stamped action registers `ProfileManager.EventActionReferenceProfiles["<action>@<id>"]`, which is never removed during the session. Long-lived servers should end finished instances.
- **Replace keys** (`IdsReplacer.ReplaceText`): plain `string.Replace` in list order, then the automatic `{InstanceId}` last.
  - A value that contains a later key's text is replaced again (cascade), so keep values free of `{...}` text. A user-supplied `{InstanceId}` key wins, because it runs first.
  - Key and value counts must match. On a mismatch MES shows a "Big error" chat message, copies the text to the clipboard, and **still creates the instance with the unreplaced `{Key}` text**.
  - `[InstanceEventGroupReplaceKeys:]`/`[InstanceEventGroupReplaceValues:]` are comma-split lists with **no escaping**: a comma inside a value splits it and trips the count mismatch. A `[MES Mission]` avoids this: its `[ReplaceKeys:]`/`[ReplaceValues:]` take one entry per tag line and keep commas (`[ReplacePairs:]` is a third form).

### F. `[MES Mission]` vs a Plain `AddInstanceEventGroup` [HARD]
A mission is an instance group plus a Keen custom contract (`MissionProfile.cs`, `Mission.cs`, `InGameContractManager.cs`):
- **Id source**: the Keen contract id becomes `{InstanceId}` (and `{ContractId}`, `MissionType:Custom` only) instead of game-time ticks, so `[TryContractSuccess:true]`/`[TryContractFail:true]` can finish the right contract.
- **Contract type**: `[ContractSubtypeId:]` *(2.75.00, default `MESContract`)* names the `MyObjectBuilder_ContractTypeDefinition` that a `MissionType:Custom` contract uses; before, it was hard-coded. The definition must exist in the game or the contract cannot be created.
- **Timing**: the contract is generated when `[ApplyContractProfiles:true]` stocks the board, and only if `[EventConditionIds:]`/`[PersistantEventConditionIds:]` pass then and the profile's `[ReplaceKeys:]`/`[ReplaceValues:]` counts match. The values go through `IdsReplacer` with the stocking grid's NpcData, so `{Faction}`, `{SpawnGroupName}` and custom strings resolve there. The event group is stamped only when a player **accepts**, after the event conditions are re-checked (`Contract no longer available` if they fail), then `[LeadPlayerConditionIds:]` and `[PlayerConditionIds:]` (a failed player check puts the contract back on the board).
- **Hooks into Keen's contract events**: an instance event tagged `Failed@{InstanceId}` or `Abandoned@{InstanceId}` has its actions run (conditions, cooldown and enabled state are bypassed) when that contract fails or is abandoned. A finished contract pays `[ReputationReward:]` and sets the `[ActivateBooleanNameOnSucces:]` sandbox boolean; an abandoned one charges `[FailReputationPrice:]`.
- **Cleanup is not automatic.** On finish, fail or abandon MES does **not** remove the mission's instance events. The template must end itself with `[RemoveThisInstanceGroup:true]` or `[TryContract*]`; otherwise the events live on in the save.
- **`[Exclusive:true]`**: accepting one contract of the mission removes the mission's other generated contracts on every board, and the mission is not added to a board while one accepted contract is still active.

## 1. Manipulation Profile Architecture (`[MES Manipulation]`)

Manipulation profiles modify NPC grids at the moment of spawning, before physics or AI initialize. Attach them to a spawn group with `[ManipulationProfiles:]` (or `[ManipulationGroups:]`); tags written directly in the `[Modular Encounters SpawnGroup]` Description are also parsed as its first Manipulation profile.

```xml
<EntityComponent xsi:type="MyObjectBuilder_InventoryComponentDefinition">
  <Id>
    <TypeId>Inventory</TypeId>
    <SubtypeId>ModPrefix-Manipulation-Standard</SubtypeId>
  </Id>
  <Description>
    [MES Manipulation]
    [UseBlockReplacerProfile:true]
    [BlockReplacerProfileNames:ModPrefix-BlockReplacement-Military]
    [RandomizeWeapons:true]
    [WeaponRandomizerTargetWhitelist:LargeGatlingTurret]
    [UseGridDereliction:true]
    [DerelictionProfiles:ModPrefix-Dereliction-Wreck]
    [ClearGridInventories:true]
  </Description>
</EntityComponent>
```

### Key Manipulation Capabilities:
- **Block Replacer**: `[UseBlockReplacer:true]` + `[ReplaceBlockOld:]`/`[ReplaceBlockNew:]` pairs (or `[ReplaceBlockReference:]`), or `[UseBlockReplacerProfile:true]` + `[BlockReplacerProfileNames:]` pointing at `[MES Block Replacement]` profiles. `[ConvertToHeavyArmor:true]` is a built-in replacement set.
  - **[HARD]** A replacement is skipped unless both blocks have the same `Size`, unless `[RelaxReplacedBlocksSize:true]` (`BlockReplacement.cs:90`). Profiles run in the order listed, so once one profile has replaced a block, a later profile matching the old subtype never sees it.
- **[HARD] RivalAI block:** with `[UseRivalAi:true]` + `[RivalAiReplaceRemoteControl:true]`, MES turns the grid's main (or first) Remote Control into a RivalAI control module (`BehaviorBuilder.cs:74-90`). Block replacement runs first (`PrefabManipulation.cs:374` before `:518`), so a replacer that turns a cockpit seat or AI block into `RivalAIRemoteControlLarge` also works. A grid with neither gets **no behavior** ("Following Behavior Could Not Be Applied"), silently.
  - **[HARD] Both tags must be in the same manipulation profile.** Each profile runs `RivalAiInitialize` on its own, and only `[RivalAiReplaceRemoteControl:true]` assigns the remote that receives the behavior; `[UseRivalAi:true]` alone writes it to no remote, not even an existing `RivalAIRemoteControlLarge`. Without a RivalAI behavior set, MES hands the `<Behaviour>` name to Keen's drone AI (`NpcData.cs` `SetDroneBehaviourFull`), which is the right path for a vanilla remote with a Keen drone behavior. `[ManipulationProfiles:MES-Manipulation-RivalAi]` (shipped with MES) sets both.
  - **[HARD] `[ConvertAllRemoteControlBlocks:true]` and vanilla remotes:** on master after 2.75.02 (`8d5a36d`, PR #442) it matches the vanilla `LargeBlockRemoteControl`/`SmallBlockRemoteControl` subtypes and converts them. Up to 2.75.02 it matched `RemoteControlLarge`/`RemoteControlSmall`, so it never converted vanilla remotes (`BehaviorBuilder.cs:30`).
  - `audit_mes_references.ps1` (Pass 4c) warns on a RivalAI `<Behaviour>` without both tags, a prefab with no (named) remote, and a behavior baked into a vanilla remote's CustomData (MES only starts behaviors on RivalAI control modules). Warnings only: vanilla setups are legal.
- **Weapon Randomizer**: `[RandomizeWeapons:true]` (§2).
- **Dereliction**: `[UseGridDereliction:true]` + `[DerelictionProfiles:]` (§3). Without the gate, `PrefabManipulation.cs:672` skips dereliction entirely.
- **Inventory Control**: `[ClearGridInventories:true]`, ContainerType assignment (§6). Ammo/fuel top-up is a spawn-group feature (§5).
- **Hull Cosmetics**: `[RecolorGrid:true]` + `[ColorReferencePairs:]` (or `[RecolorOld:]`/`[RecolorNew:]`), `[ShiftBlockColorsHue:true]`, `[AssignGridSkin:]`, `[SkinRandomBlocks:true]` + `[SkinRandomBlocksTextures:]` + `[MinPercentageSkinRandomBlocks:]`/`[MaxPercentageSkinRandomBlocks:]`, `[ReskinTarget:]`/`[ReskinTexture:]`.
  - **[HARD] Color matching** (master after 2.75.02, `9909489`, PR #457): `RecolorOld`/`ReskinTarget` in the manipulation and `OldBlockColors` in the action treat a block as a match when each of its three `ColorMaskHSV` numbers is within 0.001 of the given color, so 3-decimal values and the color menu's one-decimal H/S/V (hue in degrees, the others in percent, converted to the stored 0-1 and -1 to 1 ranges) match. Up to 2.75.02 the manipulation needed every digit equal to the prefab's, and the action rounded both colors to 3 decimals, which still missed values like a stored hue of 0.152777776 typed as 0.152.
  - **[HARD] `RecolorGrid` after part of the grid breaks off** (`GridSystem.RecolorBlocks`, master after 2.75.02, `4ba8c67`, PR #456): an invalid block is now removed from `AllBlocks`, the list the loop walks. Up to 2.75.02 it was removed from `AllTerminalBlocks`, which could throw or drop the wrong terminal block.
- **Thrust Restrictions**: `[ConfigureSpecialNpcThrusters:true]` with `[RestrictNpcIonThrust:]` / `[RestrictNpcAtmoThrust:]` / `[RestrictNpcHydroThrust:]` and per-type `ThrustForceMultiply` / `ThrustPowerMultiply` tags (e.g. `[NpcAtmoThrustForceMultiply:]`). MES has no thruster-type conversion tag.

## 2. Weapon Randomizer & Public Block Constraints

MES includes an automated weapon replacement pipeline that dynamically upgrades or randomizes turret and fixed-weapon arsenals:

- `[RandomizeWeapons:true]`: Master switch.
- `[WeaponRandomizerTargetWhitelist:<SubtypeId or TypeId/SubtypeId>]` / `[WeaponRandomizerTargetBlacklist:...]`: Which weapon blocks on the prefab may be replaced (`WeaponRandomizer.cs:969` matches either form).
- `[WeaponRandomizerWhitelist:...]` / `[WeaponRandomizerBlacklist:...]`: Which weapons may be installed as replacements.
- `[RandomWeaponChance:<int>]`, `[RandomWeaponSizeVariance:<int>]`, `[NonRandomWeaponNames:]` / `[NonRandomWeaponIds:]`.

### The `<Public>true</Public>` Requirement & Block Restrictions:
> [!CAUTION]
> **[HARD] Public Definition Gate**: In `WeaponRandomizer.cs` (lines 182–194), MES iterates block definitions in the game database and checks `if (!definition.Public)`.
> If a block definition has `<Public>false</Public>` in its SBC definition (common when modders try to hide `_NPC` weapon variants from players natively), MES **skips it** unless:
> 1. A `[MES Weapon Mod Rules]` profile specifies `[AllowIfNonPublic:true]`.
> 2. Or the SubtypeId is in `DefaultPublicBlocks`.
> Custom NPC weapons must have `<Public>true</Public>` in their SBC definition or an explicit weapon mod rule.
>
> **Block Restrictions Mod Interaction**: If you use the Block Restrictions mod to restrict `_NPC` weapons to NPCs only, author the weapon blocks with `<Public>true</Public>` in SBC as normal. Block Restrictions dynamically hides them from player G-menus/toolbars on the client and strips them from player grids server-side, leaving `definition.Public` true so MES `WeaponRandomizer` can discover and randomize them without needing weapon mod rule overrides.

## 3. Dereliction & Damaged Block Rendering (`[MES Dereliction]`)

Dereliction transforms clean prefabs into battle-damaged, smoking, sparking ruins. Reference it from a Manipulation profile with `[UseGridDereliction:true]` + `[DerelictionProfiles:]`.

```xml
<EntityComponent xsi:type="MyObjectBuilder_InventoryComponentDefinition">
  <Id>
    <TypeId>Inventory</TypeId>
    <SubtypeId>ModPrefix-Dereliction-Wreck</SubtypeId>
  </Id>
  <Description>
    [MES Dereliction]
    [Blocks:MyObjectBuilder_CubeBlock/LargeBlockArmorBlock]
    [Blocks:MyObjectBuilder_CubeBlock/LargeBlockArmorSlope]
    [Chance:40]
    [UseSeparatePercentages:true]
    [MinIntegrityPercentage:20]
    [MaxIntegrityPercentage:65]
    [MinBuildPercentage:10]
    [MaxBuildPercentage:45]
  </Description>
</EntityComponent>
```

- **[HARD] `[Blocks:]` is required**: `DerelictionProfile.ProcessBlock()` (line 144) returns immediately for any block not in the `[Blocks:]` list. With `[MatchOnlyTypeId:true]`, a listed block's TypeId matches every subtype of that type. A profile without `[Blocks:]` does nothing.
- `[Chance:<0-100>]`: Per-block roll (default `100`).

### The Separate Percentages Rule:
> [!CAUTION]
> **[HARD] The Scaffolding Trap**: In `DerelictionProfile.cs` (lines 171–188), if `[UseSeparatePercentages:true]` is omitted (it defaults to `false`), MES rolls one value from `[MinPercentage:]`/`[MaxPercentage:]` and sets:
> `build = value; integrity = value;`
> In the Space Engineers engine, when `BuildPercentage == IntegrityPercentage`, a block renders as an **unfinished construction skeleton** rather than a damaged/smoking block!
> Furthermore, `MinIntegrityPercentage`, `MaxIntegrityPercentage`, `MinBuildPercentage`, and `MaxBuildPercentage` are completely ignored unless `[UseSeparatePercentages:true]` is explicitly declared.

## 5. Replenishment (`[ReplenishSystems:]` + `[MES Replenishment]`)

Replenishment is a **spawn-group** feature: with `[ReplenishSystems:true]` in the `[Modular Encounters SpawnGroup]` Description, MES fills ammo, fuel and similar system inventories when the grid spawns (`NpcData.cs:762` → `InventoryHelper.ReplenishGridSystems`). `[ReplenishProfiles:]` (also on the spawn group) points at `[MES Replenishment]` profiles that cap or exclude items:

```xml
<EntityComponent xsi:type="MyObjectBuilder_InventoryComponentDefinition">
  <Id>
    <TypeId>Inventory</TypeId>
    <SubtypeId>ModPrefix-Replenish-Ammunition</SubtypeId>
  </Id>
  <Description>
    [MES Replenishment]
    [MaxItemId:MyObjectBuilder_AmmoMagazine/NATO_25x184mm]
    [MaxItemAmount:100]
    [RestrictedItems:MyObjectBuilder_AmmoMagazine/LargeRailgunAmmo]
  </Description>
</EntityComponent>
```

- `[MaxItemId:]` / `[MaxItemAmount:]` are paired lists (index-matched; extra entries are dropped).
- `[IgnoreGlobalReplenishProfiles:true]` on the spawn group skips server-wide profiles.
- **[HARD] Gas tanks (MES 2.75.00, commit `c6ced3e`)**: the `InfiniteTank` block logic refills an NPC-owned hydrogen/oxygen tank to 100% whenever it falls to 25% (checked every 100 ticks). Through 2.74.05 it ran only on cargo-ship grids. Now it runs on any linked grid with NpcData whose `ReplenishSystems` attribute is set, and switches itself off for grids without it. The attribute comes from `[ReplenishSystems:true]` on the spawn group and is also forced on by spawn-time weapon randomization (`PrefabManipulation.cs`). **Fails as**: an encounter with `[ReplenishSystems:false]` and no randomizer now runs its tanks dry, where a cargo ship on 2.74.05 never did. Intended: the 2.75.00 patch notes say tank replenishment now requires `[ReplenishSystems:true]` in the SpawnGroup, so set it on every encounter that must not run out of H2.
- Runtime top-up during combat is a different mechanism: `[UseAmmoReplenish:true]` + `[AmmoReplenishClipAmount:]` + `[MaxAmmoReplenishments:]` in `[RivalAI Weapons]`.
