## 6. ContainerTypes, Loot Tables & Inventory Injections

ContainerTypes bridge vanilla Space Engineers inventory generation with MES spawning and RivalAI runtime actions.

### A. Vanilla Foundation (`ContainerTypes.sbc`)
In Space Engineers, loot tables are defined in `<TypeId>ContainerTypeDefinition</TypeId>` inside `ContainerTypes.sbc`:

```xml
<Definitions xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema">
  <ContainerTypes>
    <ContainerType CountMin="3" CountMax="4">
      <Id>
        <TypeId>ContainerTypeDefinition</TypeId>
        <SubtypeId>PersonalContainerSmall</SubtypeId>
      </Id>
      <Items>
        <Item AmountMin="1" AmountMax="5">
          <Frequency>1.0</Frequency>
          <Id>
            <TypeId>Ingot</TypeId>
            <SubtypeId>Uranium</SubtypeId>
          </Id>
        </Item>
        <Item AmountMin="1" AmountMax="10">
          <Frequency>1.0</Frequency>
          <Id>
            <TypeId>Ingot</TypeId>
            <SubtypeId>GVK_CUs</SubtypeId>
          </Id>
        </Item>
        <Item AmountMin="1" AmountMax="2">
          <Frequency>0.2</Frequency>
          <Id>
            <TypeId>Component</TypeId>
            <SubtypeId>GVK_TurboEncabulator</SubtypeId>
          </Id>
        </Item>
      </Items>
    </ContainerType>
  </ContainerTypes>
</Definitions>
```

- **`CountMin` / `CountMax`**: Governs how many distinct item types from `<Items>` are rolled for the inventory.
- **`<Frequency>`**: Relative probability weight for an item to be selected.
- **`<AmountMin>` / `<AmountMax>`**: Quantity rolled once an item is selected.
- **GVK Production Pattern**: Overriding vanilla subtypes like `PersonalContainerSmall` (used across Keen prefabs and drop pods) allows injecting server progression items (e.g. Uranium, CUs, RUs, Tech components) globally without editing dozens of prefab blueprints.

### B. MES Spawning Manipulation (`[MES Manipulation]`)
Manipulation profiles modify prefab inventories at spawn:

```xml
<EntityComponent xsi:type="MyObjectBuilder_InventoryComponentDefinition">
  <Id>
    <TypeId>Inventory</TypeId>
    <SubtypeId>ModPrefix-Manipulation-LootSetup</SubtypeId>
  </Id>
  <Description>
    [MES Manipulation]
    [ClearExistingContainerTypes:true]
    [AssignContainerTypesToAllCargo:PersonalContainerSmall]
    [UseContainerTypeAssignment:true]
    [ContainerTypeAssignBlockName:Cargo-Valuable]
    [ContainerTypeAssignSubtypeId:HighTierMilitaryLoot]
  </Description>
</EntityComponent>
```

- **`[AssignContainerTypesToAllCargo:<ContainerTypeId>]`**: Replaces the container type on all cargo blocks across the grid (randomly selects if multiple are listed). Automatically ignores decorative DLC lockers.
- **`[UseContainerTypeAssignment:true]`**: **Master Gate** for selective assignment.
- **`[ContainerTypeAssignBlockName:<TerminalName>]`** + **`[ContainerTypeAssignSubtypeId:<ContainerTypeId>]`**: Paired lists mapping block names to specific loot tables.
- **`[ContainerTypeAssignmentReference:BlockName|ContainerTypeId,BlockName2|ContainerTypeId2]`**: Dictionary syntax alternative (`TagParse.TagStringDictionaryCheck`: comma-separated `key|value` pairs). **[HARD]** Every entry needs a `|` (a bare name throws `IndexOutOfRangeException`), and the duplicate check tests the *value* instead of the key, so listing the same block name twice throws on `Dictionary.Add`.
- **`[ClearExistingContainerTypes:true]`**: Flushes pre-existing container types before applying new ones.

> [!CAUTION]
> **[HARD] Silent Failure on List Count Mismatch**: In `ManipulationProfile.cs:1566`, MES checks `this.ContainerTypeAssignBlockName.Count == this.ContainerTypeAssignSubtypeId.Count`. If the counts differ, MES **silently drops all assignments** without error or warning.

### C. Non-Cargo Block Support (`MesContainerTypeKey`)
> [!NOTE]
> **Vanilla Limitation Solved**: In vanilla SE, only `IMyCargoContainer` blocks support `ContainerType`. Cockpits, lockers, cryo pods, and assemblers ignore it.
> **MES Engine Solution**: MES uses internal mod storage (`StorageTools.MesContainerTypeKey`) to assign container types to *any* block with an inventory. During spawn (`InventoryHelper.ApplyContainerTypes()`), MES generates content for all non-cargo blocks carrying this storage key.

### D. MES Loot Profiles (`[MES Loot]`)
```xml
<EntityComponent xsi:type="MyObjectBuilder_InventoryComponentDefinition">
  <Id>
    <TypeId>Inventory</TypeId>
    <SubtypeId>ModPrefix-Loot-WreckSupplies</SubtypeId>
  </Id>
  <Description>
    [MES Loot]
    [ContainerTypes:PersonalContainerSmall]
    [ContainerBlockTypes:MyObjectBuilder_CargoContainer/SmallBlockSmallContainer]
    [MinBlocks:1]
    [MaxBlocks:3]
    [AppendNameToBlock:true]
    [AppendedName: [Loot]]
  </Description>
</EntityComponent>
```

- `[ContainerTypes:<SubtypeId>]`: Assigns loot tables to matching container blocks.
- `[MinBlocks:<int>]` / `[MaxBlocks:<int>]`: Limits the number of containers receiving loot.
- `[AppendNameToBlock:true]` + `[AppendedName:<string>]`: Appends a suffix to the block custom name for HUD/terminal visibility.

> [!WARNING]
> **[KNOWN BUG] Terminal Name Suffix Failure**: In current MES builds, `[AppendNameToBlock:true]` often fails to update the block's custom name in the terminal. The loot is correctly inserted into the inventory, but the visual name suffix (e.g. ` [Loot]`) is not always applied to the block. This is a known engine/MES bug to be aware of when testing.

### E. Runtime Dynamic Loot Swapping (`[RivalAI Action]`)
RivalAI can dynamically swap container loot tables via triggers during combat or encounter progression:

```xml
<EntityComponent xsi:type="MyObjectBuilder_InventoryComponentDefinition">
  <Id>
    <TypeId>Inventory</TypeId>
    <SubtypeId>ModPrefix-Action-UnlockVaultLoot</SubtypeId>
  </Id>
  <Description>
    [MES AI Action]
    [ApplyContainerTypeToInventoryBlock:true]
    [ContainerTypeBlockNames:Vault-Safe]
    [ContainerTypeSubtypeIds:HighTierTechLoot]
  </Description>
</EntityComponent>
```

- **`[ApplyContainerTypeToInventoryBlock:true]`**: **Master Gate** for runtime container type changes.
- **`[ContainerTypeBlockNames:<TerminalName>]`** + **`[ContainerTypeSubtypeIds:<ContainerTypeId>]`**: Paired lists targeting inventory blocks when triggers execute.

Profile Definitions & Header Syntax Every profile must be defined inside an `` block with a single `` and its configuration declared inside ``. ### A. Behavior Profiles - **Header**: `[RivalAI Behavior]` or `[MES AI Behavior]` - **Key Tags**: - `[BehaviorName:]`: `CoreBehavior`, `Passive`, `CargoShip`, `Escort`, `Fighter`, `HorseFighter`, `Horsefly`, `Hunter`, `Nautical`, `NauticalRoutes`, `Patrol`, `Scout`, `Sniper`, `Strike`, `Vulture` (`BehaviorManager.cs` / `ProfileManager.cs`). `FighterPlane` and `HorseNautical` are reachable only at runtime via `[ChangeBehaviorSubclass:true]` + `[NewBehaviorSubclass:]`. - `[AutopilotData:]`: Reference to `[RivalAI Autopilot]`. - `[TargetData:]`: Reference to `[RivalAI Target]`. - `[WeaponSystem:]` (alias `[WeaponsSystem:]`): Reference to `[RivalAI Weapons]`. - `[Triggers:]`: Direct trigger references. **[HARD] One SubtypeId per tag**: repeat the tag for each trigger (`[Triggers:A]` `[Triggers:B]`). `[Triggers:A,B]` is read as a single name `A,B` (`TagParse.TagStringCheck`, no comma split), so neither loads (`BehaviorSetup` log: `Could Not Add Trigger Profile To Behavior`). Same inside a `[RivalAI TriggerGroup]`. - `[TriggerGroups:]`: Trigger group references, also one per tag. - `[RemoteControlCode:]`: Custom identifier tag for grid targeting and commands. - `[UseRetreatTimer:bool]`, `[UseNoTargetTimer:bool]`, `[UsePlayerDistanceTimer:bool]`: Despawn timer gates (`DespawnSystem.cs`; `UsePlayerDistanceTimer` defaults to `true` — 150 s beyond 25 km from any player despawns the grid). ### B. Trigger Profiles - **Header**: `[RivalAI Trigger]` or `[MES AI Trigger]` - **Required Gate**: `[UseTrigger:true]` (Omission causes the trigger to never fire). - **Key Tags**: - `[Type:]`: - `Timer`: Periodic time check via `MinCooldownMs` and `MaxCooldownMs`. - `PlayerNear`: Fires when a player enters `TargetDistance`. - `TargetNear` / `TargetFar`: Fires based on distance to target grid. - `Damage`: Fires when the grid takes damage of a listed type. **[HARD] Needs `[DamageTypes:Any]`** (or specific type names): the list starts empty and the check is `DamageTypes.Contains(type) || DamageTypes.Contains("Any")` (`TriggerSystem.cs:572`), so without it the trigger never fires. `[ExcludedDamageTypes:]` filters types out. - `Compromised`: **[HARD]** Fires when the behavior's Remote Control stops working (no power, damaged, turned off) or is removed, after it had worked, on a grid that was NPC-owned and is not being closed (`CoreBehavior.RemoteCompromiseCheck`). It is checked only when the remote's working state changes. On MES `master` after 2.75.03 (`64476e8`, not released) a remote that stops working while the game's EMP disrupts the grid's power counts as still working, so an EMP alone no longer fires it (`/MES.IGGB`: `Block EMPd`). Read in code, not tested: since nothing re-checks the remote when the EMP ends, a remote that also loses its power for real during the EMP seems to stay "working", and `Compromised` never fires. - `CommandReceived`: Fires on receiving a broadcast code (`CommandReceiveCode`). - `BehaviorTriggerA`–`G`: Triggered internally by AI behaviors (e.g. waypoint arrival, strike breakaway). - `Session`: Fires once per game session/load. - `ButtonPress`: Fires from a button panel on **this** grid (`[ButtonPanelName:]` supports variables since MES 2.74.00; buttons on other grids no longer fire it since MES 2.74.03). - `HealthPercentage`: **[HARD]** fires while grid integrity is **at or above** `[PercentageOfHealthRemaining:]` (`TriggerChecks.cs:386` uses `>=`), not when it drops below. For "below X%", use a `Damage` trigger with a Condition `[CheckHealthPercentage:true]` + `[MaxPercentageOfHealthRemaining:X]`. - `Despawn` / `DespawnMES`: fire when this grid is removed. `Despawn` is the behavior's own despawn; `DespawnMES` covers every MES removal but only runs when `[DespawnTypeFromSpawner:]` is `Any` or an exact source string (`behaviors_and_autopilot.md` §9). - `PaymentSuccess` / `PaymentFailure`: Fire after a `[ChangePlayerCredits:true]` / `[ChangeNpcFactionCredits:true]` action. - Also: `AcquiredTarget`, `ChangedTarget`, `SwitchedTarget`, `LostTarget`, `HasTarget`, `NoTarget`, `NoWeapon`, `TurretTarget`, `TargetInSafezone`, `PlayerFar`, `PlayerKnownLocation`, `Position`, `WaypointNear`/`WaypointFar` (see crash note in `diagnostics_and_troubleshooting.md` §4.4), `InsideActiveZone`/`OutsideActiveZone` (and the non-Active variants), `HealthPercentage`, `ActiveWeaponsPercentage`/`ActiveGunsPercentage`/`ActiveTurretsPercentage`, `SensorActive`/`SensorIdle`, `JumpRequested`/`JumpCompleted`, `Weather`, `Retreat`, `Despawn`/`DespawnNear`/`DespawnFar`/`DespawnMES`. - `Manual` (convention): MES has no check for this value, so the trigger never fires on its own — only `[ManuallyActivateTrigger:true]` + `[ManuallyActivatedTriggerNames:]`/`[ManuallyActivatedTriggerTags:]` fires it (that path ignores `Type` entirely, §6). Any other unrecognized `Type` value behaves the same way, silently. - `[StartsReady:bool]`: If `true`, fires immediately on spawn without waiting for initial cooldown. [HARD] Grid-Scoped, Not Global — the TriggerGroups Overhead Trade-off Every tag-consuming field above searches only the **current grid's own, already-loaded** Trigger/Event lists — there is no global registry the way `EventManager.EventsList` is for Events generally. `ManuallyActivatedTriggerTags` searches that grid's `Triggers` + `CompromisedTriggers`; `Enable`/`Disable`/`ResetTriggerCooldownTags` search all four (`Triggers`, `DamageTriggers`, `CommandTriggers`, `CompromisedTriggers`) via `TriggerSystem.ToggleTagTriggers()`. All four lists are populated exclusively by that grid's own Behavior parsing `[Triggers:]`/`[TriggerGroups:]` at load. A Trigger never attached to this specific grid's Behavior is simply out of scope, permanently, for that grid. Consequence: a "universal" Action meant to tag-broadcast across many faction/encounter-type Trigger variants (via `{Faction}`/`{}` tokens in the tag value) still requires **every** variant to be individually attached to any Behavior that might need it — almost always via one `[TriggerGroups:Value]` bundling all of them, since `[TriggerGroups:]` just calls `AddTrigger()` once per contained Trigger onto every grid that loads it (no lazy/deferred loading). The tag system removes the need to write N separate broadcasts (one shared, tokenized line instead); it does not remove the need for N Trigger variants to exist and be loaded. This is not a meaningful runtime cost even for a large bundle: `TriggerSystem.ProcessTriggerWatchers()` (the per-tick condition-check loop) is throttled to run at most every 500ms, and a `[Type:Manual]` Trigger — what every tag-broadcast target should be — has no matching case in that function's per-type branch chain, so an idle one costs a handful of skipped string comparisons twice a second and nothing else. The real cost is file/authoring bulk and a one-time per-grid deserialization at spawn proportional to bundle size, not an ongoing tick-rate problem.

# Space Engineers SBC & XML Editing Guide

Technical guide to editing Space Engineers `.sbc` files safely, configuring IDE environments, protecting `<Description>` blocks, and avoiding engine deserializer traps.

---

## 1. IDE Configuration (VS Code / Cursor / Cline)

To enable syntax highlighting, validation, and auto-completion for Space Engineers `.sbc` files:

### A. File Association (`settings.json`)
Add the following to your VS Code / workspace `.vscode/settings.json`:
```json
{
  "files.associations": {
    "*.sbc": "xml",
    "*.sbcB5": "xml"
  },
  "xml.format.splitAttributes": false,
  "xml.format.joinCDATALines": false
}
```

### B. Recommended Extensions
- **XML** (Red Hat / `redhat.vscode-xml`): Provides XML schema validation, closing tag completion, and linting.
- **DotXML** or **XML Tools**: Quick formatting and tree navigation.

---

## 2. The `<Description>` Tag Protection Rule

> [!CAUTION]
> **Standard XML Formatters Break MES**:
> In standard XML formatters (like Prettier or standard XML Tools), formatting an `.sbc` file will wrap or re-indent text inside `<Description>`.
> Because MES relies on clean line-by-line parsing of square-bracket tags (e.g. `[RivalAI Behavior]`), wrapping tags onto single lines or inserting indentation inside tag strings causes **parsing failure**.
>
> **The Rule**: Never run a blind global XML formatter on `.sbc` files. Always use the dedicated formatter `powershell scripts/Format-MesSbc.ps1`, which strictly isolates and protects `<Description>` content.

---

## 3. Ban on XML Comments Inside `<Description>`

Keen's XML deserializer reads `<Description>` elements using `XmlReader.ReadElementString()`. This method expects strictly plain text content.

```xml
<!-- FATAL: Crashes Keen with System.Xml.XmlException, MOD SKIPPED -->
<Description>
  [RivalAI Behavior]
  <!-- Zone Presence Tracking -->
  [BehaviorName:Passive]
</Description>

<!-- SAFE: Uses RivalAI comment tag syntax -->
<Description>
  [RivalAI Behavior]
  [//Zone Presence Tracking]
  [BehaviorName:Passive]
</Description>
```

- Any XML comment (`<!-- ... -->`) placed inside a `<Description>` tag causes Keen to throw `MOD_CRITICAL_ERROR` and abort loading the entire mod.
- Outside `<Description>`, standard XML comments are completely legal.
- Inside `<Description>`, always use `[//Comment]` syntax.

---

## 4. Encoding & BOM Integrity

- **Required Encoding**: **UTF-8** (without BOM or with standard UTF-8 BOM).
- **Avoid UTF-16**: Never save `.sbc` files in UTF-16 (Unicode in Windows Notepad), as Keen's deserializer will fail to read the root element.
- When generating or saving files via scripts, always specify `[System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8`.
- **Enforced by `audit_sbc.ps1` (Check 0)**: flags UTF-16 LE/BE BOMs and invalid UTF-8 byte sequences as critical errors. UTF-8 with or without BOM is accepted.

---

## 5. SubtypeId & Tag Casing Best Practices

- **Strict Case Sensitivity**: While NTFS is case-insensitive on Windows, Keen's internal dictionaries (`Dictionary<string, ...>`) and MES lookups are **case-sensitive** for profile SubtypeIds.
- **Prefix Standard**: Always use `ModPrefix-ProfileType-Name` (e.g. `GVK-Trigger-Damage-Cruiser`).
- **Single SubtypeId per `<Id>`**: Never place more than one `<SubtypeId>` in an `<Id>` block.

---

## 6. Deserializer Quirk Examples

### A. Strict Single `<SubtypeId>` per `<Id>` Block
Keen's XML deserializer strictly accepts **only one** `<SubtypeId>` per `<Id>` block:
```xml
<!-- INVALID: Second SubtypeId is discarded by deserializer; action fails to load -->
<EntityComponent xsi:type="MyObjectBuilder_InventoryComponentDefinition">
  <Id>
    <TypeId>Inventory</TypeId>
    <SubtypeId>Trigger-OutsideZone</SubtypeId>
    <SubtypeId>Action-OutsideZone</SubtypeId>
  </Id>
</EntityComponent>

<!-- VALID: One definition per SubtypeId, each with its own <Id> block -->
<EntityComponent xsi:type="MyObjectBuilder_InventoryComponentDefinition">
  <Id>
    <TypeId>Inventory</TypeId>
    <SubtypeId>Trigger-OutsideZone</SubtypeId>
  </Id>
</EntityComponent>
```

### B. Strict Single `<Id>` per `<Prefab>` Block
Duplicate `<Id>` elements inside a `<Prefab>` cause Keen to read the first one and discard subsequent ones. Prefab headers are read by hand (`MyDefinitionManager.ReadPrefabHeader`), not by the serializer: only the first `<Id>` counts; if it has a `Type` attribute its attributes win, otherwise the LAST `<SubtypeId>` element inside it wins:
```xml
<!-- INVALID: Deserializer reads the first Id, registering prefab under wrong Subtype -->
<Prefab xsi:type="MyObjectBuilder_PrefabDefinition">
  <Id Type="MyObjectBuilder_PrefabDefinition" Subtype="NST Nav Tower" />
  <Id Type="MyObjectBuilder_PrefabDefinition" Subtype="NST Base Site Tower" />
  <CubeGrids>...</CubeGrids>
</Prefab>
```
Both are enforced by `audit_sbc.ps1` (Check 3, XML DOM duplicate detection).

### C. The General Rule: Repeats Are Dropped Silently [HARD]
Keen's definition loader (`MyObjectBuilderSerializerKeen`, pre-generated serializers) and MES's own XML files (`MyAPIGateway.Utilities.SerializeFromXML`) both use `XmlSerializer`. Nothing in SE hooks its `UnknownElement` event, so none of the cases below logs anything. Tested on .NET Framework 4.8.
- **A repeated list block keeps the LAST copy.** Two `<EntityComponents>` blocks in one `.sbc` (or two `<CubeBlocks>`, `<SpawnGroups>`, MES `<StoreItems>`): each copy is read and replaces the one before, so every definition in the earlier blocks silently never loads. Merge them into one block (`audit_sbc.ps1` check 8). The flat lists append instead: bare `<Definition>` and `<Environment>` entries under `<Definitions>`, `<Icon>` on a definition.
- **A repeated single value keeps the FIRST copy.** The reader marks each member as read the first time; a later element with the same name is skipped unread. `<MinAmount>1</MinAmount><MinAmount>2</MinAmount>` reads 1, and A (one `<SubtypeId>` per `<Id>`) is a case of this rule.
- **An attribute and an element for the same field**: the element wins (`<Id Subtype="A"><SubtypeId>B</SubtypeId></Id>` gives B), because attributes are read first. Prefab headers are the exception (B above).
- **A value that does not parse** (text in a number, `True` for a bool, a wrong-case enum, a comment inside the value) throws, and the whole file is dropped, not just that field. Keen logs `MOD SKIPPED, Cannot load definition file`, but only that file is lost; the rest of the mod loads.
- **Unknown element names** are ignored the same silent way, and names are case-sensitive, so a misspelled element keeps the field's default.
- **MES world configs (`Config-*.xml` in world storage)**: a value that does not parse makes MES use the default configuration (`Could Not Load Settings From Config-X.xml. Using Default Configuration.`, always logged), and its next save writes the defaults back over the file, so the hand edits are lost.

`<Description>` tags follow their own rule (the last copy of a single-value tag wins), see [`profiles_and_tags.md`](profiles_and_tags.md) §3. MES store-items files are audited by `audit_sbc.ps1` check 7 ([`economy_and_stores.md`](economy_and_stores.md) §1 Part 1).

# MES Spawning Architecture & Conditions Reference

Deep-dive architectural guide to Modular Encounters Systems (MES) spawning algorithms, spawner types, environmental filters, threat calculations, and event spawning.

---

## 1. Spawner Types & Execution Pathways

MES categorizes all spawns into distinct operational streams:

| Spawner Type | Environment | Trigger Mechanism | Altitude & Placement |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Space Cargo Ship** | Space (Zero-G) | Periodic timer per active player | Spawns ~10–15km from player, travels in vector, despawns at end |
| **Planetary Cargo Ship** | Planet / Atmosphere | Periodic timer per active player | Spawns along planetary tangent at configured altitude, traverses waypoints |
| **Random Encounter** | Space | Player movement into unpopulated voxel/space sector | Static or slow-drifting wreckage/stations |
| **Planetary Installation** | Planet Surface | Player movement into unpopulated terrain sector | Voxel-aligned static bases, outposts, and towers |
| **Boss Encounter** | Space or Planet | Custom conditions, threat score, or MES Events | High-threat capital ships or fortified complexes |
| **Drone Encounter** | Space or Planet | RivalAI Trigger (`[Type:Damage]`, `[Type:PlayerNear]`) | Custom spawn around parent grid via `[RivalAI Spawn]` |
| **Event Encounter** | Space or Planet | MES Event Action (`[SpawnEncounter:true]`) | Spawned at exact coordinates or player offset |

---

## 2. Spawn Group Architecture (`<SpawnGroup>`)

A spawn group definition combines vanilla Keen tags with MES description tags:

```xml
<SpawnGroup>
  <Id>
    <TypeId>SpawnGroupDefinition</TypeId>
    <SubtypeId>ModPrefix-SpawnGroup-EncounterName</SubtypeId>
  </Id>
  <Description>
    [Modular Encounters SpawnGroup]
    [SpawnConditionsProfiles:ModPrefix-SpawnCondition-EncounterName]
    [ManipulationProfiles:ModPrefix-Manipulation-EncounterName]
  </Description>
  <IsPirate>true</IsPirate>
  <Frequency>5.0</Frequency>
  <Prefabs>
    <Prefab SubtypeId="ModPrefix-Prefab-EncounterName">
      <Position><X>0.0</X><Y>0.0</Y><Z>0.0</Z></Position>
      <Speed>15.0</Speed>
      <Behaviour>ModPrefix-Behavior-EncounterName</Behaviour>
    </Prefab>
  </Prefabs>
</SpawnGroup>
```

### Critical Spawn Group Tags:
- **[HARD] `[Modular Encounters SpawnGroup]` header**: `SpawnGroupManager.cs:647` only builds an MES spawn group when the Description contains this exact string. Any other header (e.g. `[MES Spawn Group]`) leaves it a plain vanilla spawn group: every MES tag in it is ignored, with no error.
- `<Frequency>`: Relative weight among eligible groups in the same pool. Higher frequency increases spawn probability relative to other groups.
- **[HARD] `<Frequency>` also weights a spawner's `[SpawnGroups:]` list.** A `[RivalAI Spawn]` (or event spawner) naming several groups picks one per spawn, weighted by each group's `<Frequency>`. `SpawnGroupManager.cs` stores `Frequency x 10` rounded with .NET `Math.Round` (banker's rounding, so `0.25` becomes `2`), adds the group to the pool that many times, and `SpawnGroupCollection.cs` picks uniformly from the pool. Groups are matched against the list with `Contains`, so listing a group twice adds no weight. **Fails as**: a group's Frequency applies to every spawner that lists it; to weight one spawner differently, give it its own copy of the group. A spawner with a single group ignores Frequency.
- **[HARD] Frequency below 0.05 never spawns, and values ending in 5 round unpredictably.** `<Frequency>` is a `float`, converted with `(int)Math.Round((double)Frequency * 10)` (`ImprovedSpawnGroup.cs:177`, MES `bc71965`). Float representation shifts the halfway cases: `0.05` → 1, `0.15` → 2, `0.25` → 2, `0.35` → 3, `0.45` → 4; `0.04` → 0. **Fails as**: a group at `0.04` or lower is never picked, with no error. Use multiples of `0.1` when the weights must be exact.
- **[HARD] A group with several `[SpawnConditionsProfiles:]` enters the pool once.** `SpawnGroupManager.cs` uses the first profile that passes and stops (`break`), so extra profiles widen where a group can spawn but never add weight.
- **[HARD] Static encounters are tracked by spawn group name.** `NpcManager.cs` drops a saved static-encounter record when no spawn group with that name (and a `StaticEncounter`/boss condition) exists any more, and then treats a static group it has no record of as new. **Fails as**: renaming a static encounter's spawn group on a live world spawns a second copy beside the one already there. Rename it only on a wipe, or delete the old grid first.
  - **Ground altitude & Water Mod [HARD]**: `StaticEncounter.cs:InitStaticEncounter` (fixed in `c35adb5`) measures planet-direction encounter altitude from the ground (`ignoreWater: true`). Previously, it measured from the higher of ground or water once the Water Mod registered, causing encounters below sea level to change altitude when re-created later.
  - **[HARD] Which conditions profile a static uses** (MES `bc71965`; these lines date from 2021, so they applied in January 2025 too). A static reads two profiles, chosen differently:
    - **The record** (trigger coords and radius, exact coords, forward/up, planet direction, faction): the **first** profile in list order with `[StaticEncounter:true]`, when the encounter is created at world load (`NpcManager.LoadNewStaticEncounters` -> `StaticEncounter.InitStaticEncounter`). The spawn group's Description is profile 0, so if it says `[StaticEncounter:true]`, the record comes from it.
    - **The spawn** (everything else: sandbox variables, zone conditions, threat, `[ForceExactPositionAndOrientation:]`, `[ForceStaticGrid:]`, `[RotateFirstCockpitToForward:]`, unique marking): the **first** profile that passes the spawn-type and common checks (`SpawnRequest.CalculateStaticSpawn` -> `SpawnGroupManager.GetSpawnGroups`, which stops at the first pass). On a planet a profile passes the spawn-type check only with `[StaticEncounter:true]`. The checks run at the **trigger coords**, not at the spawn point (`EnvironmentEvaluation(encounter.TriggerCoords)`), so strict-zone and zone conditions are tested there.
    - **Fails as**: a static whose Description sets `[StaticEncounter:true]` and its coords (each static needs its own coords, so they tend to go inline) plus `[SpawnConditionsProfiles:Shared]` for the common tags. Profile 0 is complete and passes first, so the shared profile is never used: its zone conditions, sandbox variables and rotation tags are ignored. This is what GVK hit in January 2025 (GVK-Derelicts `1aee79b` added zone conditions to a shared KOTH-Massive profile; `fd85248` moved them into each spawn group, which worked).
    - **Rule**: for statics, keep every condition tag in one profile per spawn group: either all in the Description (what GVK does now), or `[SpawnConditionsProfiles:]` alone with nothing but the header in the Description. **[HARD, tested in play]** For shared tags plus per-group coords, `[UseFirstConditionsAsPersistent:true]` makes profile 0 a gate (it supplies the record) and the spawn uses the next profile that passes; the shared profile then needs `[StaticEncounter:true]` and the placement tags.
  - **[HARD] Space statics can spawn with a profile that isn't a static one** (MES `bc71965`, since 2021; confirmed in play, reported as MeridiusIX/Modular-Encounters-Systems#417). `SpawningTypeAllowedForGroup` checks `type.HasFlag(StaticEncounterSpace) || type.HasFlag(StaticEncounterPlanet) && conditions.StaticEncounter` (`SpawnConditions.cs:177`); `&&` binds first, so off-planet every conditions profile passes the spawn-type check, with or without `[StaticEncounter:true]`, and the Description profile (index 0) is checked first. **Fails as**: a space static whose `[StaticEncounter:true]` lives in a `[SpawnConditionsProfiles:]` profile spawns with the Description's conditions instead (`ConditionIndex: 0` in `/MES.IGGD`); placement and faction still come from the static profile, but its other condition tags are ignored, and because the used profile has no `StaticEncounter`/`UniqueEncounter`, the group is not added to the unique-spawned list (`SpawnRequest.PostSpawn`), so the encounter is re-created at the next world load and spawns again (seen in a GVK test: deleted, saved, reloaded, and it came back; the `[UseFirstConditionsAsPersistent:true]` copy did not). Planet statics are not affected (that branch does require `[StaticEncounter:true]`). **Workaround**: put `[StaticEncounter:true]` and the static's condition tags in the spawn group's Description, or `[UseFirstConditionsAsPersistent:true]` so profile 0 is only a gate.
  - **Static encounter resets [HARD]**: `ResetThisStaticEncounter` (`NpcManager.cs`, fixed in `af492a5`) selects the first profile with `[StaticEncounter:true]` even if non-static condition profiles are listed ahead of it, and removes all duplicate entries from `UniqueGroupsSpawned`. To replace all spawned static encounters on a live world with fresh definitions without running Despawn actions, use `/MES.Debug.ResetStaticEncounters` (or `/MES.Debug.ResetStaticEncounters.Info` for dry run; §2D of `diagnostics_and_troubleshooting.md`).
  - **[HARD] `[ForceExactPositionAndOrientation:true]` puts the grid origin on `[StaticEncounterCoords:]` and grid +Y along `[StaticEncounterUp:]`.** `PrefabSpawner.cs` adds `UseGridOrigin` and `UseOnlyWorldMatrix`, so the prefab's saved orientation is ignored. A grid built with its up along another axis spawns tilted or upside down: before writing Up, check which way the prefab's functional blocks face (`<BlockOrientation ... Up="Down"/>` means up is grid -Y, so point Up at the planet center). The origin is the center of block (0,0,0), not the base, so measure the base's offset from it in the prefab before raising or lowering the coords.
  - **[HARD] A prefab exported while its grid was a station spawns as a station.** The export keeps `<IsStatic>true</IsStatic>` (and `<IsUnsupportedStation>true</IsUnsupportedStation>`), and MES changes it only for `[ForceStaticGrid:true]` or `[DoNotForceStaticGrid:true]` (`PrefabManipulation.ProcessManipulations`), so a ship rebuilt as a station and exported never moves. Delete both lines from a moving NPC's prefab, or set `[DoNotForceStaticGrid:true]` in its spawn conditions.
- `[SpawnConditionsProfiles:]`: Reference to one or more `[MES Spawn Conditions]` profiles.
- `[ManipulationProfiles:]` / `[ManipulationGroups:]`: Reference to `[MES Manipulation]` profiles (block replacement, weapon randomizer, dereliction via `[UseGridDereliction:true]` + `[DerelictionProfiles:]`, inventory, recolor).
- `[ReplenishSystems:bool]` + `[ReplenishProfiles:]`: Spawn-group-level ammo/fuel top-up (§5 of `manipulation_and_dereliction.md`).
- **Inline profiles**: `ImprovedSpawnGroup.InitTags()` also parses the spawn group's own Description as its first Spawn Conditions profile and first Manipulation profile (`ImprovedSpawnGroup.cs:125-128`). Each `[SpawnConditionsProfiles:]` profile is **appended** after that inline profile, not merged into it (`TagParse.TagSpawnConditionsProfileCheck`), and MES checks every profile in the list separately; whichever one passes is the one used to spawn (size, placement, faction).
  - **[HARD]** Inline condition tags only take effect when the Description is a complete conditions profile on its own, i.e. it sets a spawn type (`[PlanetaryInstallation:true]`, `[SpaceCargoShip:true]`, ...). Without one, the inline profile never passes the spawn-type check (`SpawnConditions.SpawningTypeAllowedForGroup`, `SpawnConditions.cs:133-185`; checked in `SpawnGroupManager.cs:289-295`).
  - So a spawn group that uses `[SpawnConditionsProfiles:]` silently ignores condition tags written next to it in its Description (e.g. `[PlanetaryInstallationType:Large]`). Put them in the referenced `[MES Spawn Conditions]` profile instead. If the Description also sets a spawn type, it becomes a second, independent set of conditions, not an addition to the referenced profile.
  - `[UseFirstConditionsAsPersistent:true]` turns the inline profile into a gate every other profile must also pass (`SpawnGroupManager.cs:218-260`), but the spawn itself still uses the referenced profile that matched, so placement tags like `[PlanetaryInstallationType:]` still have to go there.
  - `[PlanetaryInstallationType:]` defaults to `Small` (`SpawnConditionsProfile.cs:391`); any value other than `Small`/`Medium`/`Large` is reset to `Small` (`SpawnConditions.cs:822-824`). A misplaced tag therefore gives a Small installation with no error.
- **[HARD] `<Enabled>false</Enabled>` removes a spawn group from MES entirely.** `SpawnGroupManager.cs:606` skips disabled definitions before parsing anything else. Redefining a vanilla or other-mod spawn group (same `TypeId`/`SubtypeId`) with `Enabled = false` in your own mod disables it everywhere, with no per-world config.

### Base-game spawn groups MES picks up [HARD]
MES loads every vanilla spawn group too, whatever the world's own encounter settings say:
- **`IsPlanetaryEncounter`** groups (`SpawnGroups_PlanetaryEncounters.sbc`, `P1_SupplyPost` ... `P30_AbandonedFarmstead`) become **Planetary Installations** (`SpawnGroupManager.cs:767-770`). Their `<PlanetaryInstallationSettings><Planets>` becomes the planet whitelist (`:864-873`); groups without one (`P28_LogisticsPost`, `P29_WreckedHopper`) spawn on any planet. With `EnablePlanetaryEncounters = false` in the world they still mix into your installation/wreck pools.
- **Ways to stop them:** the official add-on "Suppress Vanilla Planetary Installations" (Steam `3796756949`, detected in `AddonManager.cs:177`, applied by `ApplySuppression`, `SpawnGroupManager.cs:993-998`); redefining each group with `Enabled = false` (above); or listing them in `Config-General.xml` `NpcSpawnGroupBlacklist`. Sister add-ons exist for vanilla cargo ships (`888457124`) and space encounters (`888457381`).
- Their prefabs stay loaded and can be used by your own spawn groups. `audit_mes_references.ps1` resolves them through `scripts/vanilla_prefabs.json`.

---

## 3. Spawn Conditions Profile (`[MES Spawn Conditions]`)

Declared in an `Inventory` EntityComponent definition.

### A. Environment & Gravity Gates
- `[SpaceCargoShip:bool]`: Enables spawning in space cargo pools.
- `[LunarCargoShip:bool]`: Enables spawning in moon cargo pools.
- `[PlanetaryCargoShip:bool]`: Enables spawning in planetary cargo pools.
- `[SpaceRandomEncounter:bool]`: Enables static space encounters.
- `[PlanetaryInstallation:bool]`: Enables planetary base/station spawns.
- `[RivalAiSpawn:bool]` / `[RivalAiAnySpawn:bool]` / `[RivalAiSpaceSpawn:bool]` / `[RivalAiAtmosphericSpawn:bool]`: Make the group eligible for RivalAI `[RivalAI Spawn]` / event spawns (`SpawnConditions.cs:174` accepts any of the four).

### B. Planetary Altitude & Placement
- `[MinSpawnFromPlanetSurface:<double>]` & `[MaxSpawnFromPlanetSurface:<double>]`: Altitude window (meters above surface) at the spawn position; `-1` (default) disables each bound (`SpawnConditions.DistanceFromSurfaceCheck`). `[MinAltitude:]`/`[MaxAltitude:]` are `[RivalAI Spawn]` tags and are ignored here.
- `[AlignToSurface:bool]` *(MES 2.74.02)*: Planetary installations align to the terrain surface instead of the default gravity-up orientation.
- **Terrain checks [HARD]:** two tags read the same `[AllowedTerrainTypes:]` / `[DisallowedTerrainTypes:]` lists (voxel material `MaterialTypeName`, e.g. `Rock`, `Sand`, `Snow`), at different places:
  - `[InstallationTerrainValidation:true]` (planetary installations only): checks the terrain at each candidate spawn spot and skips spots that fail (`PathPlacements.IsPositionSurfaceValid`). Use this to keep installations off roads or rock. Only the centre point is checked, so a large prefab can still overhang the edge.
  - `[UseTerrainTypeValidation:true]` (any spawn type): checks the most common terrain within about 165 m of the player (`SpawnConditions.cs` ~429). Turning it on next to `InstallationTerrainValidation` also blocks the spawn whenever the player stands on a disallowed terrain.
  - The MES wiki only documents the player-area meaning and has no `DisallowedTerrainTypes` card.
- Water Mod installations: `[InstallationSpawnsOnWaterSurface:bool]` / `[InstallationSpawnsUnderwater:bool]` with `[MinWaterDepth:<double>]` / `[MaxWaterDepth:<double>]` *(MaxWaterDepth added in 2.74.03)*. **[HARD]** The placement check rejects depths below `MinWaterDepth` or above `MaxWaterDepth` (`PathPlacements.cs:836-845`). Since MES 2.74.05 `MaxWaterDepth` defaults to `-1` (no maximum). In 2.74.03-2.74.04 it defaulted to `0`, which rejected every water-surface/underwater station and underwater creature placement unless it was set. `[MaxWaterDepth:0]` still allows no water placement (creatures spawn on dry land only).
- `[CutVoxelsAtAirtightCells:true]`: **[HARD]** Cuts terrain meshes only around airtight cells of subterranean stations.
- `[CutVoxelSize:<double>]`: Voxel cut buffer size in meters (e.g. `2.5`).
  > [!WARNING]
  > Never use `[CutVoxels:true]` on `[MES Spawn Conditions]`. It does not exist and silently fails. `<CutVoxels>true</CutVoxels>` is Keen's vanilla XML tag for `<SpawnGroup>`.

### C. Threat Score & Combat Readiness
MES evaluates player threat score based on block count, weapons, and grid mass in range:
- `[UseThreatLevelCheck:true]`
- `[ThreatScoreMinimum:<int>]` & `[ThreatScoreMaximum:<int>]`
- `[ThreatLevelCheckRange:<double>]`: Radius around spawn point to calculate player threat (default: 5000m).
- `[ThreatScoreGridConfiguration:All]` (or `Static`, `Dynamic`).
- `[ThreatIncludeOtherNpcOwners:bool]`, `[ThreatScorePlanetaryHandicap:<float>]`.

### D. Weather, Day/Night & Sandbox Variables
- `[UseWeatherSpawning:true]` + `[AllowedWeatherSystems:Fog,Dust,Sandstorm]`: Requires active planet weather.
- `[UseDayOrNightOnly:true]` + `[SpawnOnlyAtNight:bool]`: Day/night gate (`false` = day only).
- `[SandboxVariables:...]` / `[FalseSandboxVariables:...]`: Sandbox booleans that must be true / false. `{SpawnGroupName}` resolves in both *(MES 2.74.00)*.
- `[CheckCustomSandboxCounters:true]` + `[CustomSandboxCounters:...]` + `[CustomSandboxCountersTargets:...]` + `[SandboxCounterCompareTypes:...]` (targets list is zero-stripped — see `events_and_zones.md` §3).
- `[UseRandomCustomFaction:bool]` *(MES 2.74.00)*: Completes the random-faction set alongside the existing faction randomizers.

### E. Economy Item Contracts
- `[EnableItemTriggeredContracts:bool]` *(MES 2.74.03, default `false`; forced `true` for converted vanilla SpawnGroups)*: lets Keen's item-triggered delivery contracts seed a data item into the encounter's cargo. Needs world Economy on. Full mechanics and caveats: [`economy_and_stores.md`](economy_and_stores.md) §4.

---

## 4. RivalAI Grid-Bound Spawner (`[RivalAI Spawn]`)

Used inside Action profiles (`[Spawner:<SubtypeId>]`) to deploy escorts, defense drones, or reinforcements around a live grid.

```xml
<EntityComponent xsi:type="MyObjectBuilder_InventoryComponentDefinition">
  <Id>
    <TypeId>Inventory</TypeId>
    <SubtypeId>ModPrefix-Spawner-DefenseDrone</SubtypeId>
  </Id>
  <Description>
    [RivalAI Spawn]
    [UseSpawn:true]
    [SpawningType:CustomSpawn]
    [FirstSpawnTimeMs:0]
    [SpawnGroups:ModPrefix-SpawnGroup-DefenseDrone]
    [MinDistance:150]
    [MaxDistance:300]
    [MinAltitude:30]
    [MaxAltitude:60]
    [InheritNpcAltitude:true]
  </Description>
</EntityComponent>
```

- **Required Gate**: `[UseSpawn:true]`
- `[SpawningType:CustomSpawn]`: Spawns relative to parent grid.
- `[MinDistance:<double>]` & `[MaxDistance:<double>]`: Radial distance from parent.
- `[InheritNpcAltitude:bool]`: Aligns drone altitude to parent grid's altitude.
- `[FirstSpawnTimeMs:<int>]`, `[SpawnMinCooldown:<int>]` / `[SpawnMaxCooldown:<int>]`, `[MaxSpawns:<int>]`: Timing and cap. `[StartsReady:true]` *(parsed since MES 2.74.04; ignored before)* lets the **first** spawn skip the cooldown; later spawns still wait for it (`SpawnProfile.IsReadyToSpawn`).
- **One spot per spawn [HARD]**: the spawner picks one random point between `MinDistance` and `MaxDistance`. It re-rolls only while a player stands within 100 m of it (up to 15 tries), then checks the spawn group's conditions at that one point (`BehaviorSpawnHelper.cs`, `SpawnRequest.CalculateSpawn(_spawnMatrix.Translation, ...)`). A condition that fails there drops the spawn with no retry and no message. **Fails as:** a ring of grids spaced with `[RemoteControlCodeMinDistance:]` near the ring's size mostly fails to place. With 600 m spacing on a 300-500 m ring, a second grid fits about half the time and a fourth almost never **[SOFT: rate from geometry, failures seen in game]**. Keep the spacing well under the ring radius, and if the spawn is paid for, start the cooldown only when the spawned grid reports in.

---

## 5. MES Event Spawner (`[MES Event Action]`)

Used by global session-level events to spawn encounters at precise coordinates:

```xml
<EntityComponent xsi:type="MyObjectBuilder_InventoryComponentDefinition">
  <Id>
    <TypeId>Inventory</TypeId>
    <SubtypeId>ModPrefix-EventAction-SpawnConvoy</SubtypeId>
  </Id>
  <Description>
    [MES Event Action]
    [SpawnEncounter:true]
    [SpawnCoords:{X:60487.11 Y:32965.06 Z:44090.29}]
    [SpawnFactionTags:GAALSIEN]
    [SpawnFactionTags:SPRT]
    [SpawnData:ModPrefix-EventSpawner-Convoy]
  </Description>
</EntityComponent>
```

### Critical Event Spawner Rules:
1. **Tag Name**: Must use `[SpawnData:<SubtypeId>]`, NOT `[Spawner:]`.
2. **Master Gate**: Must declare `[SpawnEncounter:true]`.
3. **List Alignment**: `SpawnCoords`, `SpawnFactionTags`, and `SpawnData` must have strictly identical element counts.
4. **Special Flags on Spawner Profile**:
   - `[ProcessAsAdminSpawn:true]`: Bypasses standard player distance and safezone spawn rejection.
   - `[IgnoreSafetyChecks:true]`: Allows spawning near player grids or structures for scripted set-pieces.
   - `[InheritNpcAltitude:false]`: Uses absolute coordinate altitude rather than raycasting from a non-existent parent.

---

## 6. Faction Resolution & The Silent Spawn Rejection Pipeline [HARD]

When an NPC spawn group is evaluated for spawning, MES resolves the owning faction tag before any grid is spawned. If the faction tag does not exist or has a typo, **the spawn group is silently discarded with a 0% spawn rate and no in-game warning or crash**.

### A. The Resolution Code (`SpawnConditions.cs:2144-2168`)
During `ValidNpcFactions()`, MES queries the active session factions:
```csharp
var initialFaction = MyAPIGateway.Session.Factions.TryGetFactionByTag(initialFactionTag);

if (initialFaction != null) {
    factionList.Add(initialFaction);
} else {
    if (initialFactionTag == "Nobody") {
        resultList.Add("Nobody");
    }
    else if (initialFactionTag == "UseBaseGameFactionTags") {
        foreach (var baseGameTags in spawnGroup.BaseGameFactionTags) {
            resultList.Add(baseGameTags);
        }
    }
    return resultList; // <--- Returns an EMPTY list (Count == 0)!
}
```

### B. The Silent Drop (`SpawnGroupManager.cs:307-314`)
When `ValidNpcFactions()` returns an empty list, `SpawnGroupManager` immediately skips the group:
```csharp
var validFactionsList = SpawnConditions.ValidNpcFactions(spawnGroup, conditions, environment.Position, overrideFaction, forceSpawn, collection);

if (validFactionsList.Count == 0 && collection.OwnerOverride < 0) {
    SpawnLogger.Queue("   - Could Not Get Valid NPC Faction.", SpawnerDebugEnum.SpawnGroup, addToReason: true);
    continue; // Rejects group from eligible spawn pool!
}
```
- The group is never added to `collection.SpawnGroupSublists`.
- It has an absolute **0% chance of spawning naturally**.
- **Admin Force-Spawning Fails**: Even `/mes spawn <SpawnGroup>` evaluates `ValidNpcFactions()`, which still returns 0 factions and fails to spawn.

### C. Points of Failure & Where Typos Occur
1. **`[FactionOwner:<Tag>]` in `[MES Spawn Conditions]`**: Default is `SPRT`. A typo here (e.g. `SPTR`) breaks all spawn conditions referencing the tag.
2. **`[FactionOverride:<Tag>]` in the `[Modular Encounters SpawnGroup]` Description**: Overrides `FactionOwner`. A typo here breaks the entire spawn group.
3. **`[UseAllowedFactions:true]` + `[AllowedFactions:<Tag>]` in `[MES Zone]`** *(MES 2.74.00)*: In `SpawnConditions.cs:2096`, if the resolved faction is not in the zone whitelist, spawning fails with:
   `"Zone Check Failed: Faction '<tag>' is not among Allowed Zone Factions."` (`[UseRestrictedFactions:true]` + `[RestrictedFactions:]` is the blacklist twin, line 2120.)
4. **`[SpawnFactionTags:<Tag>]` in `[MES Event Action]`**: Used with `[SpawnEncounter:true]`.
5. **Missing Mod in World Save**: If a mod defining custom factions in `Factions.sbc` is omitted from the world save, or if `Factions.sbc` had XML syntax errors preventing it from loading, Space Engineers never registers the faction in `Session.Factions`, silently disabling all spawns for that faction.

### D. Special Reserved Keywords (Bypassing Faction Lookup)
- **`"Nobody"`**: Spawns the grid as completely unowned (neutral derelicts/stations).
- **`"UseBaseGameFactionTags"`**: Instructs MES to read the vanilla `<FactionSubtypeIds>` defined directly in the `<SpawnGroup>` XML.

### E. Faction Tag Conventions & Tiered Classification
1. **Player vs. NPC Faction Length**:
   - In Space Engineers, player-created factions in the GUI are strictly **3 characters**.
   - NPC factions defined in `Factions*.sbc` should use **4 or more characters** (e.g. `SPRT`, `SPID`, `GAALSIEN`) to prevent naming collisions with player-created factions.
2. **Tiered Validation**:
   - **Tier 1 (Primary & Declared)**: `SPRT`, `SPID`, reserved keywords (`Nobody`, `UseBaseGameFactionTags`), plus any faction declared in local `Factions*.sbc`. Pass silently.
   - **Tier 2 (Obscure Vanilla / Economy / Campaign)**: `CIVL`, `TRAD`, `ROBO`, `FSD`, `STEJ`, `KRI`, `INDEP`, `SHIV`, `GTI`, `ROS`, `AMPH`, `BLDR`, `MINR`, `MILT`, `PIR8`, `RED`, `BLU`. Flagged as `[INFO]` (soft notice) since modders rarely target Keen economy/campaign factions and they require specific world settings to exist.
   - **Tier 3 (Unrecognized / Typo)**: Any undefined tag causes silent 0% spawn drops and is flagged as `[WARN]`.
3. **IdsReplacer Incompatibility with Pre-Spawn Faction Tags**:
   - `IdsReplacer` runs only at runtime on active grids with `NpcData` (e.g., chat, GPS, LCDs, and `PlayerConditionProfile.CheckReputationwithFaction`).
   - `SpawnConditions.cs` (`ValidNpcFactions`) and `EventActionExecution.cs` (`[SpawnFactionTags]`) evaluate pre-spawn before `NpcData` exists.
   - Using dynamic tokens like `{Faction}`, `{Attacker}`, or `{SandboxVar}` inside `[FactionOwner:]`, `[FactionOverride:]`, `[SpawnFactionTags:]`, or `[CheckReputationAgainstOtherNPCFaction:]` causes a literal string lookup in session factions that fails, permanently locking the encounter to 0% spawn rate. Flagged as `[ERROR]`.

# Tag Recipes for Common MES Features

Known-good groups of tags for the features encounter designers build most. Each recipe lists every profile involved and the tags that must go together; the silent failure each pairing prevents is under the block. Build new profiles from these instead of copying another mod's.

Checked against MES master `5899d09`. `scripts/test_tag_recipes.py` pulls every block out of this file and runs the audits on it; run it after editing a recipe.

**How to read a block**: `== Name` starts a profile and is its SubtypeId; the next line is its header. Wrap each profile as shown in [Wrappers](#wrappers). Names use `MyMod-`; rename them all consistently. Tags not shown keep their MES defaults: look them up with `query_mes_tags.py --profile <type>` rather than writing defaults out.

---

## Wrappers

A profile is an `EntityComponent`; only the Description changes between types. A spawn group is a `SpawnGroup`. Lines starting with `<` in a recipe's spawn group block go inside its `<Prefabs>`.

```xml
<EntityComponent xsi:type="MyObjectBuilder_InventoryComponentDefinition">
  <Id>
    <TypeId>Inventory</TypeId>
    <SubtypeId>MyMod-Action-Example</SubtypeId>
  </Id>
  <Description>
    [RivalAI Action]
    [//Tags go here. Comments use [//...], never XML comments.]
  </Description>
</EntityComponent>

<SpawnGroup>
  <Id>
    <TypeId>SpawnGroupDefinition</TypeId>
    <SubtypeId>MyMod-SpawnGroup-Example</SubtypeId>
  </Id>
  <Description>
    [Modular Encounters SpawnGroup]
  </Description>
  <IsPirate>true</IsPirate>
  <Frequency>1.0</Frequency>
  <Prefabs>
    <Prefab SubtypeId="MyMod-Prefab-Example">
      <Position><X>0</X><Y>0</Y><Z>0</Z></Position>
      <Speed>0</Speed>
      <Behaviour>MyMod-Behavior-Example</Behaviour>
    </Prefab>
  </Prefabs>
</SpawnGroup>
```

A RivalAI profile only runs when something reaches it: behavior → `[Triggers:]` → `[Actions:]` → the profile. To use a trigger from a recipe, add `[Triggers:<name>]` to the behavior (one name per tag line).

[RivalAiReplaceRemoteControl:true]
[SpawnConditionsProfiles:MyMod-SpawnConditions-Raider]

# In-Game Testing & Debugging Procedures for MES Encounters

How to test an NPC mod built on MES, and how an agent writes a test procedure the mod author can follow in game. Command details are in `diagnostics_and_troubleshooting.md` §2; error signatures in its §4.

**Verified against**: MES `bc71965` (2.75.02), `Sync/ChatMessage.cs`, `Logging/LoggerTools.cs`, `Spawning/SpawnRequest.cs`, `Spawning/SpawnConditions.cs`. **[HARD]** = read in source. **[SOFT]** = field practice.

---

## 1. Rules for writing a test procedure

Work down this ladder. Only go to the next rung when the current one cannot explain the problem.

1. **Visual checks** with admin debug commands (§3).
2. **Debug chat messages** added to the profiles under test (§4).
3. **Logs** (§5). Second to last: logs are long, slow to read, and need the tester to copy buffers out.
4. **Debug lines injected into the local MES copy** (§6). Last resort, but valid: it has found real MES bugs.

Every procedure the agent writes must follow these rules:

- **Steps the tester can actually do**: chat commands, flying or walking to a spot, approaching, shooting or damaging the NPC, saving and reloading the world, editing the mod's `.sbc` files. **Never** ask them to paste text or scripts into a Remote Control or other block, edit a block's Custom Data, or run a programmable block to "inspect" MES.
- **Checks the tester can actually see**: how the grid moves, chat lines, `/MES.Debug.DrawPaths` lines, zone spheres, GPS markers, the clipboard text from `/MES.IGGB` and the other `/MES.Info.*` commands, and block states shown in the terminal (on/off, owner). **Never** ask them to look for HUD elements, markers or values that MES does not show to a player.
- **Exact commands, in order**, with where to stand, what to do, what to expect, and what each result means.
- **Spawn the NPC with MES, never from a blueprint or a pasted prefab.** A pasted grid does not go through the spawner, so it skips the spawn conditions, manipulation, faction ownership and the NPC data the behavior relies on; whatever it does says nothing about the real encounter.
- **One change per test cycle.** MES reads its profiles when the world loads, so after editing an `.sbc`: save, quit to the main menu, and load the world again (dedicated server: restart). After changing a prefab, delete its `.sbcB5` (`diagnostics_and_troubleshooting.md` §4.7).
- **Confirm the change is in the game before handing over a test.** A mod built from a project (MDK2, a deploy script) only reaches the game after a build; check the deployed copy in `%AppData%\SpaceEngineers\Mods\<mod>` for the new tag or profile, or a test runs on the old files. A local MES clone used as the mod is live without a build.
- **Clean up between runs**: `/MES.Debug.RemoveAllNpcs` removes every grid that is mostly NPC-owned and passes MES's basic cleanup checks (Keen economy stations are kept). `/MES.Debug.DeleteGrid` removes the grid under your crosshair (within 10 km) and every grid linked to it, wheels and rotor tops included (`Cleaning.RemoveGrid`).

---

## 2. Make the test NPC spawnable on demand **[HARD]**

`/MES.Spawn.<Type>.<SpawnGroupName>` (or a shortcut below) spawns that one group at the tester's position. It runs as an **admin spawn** (`ChatMessage.ProcessSpawn` -> `SpawnRequest.CalculateSpawn(..., forceSpawn: false, adminSpawn: true, ...)`):

- It **skips** spawn timeouts and the global NPC cap (`MaxGlobalNpcGrids`).
- It **still checks** every other condition of the spawn group at the tester's position: spawn type, planet and altitude, threat, zones, faction, sandbox variables and the rest. Stand where a natural spawn would be allowed.
- The spawn group name is split on `.`, so a name containing a dot cannot be spawned this way.

**The spawn group needs a conditions profile with the matching spawn type**, or the debug log says `SpawnGroup SpawnType(s) Not Matched.` and nothing spawns (`SpawnConditions.SpawningTypeAllowedForGroup`):

| Command (shortcut) | Conditions tag that must be `true` |
| :--- | :--- |

- **Static encounters: `/MES.Spawn.StaticEncounter.<SpawnGroupName>`** (`/MES.SSE`; master after 2.75.02, `a1895d9`, PR #447) spawns a static encounter that hasn't spawned yet at its own trigger coordinates, whatever your distance, through the normal static spawn checks, so a spawn group whose conditions fail still doesn't spawn (the reply says the request was sent). With no name, or a name with no pending static encounter, it replies `Static Encounter Not Found Or Already Spawned: <name>`; a second run after it spawned gets that reply. Up to 2.75.02 `ProcessSpawn` had no `StaticEncounter` case and only answered `No Spawning Type From Chat`: fly to its coordinates instead. To respawn one, use `/MES.Debug.ResetThisStaticEncounters.<SpawnGroupName>` or `/MES.Debug.ResetStaticEncounters` (`diagnostics_and_troubleshooting.md` §2D).
- **NPCs normally spawned by something else** (a `[RivalAI Spawn]` profile, an event, a store purchase) still need a spawn type to be tested alone. Add a test-only conditions profile to the group, e.g. `[SpawnConditionsProfiles:MyGroup-Conditions,MyGroup-TestConditions]`, where the test profile sets the spawn type plus `[AdminSpawnOnly:true]` so it never passes for a natural spawn. Each conditions profile is checked on its own and the one that passes is the one used for the spawn (`spawning_and_conditions.md` §2, inline profiles; `/MES.IGGD` shows its `ConditionIndex`), so copy into the test profile every placement and faction tag the real profile uses (`[FactionOwner:]`, `[PlanetaryInstallationType:]`, ...).
- **`[AdminSpawnOnly:true]` doesn't keep a group out of a random admin spawn** [HARD]. A spawn command with no group name (`/MES.SPI`, `/MES.SDE`, ...) is an admin spawn too: `ChatMessage.cs` passes `adminSpawn: true` either way, and the name only narrows the eligible list. MES has no tag that allows a group only when it is named. `Frequency` counts as well: each group gets `round(Frequency x 10)` slots in the random pick (`SpawnGroupManager.cs`), so a test group at 1.0 gets ten slots against four for a real group at 0.4. To keep test groups out of random admin spawns:
  - Gate their test conditions on a sandbox boolean (`[SandboxVariables:MyMod_TestSpawns]`). Set it with `/MES.Debug.ChangeBool.MyMod_TestSpawns.true` for a test session and `.false` after. The check runs for admin spawns.
  - Give them `Frequency` 0.1 (one slot), so a random pick rarely gets one while the gate is on. Don't go lower: below 0.05 the group rounds to no slots and never spawns, not even by name.
- **Test files must never be empty.** A 0-byte `.sbc` stops the whole world from loading (`diagnostics_and_troubleshooting.md` §4.16). Run `scripts/audit_sbc.ps1` before loading. Remove the test profiles before release, or keep them `[AdminSpawnOnly:true]` and behind the gate above.
- **Area limits need a type with an area** [HARD]. Drones and creatures have no area radius (`Settings.GetSpawnAreaRadius` returns -1), so `MaxShipsPerArea` never stops them. Test an area limit with a cargo ship, installation, random or boss encounter.
- **Spawning next to your own grids** [HARD]: admin spawns still check the distance from other grids (`MinimumSpawnDistanceFromOtherGrids` for installations, `MinSpawnDistFromEntities` for planetary cargo ships, `MinDistanceFromOtherEntities` for random encounters, in each type's config). `[SkipGridSpawnChecks:true]` in the test conditions profile skips them, and the grid checks along cargo ship paths.
- **Nothing spawned?** Check in this order: the chat reply (`No Spawning Type From Chat` = wrong type word); `/MES.GESAP` at the spot (lists the groups eligible here for natural spawns, so it also applies timeouts); then the spawn log (§5).

# Third-Party Mod & Framework Integrations

Engineering guidelines for integrating Modular Encounters Systems (MES) with major third-party frameworks: CoreSystems (WeaponCore), Defense Shields, AiEnabled, Water Mod, and Torch server plugins.

---

## 1. CoreSystems / WeaponCore (WC) Integration

MES contains built-in hooks for WeaponCore grids, but deep architectural mismatches require strict engineering workarounds:

### A. The 800m Turret Range Clamp
- **[HARD] Default Clamp**: On grid spawn and weapon randomization, MES executes `SetAutomatedWeaponRanges(useMax: false)` (`GridEntity.cs:1736`), clamping all automated weapon ranges to **800m**.
- **The Fix**: Any combat encounter with long-range or capital weapons must execute `[SetWeaponsToMaxRange:true]` in an early trigger action (e.g. on spawn, on player proximity, or on damage) to allow WC turrets to engage past 800m.

### B. SetWeaponsToMaxRange Bugs: 0 m Weapons and Skipped Subgrid Turrets (MES #332)
Checked against MES upstream master `20d6092` and WeaponCore workshop `3154371364` (`Api/ApiBackend.cs`).

- **[HARD] The Bug (MES issue #332, open)**: `SetWeaponsToMaxRange` / `SetWeaponsToMinRange` can set every WeaponCore weapon of one block type to **0 m** until the server restarts. Most likely on blocks a weapon randomizer or block replacer has just swapped in.
  - `SetWeaponCoreRandomRanges` reads `GetMaxWeaponRange(block, 0)` once per block **type** and keeps it in the static `DefaultRangeWC` (`WeaponRandomizer.cs:50, 1319-1322`); every later weapon of that type reuses it.
  - WeaponCore's `GetMaxWeaponRange` returns `0` until the weapon's platform is `Ready` (`ApiBackend.cs:1177-1183`). An early first read stores 0 for that type.
  - When ready it returns the weapon's current `MaxTargetDistance`, not the definition's max, so a weapon already clamped to 800 m reports 800.
- **[HARD] More range bugs in the same code**:
  - `SetWeaponCoreRandomRanges` loops over `grid.LinkedGrids` and collects the whole grid's weapons each pass (`GetBlocksOfType` already walks linked grids), so each weapon is set once per subgrid. A closed subgrid `return`s out of the loop early (`WeaponRandomizer.cs:1298-1303`).
  - `SetAutomatedWeaponRanges` loops over the linked grids but reads `this.Turrets` each time (`GridEntity.cs:1736`), so **vanilla turrets on subgrids never get a range set**: neither the 800 m clamp nor `SetWeaponsToMaxRange` reaches them.
- **[HARD] WeaponCore caps the requested range itself**: `SetBlockTrackingRange` sets the smaller of the request and `min(hardpoint MaxTargetDistance, ammo MaxTrajectory)` (`ApiBackend.cs:1258-1279`). It does nothing while the platform is not `Ready` or a weapon has no active ammo, so an early call is skipped, not stored.
- **The fix** (drafted for #332, not merged as of 2026-11-13): drop `DefaultRangeWC` and pass 800 or `float.MaxValue` straight to `SetBlockTrackingRange`; collect WeaponCore blocks once per grid; read `grid.Turrets` per linked grid.
- Dynamically replaced blocks also lose any WeaponCore terminal settings saved in the original prefab blueprint.
- **Production Rule** (until #332 is fixed upstream): **do not dynamically replace primary WeaponCore weapons**. Bake the exact WeaponCore blocks into the prefab with their ranges, targeting modes and fire rates set. Put long-range vanilla turrets on the main grid, not a subgrid.

### C. Getting MES to Fire WC Fixed Weapons (Prefab Setup & Proxying)
- **[HARD] Why MES-driven fixed guns never fire: the default shoot mode ignores MES.** MES calls `ToggleWeaponFire` (`CoreWeapon.cs:443`), which WeaponCore turns into `RequestShootSync(0, On, Signals.On)` (CoreSystems `ApiBackend.cs:1151`). WeaponCore only acts on that "On" trigger when the weapon's shoot mode is not `AiShoot` (or the signal is `Manual`): `onConfirmed = Trigger == On && (ShootMode != AiShoot || Signal == Manual)` (`SessionUpdate.cs:576`). `AiShoot` (terminal: "Auto (AI Controlled)") is the default (`ProtoWeapon.cs:616`), and a fixed gun (`TrackTargets:false`, `TurretAttached:false`) cannot fire itself in it, so the command is dropped. Setting the block to **Mouse Control** makes MES-driven fixed guns fire (confirmed in game); `KeyToggle`/`KeyFire` also pass the code check but are untested. MES and the WC API cannot set the mode, so it must be saved in the prefab (protobuf in the block's `ModStorageComponent`). `scripts/wc_shootmode.py` lists and sets it. `classify` sorts each weapon into TURRET (leave on Auto), FIXED-TRACKING (on Auto it fires itself only at projectiles, and only with `Smart` ammo, §G row D; MES fires it on Mouse Control), FIXED (never fires on Auto) or FLARE (§F). `audit --mods <weapon defs>` lints prefabs: it warns on every FIXED gun left on Auto and every FLARE taken off Auto. Use `--exclude` for prefabs MES never fires, e.g. static Wrecks. If the Timer Block proxy below was built because MES's own firing never worked, this may have been the reason. Details: `aircraft_behaviors_and_tuning.md` section 3B.
- **Prefab Pre-Configuration**: Fixed forward-firing weapons must have their WeaponCore settings properly configured before saving the blueprint:
  - **The shoot mode must NOT be "Auto (AI Controlled)"** (see the first bullet below). Set it to **Mouse Control** and save the prefab/blueprint.
  - Correct weapon ID/submunition slot verified.
- **[SOFT] Wide Aiming Tolerance**: Relaxing `[WeaponMaxAngleFromTarget]` from the default narrow value to **8°–12°** significantly helps MES fire fixed guns reliably. Gyro overshoot causes constant near-miss alignment failures at tight tolerances. This applies to **both WC and vanilla fixed weapons**. Confirmed on live server (GVK): wide tolerance is one of the effective workarounds even when Mouse Control mode is correctly set. See §1E for the full `[RivalAI Weapons]` template.
- **The Alignment Flicker Trap**:
  - In `CoreWeapon.cs:443`, MES calls `APIs.WeaponCore.ToggleWeaponFire(true)` when aligned to target and immediately calls `ToggleWeaponFire(false)` if the grid alignment deviates by even a fraction of a degree (`WeaponMaxAngleFromTarget`).
  - Due to gyro overshoot and rotational damping, alignment flickers every tick. For beam weapons, burst cannons, or charge-up railguns, this causes constant stuttering and aborted firing cycles where weapons never complete a shot.
- **[LEGACY] Timer Block Proxy** (no longer needed): Before the AiShoot root cause was identified, a common workaround was triggering a Timer Block that executed WC's own "Shoot Once" terminal action — bypassing the `ToggleWeaponFire` API entirely. This worked because WC honors its own terminal actions regardless of shoot mode. With Mouse Control now the correct fix, the proxy is obsolete for new builds. Existing prefabs that use it can be left as-is.


### D. The Target Lead Prediction Disaster
- **[HARD] MES ignores WeaponCore's `AimLeadingPrediction`.** MES leads targets itself (`UseProjectileLeadPrediction` / `UseCollisionLeadPrediction` autopilot tags, `AutoPilotSystem.cs:1275-1290`); the WC weapon-definition field only affects WC's own aiming (turrets), so changing it does nothing for a fixed gun MES is flying.
- **Why MES Misses 100% of Fixed Shots**:
  - In `AutoPilotSystem.cs:1304`, MES computes target lead using `VectorHelper.TrajectoryEstimation()`, which assumes a simple linear projectile speed, constant acceleration, and zero drag.
  - WeaponCore ammos feature complex ballistic physics: drag curves, acceleration profiles, gravity multipliers, multi-stage velocities, and submunitions that MES's solver cannot model.
  - SE gyroscope rotational inertia causes the NPC ship to constantly hunt and overshoot `_calculatedWeaponPredictionWaypoint`. Against an evasive or maneuvering player ship, fixed weapons spray wildly into empty space.

### E. The NPC Weapon Handicap Architecture
To bring NPC fixed-weapon accuracy on par with player grids, use these proven modding patterns:

1. **Smart / Guided Ammunition**:
   - Equip NPC-only weapons with WeaponCore smart ammunition (`Guidance: Smart` or `Guided`, tracking cones, proximity detonation / flak burst).
   - The NPC only needs to aim within the forward hemisphere; the ammunition closes the lead gap and tracks maneuvering player grids.

2. **Low-Arc Gimbaled Mounts (Disguised as Fixed)**:
   - Configure the weapon in WeaponCore with a small gimbal arc (e.g. 5°–15° traverse/elevation).
   - Lets **WeaponCore's native 60 FPS predictive solver** aim the barrel directly at the target, completely bypassing MES's clumsy hull-turning autopilot.

3. **High-Velocity / Near-Hitscan Projectiles**:
   - Drastically boosting muzzle velocity (e.g. 2,500–4,000 m/s or energy beams) collapses time-to-target (\(t = d / v\)), making lead calculation errors negligible.

4. **NPC-Only Weapon Protection (`<Public>false</Public>`)**:
   - Set `<Public>false</Public>` in the weapon's SBC definition to prevent players from grinding and salvaging these aim-assisted/homing weapons.
   - Pair with `[MES Weapon Mod Rules]` (`[AllowIfNonPublic:true]`) so MES does not skip them during spawning:
     ```xml
     <EntityComponent xsi:type="MyObjectBuilder_InventoryComponentDefinition">
       <Id>
         <TypeId>Inventory</TypeId>
         <SubtypeId>ModPrefix-WeaponRules-NpcGuns</SubtypeId>
       </Id>
       <Description>
         [MES Weapon Mod Rules]
         [WeaponBlock:MyObjectBuilder_SmallMissileLauncher/NPC_GuidedRocketPod]
         [AllowIfNonPublic:true]
       </Description>
     </EntityComponent>
     ```

5. **`[RivalAI Weapons]` Profile Tuning**:
   - In `[RivalAI Weapons]`, relax `[WeaponMaxAngleFromTarget]` (e.g. from 2° to 8°–12°) so the NPC doesn't withhold fire forever while gyro-hunting:
     ```xml
     <EntityComponent xsi:type="MyObjectBuilder_InventoryComponentDefinition">
       <Id>
         <TypeId>Inventory</TypeId>
         <SubtypeId>ModPrefix-Weapons-NpcCombat</SubtypeId>
       </Id>
       <Description>
         [RivalAI Weapons]
         [UseStaticGuns:true]
         [UseTurrets:true]
         [WeaponMaxAngleFromTarget:10]
         [WeaponMaxBaseDistanceTarget:3000]
       </Description>
     </EntityComponent>
     ```

### F. Flares (Anti-Smart Ammo) on NPCs
Checked against MES `13bcb1d` and WeaponCore workshop `3154371364` (`Data/Scripts/CoreSystems`).

**Bug status (both open as of 2026-10-04):** the MES flare-detection bug is tracked in https://github.com/GV-Server-Mods/GVK-Settings/issues/695, and the WeaponCore `LockedSmartOnly` bug in https://github.com/GV-Server-Mods/GVK-Settings/issues/696. Before relying on either bullet below, ask the user whether it has been fixed, or open the issue yourself if the user has given you permission to.

- **[HARD] MES flare logic only fires on a missile lock.** `CoreWeapon.cs:155-172` marks flare ammo `ReadyToFire` only when the weapon system has `[UseAntiSmartWeapons:true]` (default `false`) **and** `WeaponSystem.CheckForIncomingHomingProjectiles()` gets `true` from `APIs.WeaponCore.GetProjectilesLockedOn(RemoteControl)` (`WeaponSystem.cs:428`). Every other weapon goes through the normal readiness checks (§G).
- **[HARD] MES can't detect WeaponCore 2 flare ammo.** `CoreWeapon.cs:295` sets `_flareAmmo` only from the WC1 field `ammoDef.AreaEffect.AreaEffect == AreaEffectType.AntiSmart`. WC2 ammo defines anti-smart as `Ewar { Enable = true, Type = AntiSmartv2 }`. MES never reads `Ewar` for this, and its `EwarDef.EwarType` mirror in `API/CoreSystemsApiDefs.cs` stops at `Tractor`, without `AntiSmartv2`. So a WC2 flare launcher is handled as an ordinary fixed gun: `[UseAntiSmartWeapons]` does nothing for it, and §C's shoot-mode rules apply.
- **[HARD] WeaponCore bug: `LockedSmartOnly` is inverted.** It's documented as "only fire at smart projectiles locked on to parent grid". But `AcquireProjectile` (`Ai/AiTargeting.cs:684`) **skips** a smart projectile when its target block is on the weapon's own construct (`cube = lp.Info.Target.TargetObject`, then `IsSameConstructAs(...)` → `continue`). With it on, point defense and flares ignore exactly the missiles locked on their own grid. Leave it `false` until WeaponCore fixes it.
- **[SOFT] WC-native fix: let the flare launcher pick its own missiles (confirmed in game on GVK).** Give the NPC flare block its own weapon definition. No turret subparts or Phantom are needed:
  - **AI:** fixed self-tracking, i.e. `TrackTargets = true`, `TurretAttached = false`, `TurretController = false`, azimuth/elevation parts `None`.

### G. NPC Weapon Setup Matrix (who pulls the trigger)
Code-checked against MES `13bcb1d` and WeaponCore workshop `3154371364`. Three facts decide every case: the weapon **class** (`wc_shootmode.py classify`), how MES reads the **ammo guidance**, and the **shoot mode** saved in the prefab.

| Ammo guidance | MES (`CoreWeapon.cs`) | WeaponCore on a MES "On" command (Mouse Control) |
|---|---|---|
| `None` (dumb) | Normal gun: fires when lined up within `[WeaponMaxAngleFromTarget]`, line of sight clear, in range (`:177`, `BaseWeapon.cs:292`) | Fires; no target needed (`RequiresTarget` false, `AmmoConstants.cs:450`) |
| `Smart` / `TravelTo` | **Homing:** fires once it has a target in range whose type is in the weapon's WC `Threats`. **No cone, no line-of-sight check** (`:85-150`, `:294`) | Fires only if the weapon holds a target (`RequiresTarget`), with **no aim check** (`SkipAimChecks` for Smart on fixed mounts, `AmmoConstants.cs:576`; shoot gate `SessionUpdate.cs:839-841`). Target acquisition uses the grid's AI focus first (`AiTargeting.cs:149`), and MES sets that focus to its target (`WeaponSystem.cs:620-640`) |
| `Detect*` | Normal gun | These are **mine** guidances (`IsMine`, `AmmoConstants.cs:436`), not "fly straight, then home" |
| WC1 `AreaEffect AntiSmart` / WC2 `Ewar AntiSmartv2` | Flare / not detected (§F) | See §F |

| # | Situation | Shoot mode | MES weapon profile | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | Turrets (incl. gimbals) | Auto | `[UseTurrets:true]` | `[SetWeaponsToMaxRange:true]` or ranges stay clamped to 800 m (§A) |
| B | Dumb fixed gun on an MES-flown craft | **Mouse Control** | `[UseStaticGuns:true]`, cone **8-12°** | MES does lead and aim (§C/§D). A 180° cone means "fire whenever in range" |
| C | Fixed gun with `Smart` ammo (real homing, or a two-stage aim-assist round) on an MES-flown craft | **Mouse Control** | `[UseStaticGuns:true]`; cap range with `[MaxStaticWeaponRange]` | Neither MES nor WeaponCore checks the angle, so it fires off-angle whenever both have a target. The WC `Threats` list filters what MES fires at: a `Grids`-only list never fires at players on foot. Aim-assist pattern: a `Smart` base round with `SteeringLimit = 0` (no steering), plus a timed fragment (`PointAtTarget`, `PointType = Direct`, `DirectAimCone`, `ParentDies = true`). The fragment spawns aimed at the target with lead prediction, but only if the target is inside the cone (`Projectile.cs:3390-3440`); otherwise the base round flies on straight. Mouse Control: MES decides, per the ammo table |

- **[HARD] Give every NPC copy of a weapon its own `PartName`.** MES finds a block's WeaponCore definition by `HardPoint.PartName` and takes the **first** match across all loaded definitions, for ammo restock (`InventoryHelper.cs:407-412`) and weapon setup (`WeaponSystem.cs:191-196`). If an `_NPC` definition shares its name with the player one, MES restocks the player's ammo list and reads the player's settings. On GVK this filled NPC flare launchers mostly with firework magazines they can't fire, so they ran dry after one load.
- **[HARD] `wc_shootmode.py` known gaps.** It only reads definitions written as `WeaponDefinition Name => new WeaponDefinition { ... }`. A definition built by a helper (`WeaponDefinition X_NPC => MakeNpc(X, "Sub_NPC")`) reports "no WeaponCore definition found" and `audit` skips its blocks; one that copies another and swaps its ammo is classified with the original's ammo. Check those blocks by hand.

### H. Turret Relations (Vanilla and WeaponCore) vs MES Targeting
- **[HARD] Two NPC factions: the faction-to-faction relation decides turret fire.** Vanilla `MyIDModule.GetRelationPlayerPlayer` returns `GetRelationBetweenFactions` when both owners are in NPC factions; WeaponCore uses the same call (`Ai/AiDatabase.cs:105`, `:399`: `MyIDModule.GetRelationPlayerBlock`).
- **[HARD] A faction pair with no relation set counts as Enemies** (`GetRelationPlayerBlock` passes `defaultFactionRelations = Enemies`). Set every pair you want Neutral or Friendly at world build.
- **[HARD] An NPC faction and a player: the player's own relation with the NPC faction decides** (`GetRelationBetweenPlayerAndFactionRelationOnly`). That's the value faction-alignment scripts and reputation actions set.
- **[HARD] WeaponCore's Neutrals override is checked against the faction-to-faction relation** (`Ai/AiTargeting.cs:654`) and only matters for Neutral pairs. A weapon with it on also fires on every grid of a faction that is Neutral to its owner, including structures meant to be left alone. It's stored per block in the prefab: field 1 (`Neutrals`) of the same `ProtoWeaponOverrides` message as the shoot mode (§C); `scripts/wc_shootmode.py neutrals` lists and sets it.
- **MES and turrets follow the same data from master after 2.75.02** (`67320b7`, PR #461; `49b3380`, PR #463 for fixed-gun line of fire): both read the faction-to-faction relation for two NPC factions (`behaviors_and_autopilot.md` target profiles), so turrets, MES targeting and dumb-ammo fixed guns all agree. **Up to 2.75.02 they differed**, because MES used the target owner's own reputation. **[SOFT] Seen in game then:** turrets on faction A's grids fired on faction B with Neutrals off while MES rated B Neutral to A (A–B faction relation Enemies); turrets on faction B held fire on faction C grids that B's MES profile rated Enemy (B–C faction relation Friends). On those builds, set both the faction-to-faction relations (turrets) and the factions' `StartingReputation` or name-based target profiles (MES) so the two agree.

## 2. Defense Shields Integration

MES interfaces with DarkStar's Defense Shields API:

- **Shield Modulation**: NPC grids can automatically modulate shield frequency to resist incoming kinetic or energy damage based on combat triggers.
- **Overheat & Downed Shield Triggers**:
  - Use `[Type:Damage]` triggers to monitor shield collapse and execute defensive actions (e.g. popping decoy pods, activating jump drives, or triggering smoke screens).
- **Shield Bypass & Hardening**:
  - Specific action profiles can force shield generators to overcharge or enter emergency lockdown when boarding threats are detected.

## 3. AiEnabled Integration (Hostile Bot Crews)

The AiEnabled mod adds walking bots that path through grids and over terrain. MES spawns them from `[MES Bot Spawn]` profiles; profile tags, spawn paths and despawn rules: [`bots_and_crews.md`](bots_and_crews.md) §8.

- **Profile**: `[MES Bot Spawn]` with `[UseAiEnabled:true]` (the default up to 2.75.03; `false` on MES `master` after it)
- **[HARD] The role** (MES `BotSpawnProfile.cs`, AiEnabled `Bots/BotFactory.cs`, Workshop copy of 2026-05-22): MES sends the profile's `[BotBehavior:]` as the AiEnabled role (`[CreatureIds:]` spawn groups send the conditions tag `[AiEnabledRole:]` instead). AiEnabled's roles:

  | Side | Roles |
  | :--- | :--- |
  | Enemy | `ZOMBIE`, `SOLDIER`, `BRUISER`, `GRINDER`, `GHOST`, `CREATURE` |
  | Neutral (joins the `NOMAD` faction) | `NOMAD`, `ENFORCER`, `PATRON` |
  | Friendly (player-owned helpers only) | `REPAIR`, `SCAVENGER`, `COMBAT`, `CREW` |

  - A bot owned by an NPC takes an enemy or neutral role. The name is matched without case, but it must be one of the names above exactly and appear in the AiEnabled config's `AllowedBotRoles`; any other name makes AiEnabled refuse the bot and log `Something attempted to spawn a <role> helper which is not in AllowedBotRoles.`
  - **MES's default `[BotBehavior:Default]` is not a role, so the bot is refused.** Always set it, e.g. `[BotBehavior:Soldier]`. Read in code, not tested in game.
  - A blank role (the `[AiEnabledRole:]` default) picks one from the bot subtype: `Space_Skeleton` Grinder, `Space_Zombie` Zombie, `Boss_Bot` Bruiser, `Ghost_Bot` Ghost, anything else Soldier.

## 4. Water Mod & Hydrodynamic AI

When operating on worlds running the Water Mod:

- **Behavior Subclass**: Set `[BehaviorName:Nautical]` in `[RivalAI Behavior]`.
- **Autopilot Profile**: Use `[RivalAI Autopilot]` configured with nautical buoyancy locks.
- **Spawn Conditions**: Use `[MES Spawn Conditions]` with `[MustSpawnUnderwater:true]` (or `[CanSpawnUnderwater:true]`), `[MinWaterCoverage:]`/`[MaxWaterCoverage:]`, and for installations `[InstallationSpawnsOnWaterSurface:true]`/`[InstallationSpawnsUnderwater:true]` with `[MinWaterDepth:]`/`[MaxWaterDepth:]` (`MaxWaterDepth` defaults to `-1` = no maximum since MES 2.74.05; on 2.74.03-2.74.04 it defaulted to `0` and had to be set; see `spawning_and_conditions.md` §3.B).
- **Anti-Sinking Logic**: Ensure buoyancy tanks or flotation blocks are prioritized in defense triggers.

## 6. Torch Plugins & Server Compatibility

On dedicated servers running Torch or Magnetar/Pulsar plugins:

- **Grid Defender**: Suppresses low-speed collision damage while preserving high-speed missile damage. Ensure NPC collision evasion waypoints don't trigger false positives.
- **Voxel Clang Mitigation**: Falling or disabled aircraft must be despawned cleanly (`[ForceDespawn:true]`) rather than allowed to crash and penetrate terrain meshes, which traps rigid bodies in continuous Havok collision solver loops and craters sim-speed to 0.2.
